title: Transmigrated as a Vicious Supporting Female Lead? The Male Lead Insists on Marrying Me!
author: Qi Bu Long Dong
synopsis: The moment Cui Mingyu opened her eyes, she found she had transmigrated into a novel as a vicious supporting female lead who was obsessed with love and constantly stirring up trouble. Seeing that she was on the verge of being loathed and purged by the male lead, she decisively pulled back from the brink and turned to look for a better match. But who would have thought that the male lead, who had previously looked at her with disdain, would start looking at her with an increasingly strange expression... Has he lost his mind?

chapters.title: Transmigrating into a Book
chapters.content:
Cui Mingyu was awakened by a wave of scorching heat.

Her consciousness felt wrapped in thick cotton; in her confusion, she felt that the texture beneath her was wrong—it wasn't the old, washed-out cotton bedding from her dormitory, but soft satin that felt cool to the touch yet radiated body heat. She struggled to lift her heavy eyelids, and the moment her vision focused, her breath hitched.

A man was lying beneath her.

He wasn't the guy from the convenience store downstairs who always gave her an extra candy, nor was he a fitness influencer she’d scrolled past on TikTok. He had a face that would make historical drama directors fight to cast him. His sword-like eyebrows slanted toward his temples, though a fierce, "stay away" aura was knotted at the peak of his brows. His eyes, slightly upturned at the corners, were currently veiled in a layer of mist, which instead added a touch of allure not usually seen. Beneath a high, straight nose, his thin lips were pressed into a straight line. His jawline was taut, and the veins in his neck were faintly visible. Most intoxicating of all were his cheeks, which were flushed with an unnatural crimson, as if he had been intoxicated by strong liquor, or perhaps... as if he were enduring something.

Cui Mingyu was stunned.

She had clearly been in her dorm last night, grinding away at her thesis until 3:00 AM, and finally, unable to hold on any longer, she had fallen asleep at her desk. How, upon opening her eyes, had she changed locations and been gifted a top-tier handsome man?

Could it be that the stress of her thesis was so great that her brain had automatically generated a beautiful dream?

This thought had barely surfaced before she extinguished it herself—no one could dream so clearly that they could see the beads of moisture on someone's eyelashes, nor could they smell the faint scent of ambergris on him, mixed with a subtle, lingering trace of sweat—overbearing and seductive.

Cui Mingyu swallowed hard. If it wasn't a dream, how could she be seeing such a handsome man?

Her gaze moved downward instinctively, landing on the man's chest. He wore a snow-white inner garment, the fabric as thin as cicada wings, now semi-transparent from sweat and clinging tightly to his body, outlining the contours beneath with perfect clarity. The muscles of his chest were firm and full, leading down to the faintly visible grooves of his abs. Every inch exuded a sense of power, making Cui Mingyu's heart skip a beat.

"Ugh..." The man suddenly let out a low groan, his chest heaving violently. The thin fabric seemed as if it might be torn apart by the muscles beneath, making one's heart tighten.

Cui Mingyu reached out as if possessed. The moment her fingertips touched the fabric, she recoiled, startled by the scorching temperature. But then she thought, it's a dream anyway, what is there to fear? She grabbed the fabric with both hands and gave it a gentle tug along the lapel—

With a soft "rip," the collar of the inner garment was pulled open, revealing a large expanse of honey-colored skin. The firm chest muscles slammed into her view, clearly defined, with even the groove in the center looking incredibly sexy. Cui Mingyu couldn't help but poke it with her fingertip; it was soft yet firm, with surprising elasticity—even more "bouncy" than she had imagined.

"Perfect!" she exclaimed sincerely. This physique was even more stunning than the male leads in the short dramas she usually watched!

"You... get away from me!"

A cold, harsh voice suddenly exploded, filled with gnashing, teeth-gritting rage. Cui Mingyu was startled, and as she looked up, she met the man's bloodshot eyes. He struggled to sit up, his arms bracing against the bed, his muscle lines tensing even further. But the moment he lifted himself slightly, he collapsed back down heavily, more cold sweat seeping from his forehead.

Looking at him like this, it seemed as if he had been drugged?

Cui Mingyu muttered to herself, but didn't take it seriously. Mimicking scenes from TV dramas, she made a "shh" gesture at him. Her gaze fell back to the man's lips—they were already naturally red, but now, dampened by sweat, they looked even more vivid and tempting, like a ripe cherry, holding a fatal allure.

As if under a spell, Cui Mingyu leaned down and lightly touched that softness.

The sensation was warm and moist, with a slightly scorching heat, more enticing than any dessert she had ever tasted.

But the next second, a sharp pain shot from her lips—

"Sss!" Cui Mingyu recoiled violently, covering her mouth. Looking at the undisguised disgust and ruthlessness in the man's eyes, she felt incredibly aggrieved. "Why are you biting people?"

Wait.

Pain?

She froze for a moment and instinctively pinched her own cheek. A clear, sharp pain came from her fingertips—not the blurred sensation of a dream, but something so real it made her gasp.

This wasn't a dream?

Cui Mingyu panicked instantly. She scrambled off the bed, stumbled back two steps, and scanned her surroundings rapidly.

The antique canopy bed, the carved wooden windows, the ink-wash landscape painting on the wall, and the delicate pink *ruqun* (skirt) she was wearing... everything told her that this was not her dorm, nor was it the real world.

She had transmigrated?

This thought struck like a thunderbolt, making Cui Mingyu's brain buzz. She turned her head stiffly to look at the man on the bed—she had just been touching him all over and even kissed him. Now that she knew it was real, her cheeks burned bright red, and even her earlobes felt scorching hot.

It's over, it's over, I've caused a huge disaster!

Cui Mingyu paced around in a panic, but finally, she bit the bullet and walked back. She picked up the inner garment she had pulled open, carefully helped the man put it back on, and then pulled the silk quilt from the side to gently cover him.

"Um..." she stammered, her voice as small as a mosquito's. "I didn't mean to. I just... walked into the wrong room! You are a magnanimous person, please don't hold it against me."

The man's face remained flushed, his breathing had not yet steadied, and even his voice trembled uncontrollably, yet his words still carried the authority of someone in a position of power: "Cui Mingyu, don't think that just because you stopped halfway, this Prince will spare you. Bring me the antidote!"

Antidote?

Cui Mingyu was stunned. She didn't even know how she got here, let alone where to find an antidote! Furthermore, she had no idea who had drugged this man!

Just then, a vague memory suddenly flashed into her mind—last night before bed, her roommate had been crying over an ancient romance novel, complaining to her that the vicious supporting female lead in the book had the same name as her and met a miserable end. She had thought her roommate was being childish at the time and asked a few questions. She remembered her roommate saying the female lead was named Cui Mingyu, a spoiled and willful daughter of the Minister of Rites. To win the male lead, she drugged him, but the male lead would rather exhaust his internal energy than let her succeed. In the end, the male lead had the female lead's limbs removed and her body discarded in the street...

Thinking of this, Cui Mingyu shivered, a chill running from the soles of her feet to the top of her head.

She looked up stiffly at the man on the bed, her voice trembling: "You... are you the Prince of Jingnan?"

A flash of astonishment crossed the man's eyes, as if he hadn't expected her to ask that, but it was immediately replaced by rage: "Cui Mingyu, what kind of trick are you playing? Do you dare say you don't recognize this Prince?"

It's over.

Cui Mingyu's vision went dark; she almost fainted. She really had transmigrated into a book, and she had become that miserable, vicious supporting female lead! The key was that she hadn't even read the book; she had just discussed it briefly with her roommate because of her big mouth. How could she be so unlucky to have transmigrated directly into it?

Just then, a chaotic sound of footsteps suddenly came from outside, getting closer and closer. It looked like they were about to reach the door.

Cui Mingyu's heart jumped into her throat—she remembered her roommate saying that after the female lead drugged the male lead, she had deliberately arranged for people to "catch them in the act" to solidify their relationship. But the male lead had exhausted his internal energy to resist, which only made him hate her even more.

Wasn't this the classic "caught in bed" trope?

The Prince of Jingnan, Wei Songjun, on the bed clearly heard the commotion outside as well. His eyes turned icy, and he stared fixedly at Cui Mingyu, as if he wanted to tear her apart.

"It wasn't me!" Cui Mingyu waved her hands quickly, nearly crying. "I really didn't arrange this! Please, don't use your internal energy. Leave it to me, I'll handle it!"

She didn't know if she could change the plot, but she knew that she absolutely could not let Wei Songjun get angry, and even less could she let him exhaust his internal energy. In the original book, it was because he exhausted his internal energy and damaged his foundation that he grew to hate the original owner so deeply.

Wei Songjun clearly didn't believe her; the suspicion in his eyes deepened.

Cui Mingyu had no time to explain. She took a deep breath and looked around. No matter what, she had to stop the people outside first!

chapters.title: Viewing the Lotus
chapters.content:
Cui Mingyu thought that if she went out through the main door now, it would be no different from walking into a trap.

Her gaze fell unexpectedly on the carved window on the side. The window was half-open. Without a moment's hesitation, she braced her hands against the sill, twisted her slender waist with agility, and prepared to vault out. But in her panic, she forgot to calculate the height of the window frame, and her forehead slammed into the hard wood with a "thud." A dull pain spread instantly, making her gasp.

Before she could even rub her aching forehead, a sudden wave of dizziness hit her, as if countless fragmented images were exploding in her mind. Strange memory fragments surged. These images came too fast and too urgently; Cui Mingyu felt her temples throbbing. She didn't have time to think, quickly smoothed her wind-blown skirt, lifted the hem embroidered with begonia flowers, and hurried toward the main door.

Wei Songjun's ink-black eyes were filled with coldness as he watched the figure hurrying away outside the window. Waves of heat surged from his lower abdomen, as if a raging fire were burning within his body, causing an unbearable dryness to spread through his limbs. The sensation of his parched throat made his Adam's apple bob.

With his level of internal energy, ordinary aphrodisiacs could not affect him, which showed that the dosage this time was far beyond his expectations. A trace of ruthlessness flashed in Wei Songjun's eyes. He pressed his thin lips together, his teeth chattering, with only one thought in his heart: Cui Mingyu, you are dead!

Cui Mingyu had no idea of the monstrous rage of the person inside the room. She walked quickly to the main door, just in time to run into a group of people—at the head was the Old Matriarch of the Ning State Duke's mansion, with white hair and a youthful face, wearing a treasure-blue *beizi* (jacket) embroidered with longevity patterns. She was surrounded by several noblewomen and young ladies, and... her nominal father, Cui Yong, the Minister of Rites.

Cui Mingyu recognized these people at a glance, thanks to that recent collision which had jarred the original owner’s memories loose.

The crowd clearly hadn't expected to run into her here either. They all stopped in their tracks, their gazes fixed squarely upon her. Cui Mingyu’s chest was still heaving from her hurried run. She managed to steady her breathing, forcing an awkward yet polite smile onto her face, her voice still carrying the remnants of her exertion: "Hey... greetings, elders and sisters."

A young maid with a round face was the first to react. She widened her round eyes, pointed at the door behind Cui Mingyu, and asked with a tone full of surprise, "Miss! Why are you here? Weren't you..."

"Wasn't I what?" Cui Mingyu quickly interrupted her. This girl was the original owner’s maid, Chun Tao. The moment Chun Tao spoke, fragments of memory surged in her mind again, only this time they were much clearer. Today was the seventieth birthday of the Old Matriarch of the Ning State Duke’s mansion. Her father—or rather, the original owner’s father, Minister of Revenue Cui Yong—had brought her along to offer birthday wishes. Wei Songjun, being on good terms with the heir of the Ning State Duke’s mansion, had also come, and so the original owner had taken the opportunity to drug the male lead.

Cui Yong glared. "Nonsense! Why did you have Chun Tao call all these people over?"

Heaven help her, she wasn't the one who called them! Cui Mingyu looked into the distance, catching sight of the lotus flowers in full bloom in the nearby pond. As if grabbing a life-saving straw, she had a sudden inspiration. "That... Father—"

Cui Yong was already displeased that his daughter had suddenly had Chun Tao summon everyone. Now, hearing her informal address, he frowned and glared. "Nonsense! What is this 'Father' this and 'Father' that?"

Cui Mingyu groaned inwardly—she had only just received these memories and truly couldn't adapt immediately to this "suddenly popped up" father. However, she dared not show it on her face and could only smile sheepishly, pointing at the lotus pond. "Father, I... I saw that the lotus flowers in the backyard were in full bloom and thought that such a beautiful scene should be enjoyed by everyone together, which is why I asked Chun Tao to invite everyone."

No sooner had she finished speaking than a sarcastic female voice rang out: "Well, that is truly strange." The speaker was Xie Yishu, the second young lady of the Ning State Duke’s mansion. She was dressed in a pink silk gown and was quite beautiful, but her brows were slightly furrowed, and her eyes were filled with disdain as she looked at Cui Mingyu. "Since when does the lotus in our Ning State Duke’s mansion require Miss Cui to summon everyone to view it?"

Cui Mingyu’s mind immediately conjured up the past between the original owner and Xie Yishu—the two had been at odds since childhood, clashing every time they met, neither willing to yield. The original owner, being competitive, had often suffered at Xie Yishu’s hands. But Cui Mingyu was not the original owner. She was a newcomer and didn't want to make enemies just as she had found her footing, especially since Xie Yishu was quite charming and pleasant to look at.

She quickly wiped the awkwardness from her face, smiled gently at Xie Yishu, and said with sincerity, "Yes, yes, I overstepped. Seeing such beautiful lotus flowers just now, I was struck by a sudden whim and didn't think it through. I just wanted to share the scenery with everyone and forgot that this is the Ning State Duke’s mansion. Please forgive me, Second Miss."

As soon as these words were out, not only was Xie Yishu stunned, but the surrounding ladies and misses also showed expressions of surprise. Who didn't know that Cui Mingyu had always been arrogant and never spared anyone with her words? To think she would admit her mistake so gently today! Xie Yishu stared at her suspiciously, as if trying to find traces of pretense on her face, and asked with uncertainty, "Cui Mingyu, what kind of trick are you playing now?"

"Yishu!" Lady Xie quickly took her daughter’s hand, offered a kind smile to Cui Mingyu, and smoothed things over. "You child, how are you talking to Miss Cui? Miss Cui had good intentions, wanting to invite everyone to see the lotus flowers. What is wrong with that?"

Cui Yong also quickly chimed in, though he couldn't help but steal a glare at Cui Mingyu from the corner of his eye, his tone tinged with helplessness. "My daughter has a straightforward temperament and can't keep things to herself. She must have been dazzled by these lotus flowers and lost her sense of propriety for a moment. She only wanted to share this beautiful scenery with everyone. I hope the Old Matriarch and all the ladies will not take offense."

The Old Matriarch, who had been silent all this time, finally spoke. She gently turned the prayer beads in her hand, her gaze resting on the lotus pond not far away, and a kind smile appeared at the corners of her mouth. "It is no matter. The lotus flowers in my home have indeed bloomed brilliantly this year, several days earlier than in previous years. It can be considered a joyous occasion."

Cui Mingyu’s eyes lit up. She immediately followed the Old Matriarch’s lead, her face breaking into a sincere smile, her tone playful. "I knew it! The lotus flowers elsewhere are still just buds, but only the ones in your mansion have bloomed so beautifully. So it turns out these lotus flowers were rushing to offer birthday wishes to you, Old Matriarch! Knowing today is your seventieth birthday, they bloomed in a rush, wanting to bask in your good fortune!"

These words were both pleasing and apt. The Old Matriarch’s smile deepened as she looked at Cui Yong, her tone full of praise. "Minister Cui, your daughter has a very sweet tongue; it is truly comforting to hear her speak."

Xie Yishu, standing to the side, glared fiercely at Cui Mingyu, completely baffled—the Cui Mingyu of today seemed like a different person. Not only did she not snap back at her, but she could also say such things to please the Old Matriarch. It was truly strange.

Cui Yong also looked at his daughter suspiciously. His wife had passed away early, leaving him with only this precious daughter whom he pampered dearly. She was inevitably spoiled and often acted on impulse, but today she was able to speak so appropriately and charmingly. Could it be that she had truly turned over a new leaf? He suppressed his doubts and said to the Old Matriarch with a smile, "You are too kind, Old Matriarch. Since the lotus flowers have bloomed so well, we shall take advantage of this scenery today to enjoy them with you."

The Old Matriarch nodded with a smile and led the way toward the lotus pond. The ladies and misses followed one after another. The previously tense atmosphere completely eased, and the group headed toward the lotus pond in a grand procession, their footsteps and laughter gradually fading into the distance.

Cui Mingyu lingered at the back of the crowd. Watching the figures ahead, she quietly breathed a sigh of relief and raised a hand to rub her still-aching temple. The stinging pain reminded her of the memories in her mind and the man in the room who wanted to tear her limb from limb. She sighed inwardly; it seemed the mess left behind by this body would have to be cleaned up bit by bit.

chapters.title: Detoxification
chapters.content:
The voices outside the room gradually faded with the footsteps of the crowd, finally disappearing into the deep silence of the courtyard. Wei Songjun lay on the carved canopy bed, beads of sweat still clinging to his eyelashes. Every breath he took was scorching with agony—the aphrodisiac Cui Mingyu had tricked him into drinking was now raging through his meridians like a wildfire. Only his lower abdomen remained rigid as iron, throbbing with a pain so intense it threatened to shatter his sanity.

He tried to move a finger, but his whole body was as weak as if his bones and tendons had been removed. The evil fire only burned brighter; the sweat on his temples, just dried by the night breeze, beaded up again in an instant, soaking his moon-white silk undergarment. If this continued, the fire would surely attack his heart, and his life would be in danger.

Wei Songjun gritted his teeth, blood seeping from his tongue, and forced himself to lean his back against the bedpost. He closed his eyes tight, intending to channel the internal energy in his dantian to force the drug out of his body—but he knew better than anyone that this was like drinking poison to quench thirst. Not only would it deplete ten years of hard-earned internal energy, but any slight mistake could cause his meridians to reverse, leaving him permanently disabled.

"Cui Mingyu, that wicked creature!" he cursed inwardly. If not for that girl’s reckless behavior, how could he have ended up in such a pathetic state?

Just as his internal energy was about to sink into his dantian, a soft "creak" sounded from outside the door, breaking the silence of the room.

"Quick, quick! Move lightly, don't let anyone hear!" A crisp female voice lowered its volume, filled with urgency.

"Miss, what are you doing this for?" Another voice, sounding like a maid, asked in confusion. "You went to such great lengths to feed the Prince the medicine, and you were about to succeed. You could have just forced yourself on him, and from then on, you would have been the Prince’s woman. Why go through all this trouble!"

"What do you know!" the female voice scolded. Footsteps hurried closer. "Hurry and move the ice to the bathing room, be quick about it!"

Wei Songjun’s heart tightened. Just as he was about to withdraw his energy, the curtain was suddenly flung open, and a figure in begonia-colored clothing burst in. Cui Mingyu was holding up her skirt, sweat still beading on her forehead—after the group finished viewing the lotus flowers, they had all gone to the stage to watch the play, and she had taken advantage of that window to come and clean up the mess the original owner had made.

But when she saw Wei Songjun closing his eyes to regulate his breathing, his body surrounded by a faint white mist, her expression changed drastically. She rushed forward in a few steps and grabbed his wrist. "Didn't I tell you not to use your internal energy?"

Her hand was icy cold, as if she had just fished it out of the lotus pond, and it landed unexpectedly on the back of Wei Songjun’s scorching hand. The sudden chill darted through his meridians, but instead of suppressing the evil fire, it acted like a fuse, causing the drug’s power to surge even more violently.

His breathing regulation was forcibly interrupted, and Wei Songjun’s focus shattered, a suppressed groan escaping his throat. He opened his eyes abruptly, his dark pupils swirling with lust and restraint, his bloodshot eyes locked onto Cui Mingyu. The soft, fragrant beauty was within reach; the scent of gardenias from her hair mixed with the lotus fragrance, making his heart tremble, and he almost lost control and pinned her beneath him.

"You—what are you doing!" he gritted out, each word enunciated, his voice as hoarse as sandpaper rubbing together.

Cui Mingyu was startled by the fierce light in his eyes, but she forced herself to remain calm, let go of his hand, and stepped back half a pace. The original owner’s memories surged in her mind; she clearly remembered that this drug was given by Princess Chao Gui—the Emperor’s half-sister, who had been widowed at twenty and kept many male favorites in her mansion. She was a figure that noble ladies in the capital avoided, but the original owner shared her tastes, and they were bold enough to do anything crazy together.

Chaogui had laughed mischievously at the time, saying that this drug didn't need an antidote; it would naturally be resolved through intimacy, and going to the trouble of making an antidote was completely unnecessary.

"There is no antidote for this drug." Cui Mingyu met his gaze, speaking bluntly, without a hint of maidenly shyness. "There are two ways now. First, do you have a lover? I can go find her for you, and once you spend a night together, this will be resolved."

In the original book, Wei Songjun’s official match was Mu Wanzhou, but at this moment, the two shouldn't have reached the point of being lovey-dovey, so they couldn't yet be called "lovers."

Wei Songjun’s expression darkened instantly, the disgust in his eyes deepening. This woman was truly shameless to be able to say such explicit words so casually. Although he had been to brothels and seen the fawning of courtesans, he had never met anyone like Cui Mingyu, who spoke of intimacy as casually as eating or drinking.

"And the second way?" he said coldly, his impatience nearly overflowing.

"I had Bitao move ice blocks into the bathhouse and pour in ice water." Cui Mingyu blinked, her limpid almond eyes staring straight at him, oblivious to how shocking her words were. "If you soak in there for two hours, once you regain your strength, you can just use 'Miss Five' to take care of it yourself. Anyway... as long as you release the heat, the drug's effects should wear off, right?"

At the mention of "Miss Five," Wei Songjun was stunned. Once he realized what she meant, his earlobes turned a rare, faint red, quickly replaced by shame and anger. He clenched his fists so hard that the rage in his chest almost eclipsed the drug's potency. "You... do you even know the meaning of shame?"

What was shame compared to one's life? Cui Mingyu frowned. The urgent task was to help him neutralize the drug—if this man were ruined, her own life would likely be compromised as well. She took another step forward, her limpid eyes fixed on him. "Your Highness, don't dawdle. Just pick one."

Wei Songjun already detested her reckless behavior, but looking into those limpid almond eyes, he felt an inexplicable, soul-stirring magic, and a sudden, intense possessiveness rose from the depths of his heart. He shook his head violently, telling himself it must be the drug playing tricks, causing him to have such illusions about this shameless girl.

Seeing him remain silent, Cui Mingyu simply took it as him choosing the second option. "Fine, the second one it is! Can you still walk? I'll help you."

As she spoke, she pressed against him, draping his arm over her shoulder. The moment she exerted force, she couldn't help but curse inwardly: *Why is this man so deathly heavy!*

Supported and half-carried by her, Wei Songjun’s body was almost pressed against hers. The scent of fresh gardenias on her grew more intense, drilling into his nostrils and winding around his heart, causing the drug-fueled fire already churning within him to boil over. His heart hammered like a drum; all he could hear were his own heavy breaths and her shallow gasps. His eyes grew increasingly bloodshot, the strings of his reason on the verge of snapping.

Cui Mingyu was sweating from the effort. Unable to hold him up any longer, she shouted toward the bathhouse, "Bitao! Come help!"

Bitao ran in at the call. Seeing her mistress nearly bent double under the weight, she hurried over to support Wei Songjun’s other arm. The two of them, one on each side, used every ounce of their strength to finally move the limp yet burning-hot Wei Songjun into the bathhouse.

The wooden tub was already filled with ice water, with several unmelted ice blocks floating on top. The moment Wei Songjun was helped into it, the icy sensation spread through his limbs, finally easing the burning agony. He let out a long sigh, nearly collapsing against the side of the tub.

But the next second, a faint, fishy stench wafted up from the water, mixed with the chill of the ice. It made him knit his brows in disgust; his stomach churned, and he nearly vomited.

Standing by the tub, Cui Mingyu saw his expression soften slightly and breathed a sigh of relief. "You soak for now. I'll keep watch outside. If you need anything, call me." With that, she grabbed Bitao and fled as if escaping.

chapters.title: The Bathhouse
chapters.content:
"Cui Mingyu!"

The cold, sharp voice, laced with impatience, sounded like a winter wind blowing through the copper bells under the eaves.

Cui Mingyu, who had just stepped out of the bathhouse, froze in her tracks, her spine stiffening imperceptibly. She turned around slowly, forcing herself to put on a meek and respectful expression, and curtsied. "Your Highness, what are your orders?"

Wei Songjun’s brows were knit into a deep furrow, his tone filled with loathing. "What kind of water did you prepare for me? It reeks of fish—how dare you present this to me?"

Cui Mingyu’s heart sank. She lowered her lashes to hide her anxiety, her smile becoming stiff, her voice turning unnaturally dry. "Your Highness, please forgive me. This is, after all, a side courtyard of the Duke of Ning’s estate. There are many prying eyes among the servants, so I couldn't fetch ice openly and had to sneak some from the kitchen. Perhaps it picked up the kitchen’s fumes, causing the odor. Could you... could you please make do for now?" In truth, she and Chuntao had taken the ice from a crate filled with fresh fish; the ice had clearly absorbed the fishy smell. If Wei Songjun found out the ice came from a fish crate, he might send her to meet the Buddha immediately.

"Make do?" Wei Songjun sounded as if he had heard the greatest joke in the world. He was already hot and agitated from the drug, and this fishy smell made him even more miserable. "Cui Mingyu, are you intentionally toying with me? Go, fetch Xie Changchuan for me!"

Xie Changchuan was the heir to the Duke of Ning’s estate, and the two were close. Cui Mingyu panicked, stepping forward, her voice rising slightly. "Your Highness, absolutely not! Young Master Xie is known for his wide circle of friends and his love for jokes. If he finds out about today’s events and lets it slip, wouldn't it ruin your reputation?"

Wei Songjun was proud and arrogant, valuing his face above all else. Being drugged and trapped here by the original owner was already a great humiliation; if that witty rascal Xie Changchuan found out, he would be teased for the rest of his life.

Sure enough, this hit Wei Songjun’s sore spot. His chest heaved violently, a muffled groan escaping his throat. He let out a bitter, frustrated breath, the rage in his eyes finally suppressed by his concern for his reputation. He glared viciously at Cui Mingyu, grinding out each word: "Get out!"

"Yes, yes, yes!" Cui Mingyu felt as if she had been granted amnesty. She responded hurriedly and turned to run toward the door.

But just as she gripped the cold door bolt, Wei Songjun’s cold, indisputable command came from behind, icy as winter icicles: "Wait in the room. Do not go far."

Cui Mingyu’s movements stiffened. She groaned inwardly but dared not disobey. She could only respond with a dejected "Yes" and retreated behind the sandalwood screen outside the bathhouse to keep watch, staring blankly at Chuntao as the atmosphere grew stagnant.

Leaning against the cold screen, Cui Mingyu calculated in her heart, hoping only that Wei Songjun would successfully neutralize the drug. As long as he was safe and sound, she would be more cautious in the future and stay far away from this god of plague, which should be enough to save her life.

*Sigh*, if only she had transmigrated into the book a few days earlier. If she had arrived before the original owner had lost her mind and drugged Wei Songjun, she wouldn't be in this impossible predicament. The original owner was arrogant and overbearing, obsessed with marrying Wei Songjun, using clumsy and flashy methods, only to end up having her limbs severed by him and dying in the wilderness. Just thinking about it made her blood run cold.

"Miss," Chuntao said, seeing her gloomy expression, unable to help but ask, her tone full of confusion, "What is all this for? First you drug the Prince, and now you’re waiting on him hand and foot. Isn't this exhausting?"

Cui Mingyu looked at the maid, a cold glint flashing in her eyes. Chuntao was the original owner’s dowry maid; her loyalty was real, but her intelligence was truly lacking. In the past, the original owner’s endless antics had been egged on by this girl.

Thinking of the original owner’s tragic end, Cui Mingyu felt a chill, her tone sinking involuntarily, carrying a hint of intimidation. "Don't ask so many questions. Bury today’s events in your stomach; don't let out a single word. Otherwise, I... I will cut out your tongue."

Chuntao was startled by her stern tone and quickly covered her mouth. Her eyes turned red instantly, tears welling up as she shook her head, weeping. "Miss, I wouldn't dare! Please don't scare me, don't cut out my tongue, I will never tell anyone!"

"Enough, enough, stop it." Cui Mingyu was annoyed by her crying and waved her hand. "Let me have some peace. Go to the courtyard gate and keep watch. If anyone comes, warn me in advance. Be sharp, don't mess this up."

"Yes! I'm going right now!" Chuntao wiped her tears messily and scurried to the courtyard gate, peeking through the door frame like a frightened little squirrel.

The area behind the screen fell silent. Cui Mingyu listened for sounds from the bathhouse. After a long while, hearing nothing, she began to panic. After hesitating for a moment, she gathered her courage and peeked through the carved gaps in the screen into the bathhouse.

Wei Songjun was still soaking in the tub with his eyes closed. The strange flush on his face had faded somewhat, but his lips, which were usually a vibrant red, were now a frightening, bruised purple.

Cui Mingyu subconsciously touched her own lips, her heart skipping a beat. Just now, thinking it was a dream, she had impulsively leaned in and kissed him—*I'm dead, I'm dead!*

Cui Mingyu was filled with shame and annoyance. Looking at his bruised lips, a bold thought suddenly emerged: *If Wei Songjun just... died? If the male lead of this book died, could she completely escape his clutches?*

As soon as the thought surfaced, she suppressed it violently. *No, no, how could the male lead die so easily? If he dies, will the world of this book collapse? Where would she go then? Would she return to her own reality, or would she vanish along with it?*

The more she thought, the more chaotic she became. Cui Mingyu scratched her head in frustration. She didn't know how much time had passed, but just as she was about to lean in closer to check on Wei Songjun, she heard Chuntao’s panicked footsteps at the courtyard gate, accompanied by a hushed cry: "Miss! It's bad!"

Cui Mingyu’s heart tightened, and she hurried to meet her. "What is it? Why are you panicking?"

"Young Master Xie and the Second Miss Xie are here!" Chuntao was drenched in sweat, her voice trembling. "I just saw them followed by the Duke’s servants, and they’re heading this way!"

Cui Mingyu’s face turned white instantly.

Xie Changchuan was manageable; at most, he would make a few jokes. But the Second Miss Xie, Xie Yishu... she was a female supporting character in the book who openly harbored feelings for Wei Songjun. Xie Yishu was gentle and intelligent, and she had always disliked her—the woman who "harbored malicious intentions toward the Prince." Now that Wei Songjun was resting here and she happened to be keeping watch, with Xie Yishu’s sensitivity, she must have sensed something wrong and come to investigate!

If Xie Yishu caught them in a room alone while Wei Songjun was under the influence of the drug, she and Wei Songjun would never be able to clear their names. Wei Songjun would surely hate her to death, and all her hard work would be for nothing!

chapters.title: The Dispute
chapters.content:
Xie Yishu was half-dragging Xie Changchuan forward, causing the tall and sturdy Xie Changchuan to stumble, his silk boots clicking sharply against the stone slabs.

"Shu'er, slow down! Be careful not to fall." Xie Changchuan helplessly reached out to support her elbow, his tone a mix of indulgence and reproach.

Xie Yishu stopped abruptly. "Brother, you knew Prince Jingnan was resting in this villa, why didn't you tell me sooner? I saw Cui Mingyu lurking around here earlier. She even dragged a group of noblewomen to the front courtyard to look at lotus flowers. After the opera ended, I searched the front hall and the back courtyard but couldn't find her. She must have come here to scheme against the Prince! I absolutely cannot let her succeed!"

Wei Songjun, the only prince of a different surname in the Great Qi Dynasty, was the man she had held in her heart since she came of age. He was the hero who helped the current Emperor ascend the throne and the man of every noble girl's dreams in the capital. How could she stand by and watch a woman like Cui Mingyu get there first?

Xie Changchuan looked at his sister’s reddened eyes and sighed softly: "Why are you worrying about nothing? His Highness is peerless in martial arts; back on the battlefield, he could charge into enemy camps alone. He acts with lightning speed and his mind is as deep as a cold pool. How could a mere girl from a boudoir get the better of him?"

Xie Yishu immediately pulled her hand away, her eyes growing even redder. "Cui Mingyu is full of devious tricks and is best at using dirty tactics! His Highness is upright and honorable, with his mind set on the affairs of the state and the family; how would he know anything about these petty, underhanded schemes of the boudoir? What if he really gets deceived by her?"

Xie Changchuan knew clearly in his heart that the "upright and honorable" Prince Jingnan his sister spoke of was never a pure gentleman. Although Wei Songjun’s title was inherited from his father’s merits, everyone understood that if he hadn't exhausted the power of the Prince Jingnan’s estate five years ago to support the current Emperor—who was then neglected and nearly squeezed out of the capital—not only would the Prince Jingnan’s estate have long since become cannon fodder in the power struggle, but the very foundation of the Great Qi dynasty might have changed hands. How could a man who could stand firm in the treacherous imperial court and push the glory of the Prince Jingnan’s estate to its peak be a simple soul who didn't understand calculation?

As for Cui Mingyu, she was merely a noble daughter who had been spoiled beyond measure. Who in the capital didn't know she was obsessed with Wei Songjun? She had made quite a fool of herself for his sake—blocking the gates of the Prince Jingnan’s estate, sending carts full of love poems, and even "accidentally" tripping toward Wei Songjun during a hunt. Such desperate, clingy behavior had long been the talk of noble ladies in the capital. In front of Wei Songjun, she was likely as easy to crush as an ant.

Wei Songjun was a fine general and a trusted friend with whom one could entrust their life, but he was certainly not a suitable match. He never understood how to cherish the fairer sex. In his eyes, the difference between men and women was merely a matter of physical strength. For years, even when frequently besieged by noble ladies or socializing in pleasure quarters, he had always kept himself clean and disciplined; no one had ever heard of him losing his heart to any woman. Countless noble ladies had fallen for him, only to end up with nothing. Naturally, he did not want his own sister to step into this muddy water.

"Alright, enough," Xie Changchuan suppressed his thoughts, his tone deepening slightly. "His Highness was persuaded to drink a few too many cups at the birthday banquet at noon and said he felt dizzy and tired, so he came to this side courtyard for a nap. I’m going to check on him. You behave yourself and follow behind me; don't make a scene and disturb him, understand?"

With that, he stepped forward first. As he walked, his brows furrowed slightly—he knew Wei Songjun’s tolerance for alcohol. Being able to drink a thousand cups without getting drunk might be an exaggeration, but it was impossible for him to be so drunk that he would sleep for this long after only a few cups.

Passing through the moon-shaped gate, the view suddenly opened up. A large lotus pond spread out before them, with emerald leaves reaching toward the sky and tender pink lotus flowers peeking out from between them. Some were in full bloom like clouds, others were still in bud. As the wind blew, a fresh fragrance mixed with water vapor rushed toward them. It should have been an elegant and tranquil scene, but it was disrupted by a figure in begonia-colored clothing.

A young girl in a begonia-colored ru skirt stood by the pond, standing on tiptoe and reaching out to touch the most vibrant lotus flower in the center of the pond. Her slender fingers were only an inch away from the petals when she tripped over something, her body lunging forward. With a cry of alarm, she looked as if she were about to fall into the murky water.

"Careful!" Xie Changchuan was quick-witted; he lunged forward, caught the girl’s wrist firmly, and used the momentum to pull her back. The girl stumbled twice, still shaken, and instinctively grabbed his arm to steady herself. Her chest heaved violently, and her face was as pale as paper.

"Th-thank you, Heir, for saving me..." It took a long while for the girl to steady her voice. When she looked up, her eyes still held lingering terror. Seeing it was Xie Changchuan and Xie Yishu, she immediately curtsied. "Greetings to the Heir and the Second Miss."

Xie Yishu walked up quickly, and when she saw the girl’s face, her expression darkened instantly. "Cui Mingyu? It really is you! I knew you were hiding here with bad intentions! Are you plotting against Prince Jingnan?"

Xie Changchuan was also stunned. The girl before him had delicate features, a timid expression, and reddened eyes, looking utterly pitiful. Where was the arrogant, overbearing, and rude Miss Cui he remembered? He even blinked subconsciously, thinking he had recognized the wrong person.

"What does the Second Miss mean by that? Is His Highness here too?" Cui Mingyu looked up, her eyes filled with confusion and a hint of grievance, her voice soft and thin. "I was just feeling a bit stifled watching the play in the front hall, so I came to this courtyard for some air. The lotus flowers are blooming so beautifully, I thought I’d pick one to put in a vase, but I slipped and almost..." She turned to Xie Changchuan, patted her chest lightly, and said with a sincere tone mixed with lingering fear, "Thanks to you today, Heir, otherwise I would have made a fool of myself."

Xie Changchuan looked into her clear eyes, and his doubts grew even stronger—was this really Cui Mingyu?

"Brother, look at her!" Seeing her brother hesitate, Xie Yishu tugged at his sleeve, her voice low but intentionally loud enough for Cui Mingyu to hear. "She’s clearly faking it! She must be up to some trick!"

Cui Mingyu’s eyes turned even redder instantly, large tears welling up but held back stubbornly. "Second Miss, I really didn't... I just wanted to pick a lotus flower. If the lotus flowers here cannot be picked, then I won't pick them. Why must you wrong me so?" As she spoke, she lowered her head slightly, her shoulders trembling, looking even more pitiful.

"You're still pretending!" Xie Yishu had already decided that Cui Mingyu was up to no good. Seeing her act this way, her anger flared. Her chest heaving, she stepped forward and slapped Cui Mingyu across the face.

"Slap!" The crisp sound of the slap was particularly jarring in the quiet lotus courtyard, startling the dragonflies resting by the pond into flight. Water droplets on the lotus leaves fell with a rustle, creating ripples in the pond.

Cui Mingyu covered her face, stumbling back. Five clear red finger marks appeared on her cheek, glaringly bright. She bit her lower lip, and the tears finally fell, but she stubbornly refused to cry out. When she looked up at Xie Yishu, her eyes were full of grievance and confusion, looking so pitiful that anyone would feel compassion.

"Yishu! Stop!" Xie Changchuan’s brows knit tighter. He quickly grabbed Xie Yishu, who was about to step forward again, and said in a low voice, "Today is the Old Matriarch’s birthday, and Miss Cui is a guest. How can you be so rude! If this gets out, people will only say that we Xie family daughters don't know the rules!"

He turned to Cui Mingyu, his tone apologetic, and bowed slightly. "Miss Cui, my sister is young and ignorant, acting on impulse and losing her sense of propriety. I am truly sorry. I will have someone take you to apply medicine; let’s not ruin today’s mood." With that, he ordered the maid following him: "Take Miss Cui to the side hall to apply medicine." He really didn't want the two to argue here and cause more trouble, so he immediately dragged Xie Yishu away.

Cui Mingyu covered her face, watching their retreating backs. Her eyes flickered imperceptibly toward the tightly closed wooden door deep in the courtyard, and she let out a quiet sigh of relief. Thank goodness, she had finally managed to send them away. This slap hurt, but as long as she could hide what was happening in the room and save her own life, what was a little pain?

But before they had gone two steps, Xie Yishu suddenly broke free from Xie Changchuan’s hand, stepped back, and shouted, "Big Brother! We haven't seen His Highness yet! We’ve been arguing here for so long, talking and hitting, making such a loud noise—how could His Highness not react at all? We made a scene at the courtyard gate earlier too, and he didn't wake up—His Highness has a great tolerance for alcohol, how could he sleep so soundly? There must be something wrong in there!"

This sentence was like a thin needle, piercing the hope in Xie Changchuan’s heart. His heart tightened, his brows locked even tighter, and his previous doubts surged up again. That’s right, how could Wei Songjun sleep so soundly? Even if he had drunk too much, he should have woken up with such a commotion. He didn't hesitate anymore, ignoring Xie Yishu, and strode toward the room where Wei Songjun was resting.

Cui Mingyu’s heart jumped into her throat, and her face turned deathly pale. Oh no! Oh no! Wei Songjun was at the critical moment of the drug’s effect! If they saw Wei Songjun in his current state of burning heat, he would definitely not let her go!

She wanted to step forward to stop them, but her feet felt as heavy as lead. She could only stand frozen in place, watching helplessly as Xie Changchuan reached out and pushed open the wooden door carved with pine and crane patterns.

"Creak—" The sound of the wooden door turning seemed exceptionally long, as if it were tugging at everyone’s heartstrings.

Just then, a low, hoarse voice came from inside: "What is the commotion? Disturbing my rest."

Xie Yishu, Xie Changchuan, and Cui Mingyu were all startled, each standing frozen with their own thoughts.

The next second, a man in a black brocade robe walked out of the room. His posture was as straight as a pine tree, his dark hair half-tied, with a few stray locks hanging over his forehead, adding a touch of laziness and weariness to his deeply contoured face. However, his complexion was slightly pale, his eyes held lingering fatigue, his thin lips were pressed tightly together, and the air around him was heavier than usual—the pressure of someone who had long held a position of power.

It was Wei Songjun.

***

Seeing Wei Songjun, the heavy feeling that had been hanging in Cui Mingyu’s chest for nearly an hour finally dissipated, and her shoulders slumped unconsciously. But when she looked closely at Wei Songjun, her heart, which had just settled, tightened again.

Although Wei Songjun stood straight and steady, his face was as pale as rice paper, and a trace of lingering weariness remained between his brows. Cui Mingyu’s gaze lingered on his pale face, secretly wondering: Is he better, or has he not fully recovered? I hope he didn't force himself to use his internal energy...

Xie Changchuan stepped forward quickly. He caught the impatience and weakness hidden between Wei Songjun’s brows, and his heart rose instantly. His tone became cautious: "Your Highness? Is something wrong?"

Wei Songjun’s gaze slowly swept over the servants standing with bowed heads and the Xie family members. His eyes were as indifferent as a cold pool, calm and waveless, but they paused for a split second when they touched Cui Mingyu’s cheek. The faint finger mark was still clearly printed on her fair, delicate skin, like rouge on fallen snow, causing a flash of coldness to pass through his eyes—so fast that no one could notice. Before Cui Mingyu could detect this fleeting look, he had already shifted his gaze to Xie Changchuan, his voice laced with an unmistakable fatigue: "Changchuan, my migraine has flared up. I am returning to the Prince Jingnan’s estate. Please convey my apologies to the Old Matriarch on my behalf."

"A migraine?" Xie Changchuan’s heart tightened, his brows knitting into a knot. He clearly remembered that Wei Songjun’s chronic illness had been treated by famous doctors in the capital for half a year and usually wouldn't flare up easily. Why would it recur so suddenly today? "Your Highness, why don't you rest in the side hall of the estate for a moment? I will send someone to invite the estate physician to take your pulse."

Xie Yishu, standing to the side, also hurriedly stepped forward half a step. Her face was filled with genuine concern, and her voice was so soft it could drip with water: "Yes, Your Highness. My family’s physician is among the best in the capital, especially skilled in treating head ailments. Please, let him take a look at you."

Wei Songjun waved his hand slightly: "No need. Prepare the carriage for me."

Seeing this, Xie Changchuan knew that further persuasion would be futile—he knew Wei Songjun’s temperament best; once he made up his mind, ten oxen could not pull him back. He reached out to gently press down on Xie Yishu, who was about to speak again, and bowed to Wei Songjun: "Then, Your Highness, please wait a moment. I will go make arrangements." With that, he half-dragged and half-coaxed the clearly unwilling Xie Yishu away, applying subtle pressure with his fingertips to signal her not to act recklessly.

The courtyard fell silent instantly, leaving only Cui Mingyu and Wei Songjun standing opposite each other. A faint blush suddenly appeared on the tips of Wei Songjun’s ears, which, against his pale complexion, made him look strangely fragile and embarrassed. He coughed unnaturally, deliberately using a cold, stiff tone to mask his discomfort, and after a pause, spoke in a voice lower than before: "Go and clean the room."

Cui Mingyu was stunned for a moment before realizing what he meant—it seemed the effects of the aphrodisiac had finally worn off. Her heart leaped with joy, and she quickly put on a smile and stepped forward, her tone carrying a hint of deliberate ingratiation: "I’ll go right away. Your Highness, does this count as making up for my mistakes? Could you please be the bigger person and not hold it against me? I promise to keep to myself from now on and never cause you trouble again. In the future, wherever you are, I guarantee I will automatically keep my distance and never be an eyesore to you!"

Hearing this, Wei Songjun let out a faint, cold laugh. The sound escaped his nostrils, tinged with mockery. He truly could not understand this woman before him. Previously, she had been eager to pester him, sending flowers and notes, her words full of blatant affection. Yet now, she avoided him as if he were a flood or a wild beast, wishing to draw a clear line. She was the one who had drugged him; she was the one who had plotted against him, and yet, at a critical moment, she was also the one who had appeared out of nowhere to try and preserve his dignity. His long, narrow eyes narrowed slightly, and his cold, sharp gaze fell upon Cui Mingyu like a blade: "Cui Mingyu, I don't care what you are planning. I will spare your life for now, for the sake of your father, but that does not mean your merits and faults are balanced."

Cui Mingyu’s eyes, which had been bright as stars just a moment ago, instantly dimmed, and the heart she had just set at ease rose back into her throat. She frowned, full of confusion: What did he mean by that? Why did he have to leave half his words unsaid? Had he forgiven her or not? Was he still going to pursue the matter of the drugging, or did he have other demands? She opened her mouth, about to step forward and ask, but the rhythmic footsteps of guards could be heard in the distance—Wei Songjun’s personal guards had arrived and were standing respectfully to the side with their heads bowed, not daring to breathe loudly.

Wei Songjun did not look at her again. His thin lips were pressed into a cold, hard line, and his black robes fluttered slightly in the wind. He walked straight toward the courtyard gate, his back straight, exuding an indescribable coldness and aloofness.

Cui Mingyu watched his retreating figure, so angry she couldn't help but stomp her foot, muttering under her breath: "What kind of person is he? Speaking so unclearly!" But then she thought, at least there was a turning point—at least Wei Songjun hadn't mentioned taking her life again. The mess the original owner had made by drugging him had, at the very least, been eight-tenths cleaned up. Thinking this, the fire in her heart subsided, and she sighed helplessly, turning to walk toward the bathhouse, followed by a bewildered Bitao.

As soon as she pushed open the door to the bathhouse, a thick, fishy scent of semen hit her, making Cui Mingyu subconsciously cover her nose, her brows knitting together. Even though she was usually thick-skinned, the tips of her ears turned bright red, and even her neck was stained with a faint pink. In her heart, she cursed both the original owner and Wei Songjun in turn: It was all these two people—one reckless and impulsive, drugging him, and the other, once the drug took effect, creating this mess. In the end, she, an innocent transmigrator, had to clean up the aftermath. It was truly the worst luck!

Bitao followed behind, sniffing the air in confusion, her little brows also knitting together. Curious and puzzled, she looked up and asked: "Miss, what is this smell? It’s strange, it doesn't smell like the fishy smell from the ice we brought over!"

"Don't sniff it, don't sniff it!" Cui Mingyu waved her hands, fearing she would keep asking, "Just wash this bathhouse thoroughly and wipe it clean. Make sure no one finds out, or we’ll both be in trouble!"

Although Bitao wasn't very bright, she was very obedient and worked efficiently. Hearing her mistress's words, she immediately nodded: "Oh, I understand, Miss!" She scrubbed the bathhouse with nimble hands, and before long, the strange smell was largely washed away by the water, and the room began to fill with the clean scent of soap locust. Cui Mingyu stood at the door supervising, and only when she saw the room becoming clean and tidy did she finally breathe a sigh of relief.

On the other side, Xie Changchuan had already prepared the carriage. Wei Songjun walked to the side of the carriage and was about to bend down to board when his footsteps suddenly paused. His gaze shifted to Xie Yishu, who was standing under the veranda not far away—she was looking in his direction, the affection and expectation in her eyes almost overflowing, yet she was forcing herself to appear dignified, her fingers tightly clutching her skirt.

For some reason, the slap mark on Cui Mingyu’s face flashed clearly in his mind. He withdrew his gaze and lowered his voice to Xie Changchuan beside him: "Your sister should be disciplined properly."

Xie Changchuan’s heart sank. He realized that his sister’s recklessness, arrogance, and jealousy at inappropriate times had all been seen by Wei Songjun, and his impression of her must be extremely poor.

But the next second, his heart inexplicably eased—perhaps this was for the best. Wei Songjun was of noble status and unfathomable mind; if his sister were to marry him, she might not find happiness. Now that His Highness had no affection for her, it might help her break that unrealistic delusion, which, for her, might not be a bad thing.

He quickly replied: "Thank you for the reminder, Your Highness. I will certainly restrain my sister and discipline her strictly in the future, so she will never cause trouble or offend others again."

Wei Songjun did not speak again, only nodding slightly before bending down to enter the carriage. The heavy brocade curtain fell, cutting off the noise and figures outside. The coachman shouted, the horsewhip flicked lightly, and the carriage wheels slowly turned, rumbling out of the courtyard gate toward the Prince of Jingnan’s mansion.

chapters.title: Xia Yuning
chapters.content:
After finishing dinner at the Xie residence, Cui Mingyu and her father took a carriage home. Her father sat in the carriage in front, while she and Chuntao sat in the one behind. She subconsciously reached up to touch her left cheek—the ointment Xie Changchuan had sent was truly as effective as rumored; the skin was now delicate and smooth, and not even a trace of red remained.

Chuntao sat to one side, carefully holding two items. One was a clean bottle carved from mutton-fat white jade, the bottle body as lustrous as warm jade, with a few fresh lotus flowers tucked inside. The other was a sandalwood box with gold-traced lotus patterns, filled with a斛 of South Sea pearls, each the size of a thumb, round and plump. It was said that they could reflect seven layers of luster in the sunlight. These were all specifically sent by Xie Changchuan as an apology for his sister, Xie Yishu.

Cui Mingyu leaned against the soft couch, her gaze sweeping over the wooden box, and a faint curve appeared at the corner of her mouth, without the slightest intention of declining. After all, that slap had been truly painful, and the original owner had been so pampered that she had never suffered such grievances. Now that she had received this斛 of pearls, it could be considered a real compensation, and the frustration she had been holding in her heart faded by more than half along with the shimmering pearls. Seeing her expression soften, Chuntao whispered: "Miss, the eldest young master Xie is quite sincere, but the second young lady Xie was too much. We should stay away from her in the future."

When the carriage reached the main gate of the Cui residence, the gatekeeper was already waiting. Seeing the carriage stop, he immediately stepped forward to lift the curtain and set up the footstool. Cui Mingyu stepped out with Chuntao’s help. Just as she stood steady, she felt the night breeze carrying the warm light of the lanterns hit her face. Two vermilion lanterns hung on the pillars in front of the gate, swaying gently in the wind. The warm yellow glow flickered, outlining a figure in the shadows not far away, though it was blurry, one could vaguely tell it was a standing man.

Chuntao beside her immediately pouted, lowering her voice with impatience and disdain: "It’s this Young Master Xia again. Why is he like a piece of sticky candy, haunting us? This is the how many-th time? Miss clearly threw away the things he sent before, and yet he still comes."

Young Master Xia? A thought stirred in Cui Mingyu’s mind, and two memories instantly flooded her brain. One was from the original owner—this man was Xia Yuning, the legitimate second son of the Marquis of Changning. His mother was the Marquis’s second wife, born into a Jiangnan merchant family. Ever since he saw the original owner at the Lantern Festival three years ago, he had become her most loyal suitor, sending flowers, tea, and snacks, rain or shine, only to be coldly rejected by the arrogant original owner every time, sometimes even being humiliated. The other memory was from the real world she came from, where her roommate discussed this ancient romance novel with her: "Look at this Xia Yuning, he’s so infatuated! The female supporting character is so bad, and in the end, she’s killed and abandoned in the wilderness by Wei Songjun. Everyone in the capital fears Wei Songjun’s power and no one dares to go near her, but it’s him who collects her body and finds a good place to bury her. For such a bad character to have someone so infatuated with her, that’s the kind of treatment only a female lead should get!"

As she was pondering, the figure had already walked up quickly, bowing respectfully to Cui Yong who was coming to meet them. His movements were standard, his attitude humble, and his voice clear yet tinged with a hint of restraint: "Junior Xia Yuning pays his respects to Minister Cui."

Cui Yong’s gaze first swept over his daughter, then fell back on Xia Yuning, his eyes filled with a hint of approving warmth. He had always favored this young man; although he was from a Marquis’s house, he had none of the dissolute air of a noble son. He was neither addicted to pleasure like other young aristocrats nor did he engage in vices like cockfighting or dog racing. His mother was from a merchant family, and he had helped her manage their business since he was young. Although he had no interest in an official career, he had no trace of merchant-like vulgarity; instead, he was upright, humble, and possessed a gentle, jade-like demeanor. It was a pity that his own daughter had eyes only for the Prince of Jingnan, Wei Songjun, and had always turned a blind eye to Xia Yuning’s overtures, even showing great disgust.

Cui Yong sighed softly, his gaze catching the sandalwood food box Xia Yuning was clutching tightly—the box didn't look large, but it was made of fine materials, with tiny beeswax embedded in the corners, clearly prepared with great care.

Xia Yuning hurriedly said: "I went to Jiangnan and brought back some candied fruits, specifically to bring them for the residence to taste."

Cui Yong understood his intentions and said gently: "You are very thoughtful to make this trip. She has always loved sweets; since you are here, why not give them to her yourself!"

Upon hearing this, as if he had received a great favor, Xia Yuning quickly replied "Yes," and walked quickly toward Cui Mingyu, his steps even a little unsteady.

Cui Yong shook his head slightly, watching his back, and secretly thought that all his painstaking efforts were likely to go to waste once again.

By the dim, yellowish light of the lantern, Cui Mingyu finally saw his appearance clearly. Unlike the impression of him being "slightly chubby" in the original owner's memory, the man before her had a face that was indeed a bit round, but by no means bloated. Instead, it looked like a youth whose features had not yet fully matured, carrying a certain boyish innocence and gentleness. His eyebrows were straight, sword-like brows; though his eyes were not particularly large, they shone as if filled with starlight. His nose was well-defined and his lip line clear, though he was biting his lips slightly out of nervousness. He wore a moon-white brocade robe with subtle patterns, which made his posture appear straight and tall. Standing in the flickering light, he lacked any of the "chubby" clumsiness, instead exuding the refined elegance of a young man from a noble family, which, paired with his slightly constrained expression, added a touch of sincerity.

"Miss Cui," Xia Yuning’s voice was lower than when he had spoken to Cui Yong just moments before. His eyes were filled with cautious anticipation as he slowly lifted the lid of the food box. "I just returned to the capital from Jiangnan today. I heard that the candied fruits from there are the most authentic, so I specifically had someone pick some out from a time-honored shop. I wonder if you might like them?"

As the food box opened just a crack, a rich yet not cloying sweet fragrance, mingled with a faint scent of fruit, wafted out. Cui Mingyu leaned in to look and saw that the box was divided into four small compartments, each neatly arranged: square-cut hawthorn jelly, translucent golden candied dates coated in sugar frost, plump and enticing emerald-green candied plums, and dark-brown salted tangerine peel. One look was enough to tell they were carefully selected delicacies. Cui Mingyu had eaten a hearty dinner and was feeling a bit greasy, so these candied fruits arrived just at the right moment, perfectly suiting her mood.

"I... I didn't know which flavor you preferred, so I prepared a bit of everything," Xia Yuning said, looking at her with eager eyes. He gently pushed the food box forward, his tone hiding an irrepressible nervousness, not even daring to look her in the eye. "If they aren't to your taste, next time I will..."

"That won't be necessary." Cui Mingyu softly interrupted him. His robes carried the damp, humid air characteristic of Jiangnan; he must have just stepped off the canal boat and, without even returning to the Changning Marquis Mansion, rushed to the Cui residence with the candied fruits. Such dedication would move even a heart of stone.

She reached out with both hands to take the food box. "Thank you for your trouble, Young Master Xia. These candied fruits look wonderful." As she spoke, she picked up a candied plum and gently placed it in her mouth. The clear, sweet sugar coating melted on the tip of her tongue, followed by the slight tartness of the plum, which instantly washed away the greasy feeling in her mouth and left her heart feeling refreshed. Her eyes brightened slightly, and she praised him sincerely, "The taste is excellent. I like it very much."

At these words, Xia Yuning’s eyes lit up instantly, as if stars had suddenly ignited in a silent night sky. He had been fully prepared for rejection—after all, the silks, satins, and rare trinkets he had sent before were either thrown to the ground by the original owner or given away to servants; there had never been a moment where his gifts were accepted so readily, let alone praised. He opened his mouth, unable to speak for a long time, and only after a while did he stammer, "I... I'm glad you like them! Then... if you prefer any particular kind, I will have someone go to Jiangnan to purchase more, or have the shop there send them regularly every month. I guarantee they will always be fresh!"

Watching his nervous yet sincere demeanor, Cui Mingyu couldn't help but laugh, her eyebrows curving like peach blossoms in spring. Her gaze swept over the lotus flowers and pearls in Chun Tao's arms. The pearls were a treasure she had just acquired, and she naturally couldn't bear to give them away as a return gift, so she pointed to the lotus flowers in the mutton-fat jade vase. "You went to the trouble of bringing me candied fruits, so I should give you a return gift. These lotus flowers were freshly picked and look quite fresh. I hope you won't mind, Young Master Xia." Cui Mingyu did not understand the value of the mutton-fat jade vase; had she known, she likely wouldn't have been willing to give it to Xia Yuning either.

Xia Yuning was even more pleasantly surprised, his body straightening almost subconsciously. Having followed his mother in business since childhood, he had a sharp eye and could tell at a glance that the white jade vase was of excellent quality—warm, delicate, and without a single flaw. This vase alone was worth a hundred times more than his entire box of candied fruits. That she was willing to give him such a precious container holding lotus flowers made his heart burn with an intensity that surpassed any treasure.

He hurriedly took the jade vase with both hands, holding it firmly to his chest, his voice trembling with irrepressible emotion: "I don't mind! How could I mind? Thank you, Miss! Thank you, Miss!" He looked down at the beautiful lotus flowers in the vase, his heart feeling as if it had been soaked in honey, swelling with sweetness.

After hesitating for a moment, he summoned all his courage, looked up at Cui Mingyu with eyes full of sincere anticipation, and said in a voice that was soft yet exceptionally clear: "Since you also like lotus flowers, I have heard that in a few days, the lotus flowers at Yancui Lake will bloom one after another. At that time, the lotus leaves will stretch to the sky, and the lotus flowers reflecting the sun will be a magnificent sight. I wonder... I wonder if you would do me the honor of going to view the flowers with me?"

After saying this, he stared intently at Cui Mingyu’s eyes, his palms sweating, his breath held. The warm light of the lantern fell upon his face, clearly revealing his nervous and expectant expression.

Seeing him like this, Cui Mingyu felt a stir in her heart. She didn't agree immediately, nor did she refuse, but her fingers tightened around the food box. Although she had a favorable impression of Xia Yuning, she couldn't afford to be too obvious, so she said softly, "This... let's talk about it in a few days."

Though slightly disappointed, Xia Yuning was also relieved—at least she hadn't refused outright! He nodded hurriedly, a smile blooming on his face again: "Good! Good! Then I shall await your good news! I won't disturb your rest any longer; I shall take my leave!"

He bowed to Cui Yong once more before leaving the entrance of the Cui residence, clutching the vase of lotus flowers and looking back every few steps. His figure gradually disappeared into the night, his footsteps even lighter than when he had arrived.

Cui Mingyu stood where she was, watching his retreating figure. Chun Tao leaned in, somewhat surprised, and said, "Miss, you actually accepted Young Master Xia's gift today? Didn't you hate him the most before?"

Cui Mingyu smiled without explaining. This Xia Yuning, whom her roommate had called the "infatuated second male lead," was far more real than that cold-hearted Prince Jingnan, Wei Songjun.

chapters.title: Father and Daughter Heart-to-Heart
chapters.content:
Cui Yong’s gaze was fixed on the hem of her begonia-colored skirt, the turbulent waves in his heart refusing to settle.

The Cui Mingyu of today was truly different.

At the birthday banquet at the Xie residence this afternoon, faced with the thinly veiled mockery of other noble ladies, she neither lashed out as she usually did, nor did she leave in a fit of pique. Instead, she handled the situation with composure, coaxing the Old Matriarch Ning into high spirits.

And now, seeing her treat Xia Yuning—whom she had always treated like discarded shoes—with such kindness, Cui Yong felt his head buzzing. In his forty-plus years of life, he had seen enough intrigue and fickle behavior in the imperial court, but he had never imagined that his own daughter, whom he knew best, would one day become a complete stranger to him.

"Mingzhu'er," Cui Yong finally could not suppress the doubt in his heart, "you are... rather strange today."

Mingzhu'er was the pet name he had used since her birth. When Cui Mingyu was born, she was as delicate as if carved from jade. Overjoyed, Cui Yong declared her the "bright pearl" (Mingzhu) of the Cui family and wanted to name her Cui Mingzhu. However, Madam Cui felt the name "Mingzhu" was too common, and after much deliberation, settled on "Mingyu," taking the meaning of "pearls and jade by one's side, warm and radiant." Yet, Cui Yong could never change his habit, still calling her "Mingzhu'er," as if only by doing so could he express how much he cherished his daughter.

Hearing this, Cui Mingyu felt a subtle pause in her heart.

She was indeed strange.

Since she had occupied the original owner's body, she could not let the tragedy repeat itself. She had to change the original owner's fate, and naturally, she could not follow the original path. But the concept of transmigrating into a book was too shocking; if people found out, she feared she would be burned as a demon. Therefore, she had to be extremely careful—changing her destiny without exposing her identity.

She turned her head to look at her father’s face, filled with confusion and inquiry. A flash of playfulness crossed her eyes, and her tone carried a touch of spoiled innocence: "Father, do you not like me being this way?"

Cui Yong waved his hands hurriedly, his tone urgent: "Like it? How could I not like it? I am overjoyed!"

How could he not like it? His daughter had been so arrogant in the past, offending many people. He didn't know how many messes he had cleaned up for her in private, nor how many times he had tried to persuade her, but she had always let his words go in one ear and out the other. Now that his daughter had become sensible and steady, with a proper sense of propriety, this was exactly what he had dreamed of.

The father and daughter walked side by side into the mansion, passed through the covered walkway, and sat down in the flower hall. A maid served freshly brewed Longjing tea, the fragrance curling in the air. Cui Yong picked up his teacup but did not drink; instead, he looked at his daughter and said earnestly, "Mingzhu'er, Father knows you used to look down on that boy from the Xia family, but I can tell that the second Xia boy is honest and sincere toward you. If you have feelings for him, that would be for the best; but if you don't, then don't smile at him like that, lest you give him the wrong idea and toy with someone's genuine heart."

He paused here, his tone becoming increasingly grave: "As for Prince Jingnan... Mingzhu'er, listen to your father's advice. That man is deep-thinking and unpredictable, and his surroundings are fraught with crises and complex situations. Let's not wade into those muddy waters. Can't you choose someone else to like?"

Cui Mingyu’s fingers, holding the teacup, paused slightly, and a warm current surged in her heart.

She knew that the original owner’s mother had passed away from illness when she was ten. Fearing that a stepmother might mistreat his daughter, Cui Yong had ignored the advice of others and never remarried. As the Minister of Revenue, he was busy with official duties, but whenever he had time, he would personally teach his daughter to read, write, and conduct herself in the world. It was just that most of the time, he was spread too thin, and the tutors and nannies in the mansion, knowing how much Minister Cui treasured his daughter, dared not truly discipline her strictly. Over time, this had fostered the original owner's lawless personality.

When the original owner was alive, Cui Yong had given her such earnest advice countless times, but she had been so infatuated with Prince Jingnan’s stunning beauty and immense power that she hadn't listened to a word. Every time, it ended with the father and daughter parting on bad terms. Cui Yong likely hadn't expected these words to have any effect today, just mentioning it in passing.

But Cui Mingyu raised her eyes, looking at her father with clear, limpid eyes, and nodded solemnly: "Okay, I won't like him anymore from now on."

"What did you say?" Cui Yong looked up abruptly, his eyes full of disbelief. The teacup in his hand clattered against the table, splashing a few drops of tea. He stared blankly at his daughter, as if seeing her for the first time. "Mingzhu'er, are... are you serious?"

Cui Mingyu picked up the teapot and refilled her father’s cup, her movements skillful and gentle: "Father, today while I was resting in the side courtyard of the Ning residence, I had a dream in my daze."

She lowered her eyes, her voice carrying a touch of well-timed lingering fear: "I dreamed that I was obsessed with Prince Jingnan, but I ended up in a miserable state, not even getting to see you one last time."

At this point, she looked up, her eyes shimmering with a hint of moisture, her tone incredibly sincere: "Father, that dream was so real; it frightened me so much that I woke up covered in cold sweat. I don't want to like him anymore. Even if I run into him on the street in the future, I will stay far, far away from him."

Cui Yong listened quietly, his eyes gradually reddening. He reached out, trembling, wanting to stroke his daughter's hair. The Prince of Jingnan held immense power and was ruthless in his methods; he had long worried that his daughter would suffer grievances if she married into that household. With the Cui family's influence, they were insignificant before the Prince of Jingnan. If his daughter truly married him and Wei Songjun treated her poorly, even if he risked his old life, he might not be able to protect her.

"Good child, good child..." Cui Yong’s voice choked, and tears finally spilled over, rolling down his cheeks and dripping onto his lapel. "It’s fortunate that it was just a dream, fortunate that you woke up. The Xia family is different. Although the Xia Marquis’s estate is gradually declining, the Xia second son is kind-hearted and sincere toward you. As long as I am alive, I can protect you, and the Xia family would never dare to treat you poorly in the slightest."

Watching her father’s agitated and incoherent state, a warm current surged through Cui Mingyu’s heart. Although the original owner had been spoiled, having a father who loved her so dearly was a stroke of luck. She smiled softly: "Father, who says I must marry the second young master of the Xia family?"

Cui Yong was startled, then laughed, wiping the tears from his face, his eyes full of relief: "Not marrying him is fine, too. Not marrying is fine. If there is someone you have your eye on, as long as they are of upright character and pure heart, and someone I can manage, I will agree to it."

He looked at his daughter’s delicate brows and eyes, his tone incredibly solemn: "I do not ask for you to be wealthy or noble, nor do I ask for you to marry into a family of princes, generals, or ministers. I only hope that you can live your life steadily, safely, and happily—that is enough."

"Father..." Cui Mingyu felt a lump in her throat, and her eyes reddened as well. Having transmigrated into this strange world, she had been all alone, but the love of this father before her gave her a long-lost sense of warmth. She stood up, walked to her father’s side, and gently hugged his arm, her voice soft and sweet: "In the past, it was your daughter who was ignorant and caused you worry and heartache. From now on, your daughter will definitely be well-behaved, listen to you, study hard, learn the rules, and never make you angry again."

"Yes, yes!" Cui Yong responded repeatedly, so moved that he didn't know where to put his hands, eventually settling for holding his daughter’s hand tightly. Her hand was soft and warm, and the temperature it transmitted made his heart feel incredibly comforted. He had hoped for his daughter to become sensible for so many years, and today, having finally seen his wish come true, he was deeply gratified and could not find more words to say, only wiping away his tears incessantly.

As the night deepened and the moon climbed to the center of the sky, the father and daughter exchanged more casual conversation. Cui Mingyu personally saw her father back to his study before turning to return to her own courtyard.

Cui Yong sat in his study, but he felt no sleepiness. He stood up, picked up an oil lamp from the table, and walked slowly toward the ancestral hall in the backyard.
