Cui Mingyu pouted in disappointment upon hearing this. It was true; which young lady in the capital didn't want to show her face in public? But with Mu Wanzhou present, everyone else would become mere background, so naturally, few were willing to go and invite humiliation.

She propped her chin on her hand, lost in thought. "Isn't there anyone outstanding among the male guests? Can't someone show up to make this invitation worth a bit more?"

Bitao tilted her head, thinking, and her eyes suddenly lit up. "Oh, right, Miss! I heard that the Prince of Jingnan’s estate also received an invitation from Grand Tutor Xu this year! But I don't know if His Highness the Prince of Jingnan will go."

"Wei Songjun?" Cui Mingyu was startled, her fingers tightening subconsciously on the invitation. He actually received an invitation? Would he go?

If he went, she wouldn't. She had already made up her mind to keep her distance from him and avoid any further entanglement, so she naturally didn't want to run into him at such an event and increase the awkwardness.

Qinghe, listening from the side, laughed and said, "Miss, don't worry. His Highness the Prince of Jingnan has always shown respect to Grand Tutor Xu and accepts the invitation every time, but look—has he ever actually gone? He just goes through the motions to be polite."

Is that so? Cui Mingyu felt uneasy. In previous gatherings, there was no Mu Wanzhou, so it was normal for him not to go. But this time, his official love interest, Mu Wanzhou, would be making an appearance. Given the inertia of the original plot, would the male lead really be absent?

***

chapters.title: The Poetry Gathering
chapters.content:
Morning dew still clung to the crabapple trees in the courtyard when Cui Yong began urging Cui Mingyu: "Mingzhu, hurry up and get up! We can't be late for the Xu family’s poetry gathering today!"

Cui Mingyu sat up, rubbing her sleepy eyes, and before she could react, she was surrounded by several maids personally assigned by her father. In front of the mirror, the fragrance of powder lingered as the maids skillfully styled her hair, inserting a gold-inlaid kingfisher feather hairpin. They then brought over the dress that had been prepared—a bright red, cross-collared, wide-sleeved gown with dark gold lotus patterns embroidered on the hem. Sunlight streamed through the window, casting a warm, brilliant luster on the fabric.

"Father, isn't this a bit too flashy?" Cui Mingyu frowned at the mirror. The original owner’s appearance was already outstanding, and this vibrant attire made her features look like a painting, her lips like cherries, giving her a beauty that was even more breathtaking than usual.

Cui Yong stood to the side with his hands behind his back, looking at his beautiful daughter in the mirror with a satisfied expression. "As the eldest daughter of the Cui family attending a poetry gathering, one must naturally look dignified. This way, others can see that the young ladies of the Cui family are second to none." After giving a few more instructions about "not losing decorum" and "making friends with other noble ladies," he finally let her leave.

The Cui family’s carriage slowly pulled up in front of the Xu residence. Just as she lifted the curtain, she saw another plain cloth carriage pull up on the other side. The curtain was lifted, and Princess Chaogui stepped out. Today, Chaogui looked completely different from usual; she wore no elaborate palace attire, only a simple white cross-collared dress with faint orchid patterns embroidered on the cuffs. She wore only a single mutton-fat jade hairpin, looking as pure as if she were unstained by dust. Yet, that innate nobility and elegance gave her a grace that was "like a lotus rising from clear water, natural and unadorned."

Their eyes met, and they both smiled. Chaogui walked over first and naturally took her arm. "You’ve come at just the right time."

As Chaogui held her arm, Cui Mingyu looked down at her own red dress and then glanced at Chaogui’s plain attire. Her cheeks warmed; by comparison, she looked like a peacock deliberately fanning its tail, far too eye-catching.

"You’ve certainly put effort into this outfit," Chaogui said, looking her over with a nod of approval, her tone teasing. "It is indeed a feast for the eyes."

Cui Mingyu’s cheeks flushed even more, feeling that Chaogui was implying something, so she quickly changed the subject. "Princess, I remember you never attended these kinds of poetry gatherings before. Why are you here today?"

Chaogui carelessly brushed a stray lock of hair from her temple, her tone casual. "I’m different from you. You don't know how, and I don't care to. I’m here today entirely to give you face." She paused, leaned closer to Cui Mingyu, and lowered her voice. "Besides, I also want to see if there are any young men in this capital who catch my eye."

Did she have to be so blunt? Cui Mingyu rolled her eyes inwardly, but couldn't help but smile as she walked into the Xu residence with Chaogui.

The Xu family’s garden was already beautifully arranged with rockeries, flowing water, and winding paths. Tables and chairs were set up everywhere, and noble youths and young ladies were gathered in small groups, chatting. As soon as Cui Mingyu and Chaogui sat down in a spot overlooking the lake, low whispers broke out around them, and gazes were cast their way.

"Heavens, Princess Chaogui is actually here? Could it be that she’s using the poetry gathering to choose a new husband?"

"Hard to say. Look at the eldest Miss Cui beside her. She used to have her heart set on the Prince of Jingnan, but now she’s here too. Perhaps she’s given up on him and is looking for a new match."

"Then what does that have to do with the Princess?"

"Have you forgotten? The Princess and the eldest Miss Cui have always been close; she must be here to help her vet the candidates."

"I personally think the Princess is the one looking for a husband!"

"Stop joking. With so many handsome attendants in the Princess's manor, why would she give up the whole forest for just one tree?"

"By the way, why hasn't Miss Mu arrived yet?"

"A person as ethereal as a celestial being naturally needs to make a grand finale entrance to be worthy of her status."

At this moment, a disdainful voice cut in, tinged with a hint of jealousy: "What celestial being? I heard that Mu Wanzhou is hell-bent on becoming the Empress. But the Emperor has been on the throne for five years, and the position of the Middle Palace remains vacant. She must be getting impatient, which is why she’s come to this poetry gathering to seek other options."

"Really?"

"My father serves in the imperial court, and I've heard that people submit memorials every day requesting the appointment of an Empress, but the Emperor simply won't budge. No one knows what he's thinking."

The voices behind them dropped to a whisper. Cui Mingyu pricked up her ears, but could only catch a few fragmented words, her curiosity piqued. She turned to look at Chaogui beside her, only to see the Princess leaning lazily on a carved chair, her slender fingers pinching a pink, translucent candied fruit, slowly bringing it to her lips. The sunlight fell on her plain white sleeves, making the orchid patterns look even more elegant. Suddenly remembering that Chaogui was the Emperor's own sister and must know the inside story, she leaned over and whispered, "Princess, your Imperial Brother... why has he never appointed an Empress?"

Chaogui’s hand holding the candied fruit froze abruptly. A flash of something strange crossed her eyes before she returned to her languid demeanor. She didn't answer, but instead pinched a piece of the fruit and stuffed it into Cui Mingyu’s mouth. The sweetness melted on her tongue instantly. "The Emperor's heart is unfathomable," she said in a flat tone. "Some things, the less you know, the longer you live."

As she spoke, she picked up another piece for herself. Her gaze fell on the lotus pond outside the pavilion, as if watching the fish or perhaps lost in thought, her brows hiding a depth of mystery that Cui Mingyu could not decipher.

Caught off guard, Cui Mingyu nearly choked on the candy and had to cough twice to recover. Seeing Chaogui’s inscrutable expression, she immediately understood—imperial matters were the most complex, and as a daughter of a noble family, she really shouldn't pry. She suppressed her curiosity and stopped asking.

Just then, a greater commotion broke out among the ladies. Even those who were chatting stopped, their gazes fixed on the garden entrance. Cui Mingyu followed their eyes, and her heart skipped a beat—a dark-robed figure was walking along the path through the flowers and trees. His black hair was tied up with a jade crown, his posture as straight as a pine, and the white jade pendant at his waist chimed softly with his steps. The man’s brows were deep and cold, carrying an inherent, unapproachable majesty. It was none other than Prince Jingnan, Wei Songjun.

Why was he here? Could this be the so-called "protagonist effect"? Presumably, that Miss Mu should be arriving soon. Once the male and female leads met, there would surely be lingering glances and budding romance—where would there be any room for her, the "vicious supporting female character"?

"I'm going to hide," Cui Mingyu whispered, rising to leave, but Chaogui grabbed her wrist.

"What are you doing?" Chaogui raised an eyebrow, looking puzzled.

"I told Prince Jingnan that I would keep my distance whenever I saw him," Cui Mingyu said urgently. "I’d better leave quickly so as not to be an eyesore."

Instead of letting go, Chaogui applied a little force and pulled her back into her seat. She looked toward Wei Songjun, her eyes filled with the pride of imperial nobility, her tone domineering: "What are you panicking about? Is this Xu family poetry gathering his territory?" She turned to look at Cui Mingyu and patted her hand gently. "Sit still. As long as I, the Princess, want you here, even if the Emperor himself came, he wouldn't have the right to chase you away."

chapters.title: Walking on Thin Ice
chapters.content:
A subtle commotion rippled through the edge of the crowd, followed by hushed discussions spreading like waves.

"Why is His Highness Prince Jingnan here?"

"Why wasn't there even a whisper of this beforehand? Although this poetry gathering is hosted by Grand Secretary Xu, the Prince has never involved himself in such leisurely, elegant occasions!"

"Why else? Perhaps he heard that Miss Mu Wanzhou would be here today and came specifically to admire her grace!"

"I was wondering why the Cui family miss came too—she’s never been interested in poetry. It turns out she knew His Highness would be here and came specifically to see him!"

"It was always rumored that Prince Jingnan wasn't interested in women. It seems that was just a rumor; he clearly has someone in his heart!"

The snippets of conversation drifted into Cui Mingyu's ears. Her fingers, clutching her round fan, tightened until the fan ribs pressed painfully into her palm. Her temper flared like a lit fuse—what did this have to do with her? If she had known Wei Songjun would be here, she would have stayed home and feigned illness for three days rather than set foot in the Xu manor!

Just as she was fuming, she saw Wei Songjun’s gaze sweep across the crowd, pausing briefly on a girl in red with bright, expressive eyes. He then lowered his gaze, masking all emotion, and walked steadily toward the guest seats near the main table.

"Your Highness! What brings you here today?" Xie Changchuan, the heir to the Duke of Ning, was the first to stand up, his face full of surprise. He had known Wei Songjun since childhood and knew well that the Prince loathed tedious formalities; even ten invitations to a typical poetry gathering wouldn't be enough to move him.

After sitting down, Wei Songjun raised his eyes and replied coolly, "Nothing to do, just came to look around." His tone was flat, revealing no ripples of emotion.

At this point, Grand Secretary Xu, dressed in brocade robes and looking vigorous despite his age, stood up from the main seat to welcome him, stroking his goatee with a hearty laugh: "Songjun, what a rare guest! I thought you would decline this invitation again."

Wei Songjun stood up upon hearing this, bowing slightly with a demeanor that was proper yet distant: "Since the teacher invited me, it would be rude to refuse."

Cui Mingyu, listening from not far away, couldn't help but sneer inwardly. How high-sounding. Grand Secretary Xu had invited him before, so why did he happen to come today? It was clearly because he knew the original female lead, Mu Wanzhou, would shine at this gathering, and he, the male lead, had rushed over to make his presence felt.

No sooner had she finished her internal monologue than she felt a sharp gaze land on her. Cui Mingyu’s heart jumped. She looked up and met Wei Songjun’s eyes—his gaze seemed to carry inquiry, perhaps even some hidden meaning, making her spine stiffen. She hurriedly composed herself, lowered her head to pretend to adjust her skirt, and didn't dare to glance in that direction again, hoping only to shrink into a shadow and remain unnoticed.

Grand Secretary Xu, being a perceptive man, laughed and patted Wei Songjun’s shoulder pointedly: "Since you’re here, don't leave empty-handed."

Everyone present understood. It was clear that Grand Secretary Xu hoped Wei Songjun would find a romantic connection at the gathering, and the only person who could bring this cold-faced Prince here today was surely the renowned first talented woman of the Great Qi, Mu Wanzhou, who had yet to make her appearance.

Wei Songjun took a sip of tea, his tone unreadable: "Then I shall take your auspicious words, Teacher."

His tacit agreement sparked another round of whispers among the crowd, though this time with more envy and resignation.

"If I had known Prince Jingnan would be here, I wouldn't have spent three hundred gold pieces on this invitation! Isn't it obvious there’s no chance now?" a pale-faced young man muttered with a bitter expression. Three hundred taels was no small sum; he had hoped to make a name for himself, but with the Prince here, all the spotlight would surely be stolen.

Someone next to him scoffed: "You’re good at counting—even if the Prince didn't come, did you think you’d catch Miss Mu’s eye? Seeing Miss Mu’s divine beauty and talent with your own eyes for three hundred taels is already a bargain!"

"That’s true... I heard Miss Mu is not only talented in poetry but also breathtakingly beautiful. Finally, I’ll get to see her today."

Cui Mingyu gasped in disbelief. Three hundred taels? The invitations for male guests had been bid up to that price? She sighed subconsciously, calculating—if she had known Wei Songjun would come, would the female guest invitations have been bid up to astronomical prices too? If so, she could have resold hers for a profit and wouldn't be sitting here on pins and needles.

"Why are you sighing?" A crisp voice came from beside her. Princess Chaogui leaned over, holding a bowl of almond curd, her eyes curved into crescents as she looked at her.

Cui Mingyu clutched her chest, her face full of heartache: "I was thinking, if I had known Prince Jingnan would come, the female guest invitations might have sold for a fortune. If I had sold mine, I could have made a killing."

Chaogui curled her lip, glanced at Wei Songjun not far away, and said with disdain: "Him? A pretty face... but a useless embroidered pillow, and a cold-faced block of ice at that. Besides you, who would pay a high price just to see him? Not worth it!"

Cui Mingyu’s face fell instantly. Her sigh deepened, and she wished she could reach out and cover Chaogui’s mouth. She lowered her voice urgently: "Princess! You promised not to bring that up again!"

Chaogui said "Oh," and quickly added, "I won't say it, I won't! I just couldn't help myself!" But she couldn't resist looking at Wei Songjun again, sighing with a frown, "Honestly, Mingyu, look at him, he’s so handsome, why is he... it’s such a waste of that face, a total squandering of heaven’s gifts!"

"Princess!" Cui Mingyu rolled her eyes so hard they nearly disappeared. She gritted her teeth and whispered, "You really misunderstood. He is very capable—extremely capable! Please, I beg you, don't mention it again. If this keeps up, I’ll be crushed into dust by him sooner or later!"

Chaogui was taken aback by her agitation and stared at her blankly for a long time. Cui Mingyu thought she had finally gotten through to her and was about to breathe a sigh of relief, but then she saw a mischievous glint in Chaogui’s eyes. The Princess leaned into her ear and whispered: "Did you... try it out that day?"

"Pfft—" Cui Mingyu nearly spat out a mouthful of blood, her head throbbing. This matter was only getting darker the more she tried to explain it; she wouldn't be able to clear her name even with a hundred mouths! She grabbed Chaogui’s wrist, pleading with a bitter face: "Princess, I beg you! If you still want me to keep this little life of mine to accompany you for a few more years, please, in your great mercy and magnanimity, forget about this, okay?"

Seeing that Cui Mingyu was truly panicked, Chaogui dropped the teasing and nodded seriously: "Fine, I won't say it."

Cui Mingyu finally relaxed and took a sip of tea to calm her nerves. But before she could settle down, Chaogui spoke again, her tone playful: "Hey, Mingyu, Wei Songjun is looking at us."

"Huh?" Cui Mingyu’s heart tightened, and she looked up instinctively. Sure enough, Wei Songjun was staring at them with a heavy gaze. There was no emotion in those deep eyes, yet it made her inexplicably flustered. She was just about to pull Chaogui away when she saw the Princess grinning at Wei Songjun, a smirk on her face that was so mischievous it was practically blinding.

It’s over! Cui Mingyu’s heart sank to the bottom. Wei Songjun was the most vengeful person; he must think she was bad-mouthing him behind his back again! After being tormented by him until she was half-dead last time, she had finally managed to stay out of trouble for a few days, but now she was surely going to fall back into his clutches.

In a moment of desperation, Cui Mingyu reached out, grabbed the dish of candied fruit from the table, pinched a piece of osmanthus candy, and shoved it into Chaogui’s mouth, forcibly stifling her laughter and masking the insufferable expression on her face. "Princess, try this. It’s very sweet." She dared not look toward Wei Songjun again, praying silently that he wouldn't overthink things and, above all, wouldn't set his sights on her miserable life.

Wei Songjun watched that flustered, busy figure. A faint, sharp glint flashed in his eyes, and the corners of his mouth lifted imperceptibly. Xie Changchuan, sitting to the side, saw him staring intently at the Cui family miss and curiously followed his gaze. He couldn't help but stroke his chin, pondering to himself: Cui Mingyu is quite different today compared to the past. In the old days, she could never sit still; she would have been hovering around the Prince of Jingnan long ago. Come to think of it, this Prince of Jingnan is acting strange too—why is he staring in Cui Mingyu’s direction? When has he ever paid her any mind before?

chapters.title: First Kiss
chapters.content:
Seeing that Chaogui had finally stopped harping on the matter, Cui Mingyu dared to let out a soft sigh of relief.

But before that breath could fully escape, a voice as gentle as spring water drifted from her side, with just the right amount of lightness. It didn't startle anyone else, but it tugged at Cui Mingyu’s heartstrings.

"Greetings, Miss Cui."

Cui Mingyu looked up at the sound, and when her gaze collided with a pair of smiling almond eyes, she froze in place. The person standing there was Xia Yuning. Since she had been bedridden with a cold, they hadn't met, yet her courtyard had never been without his tokens of affection—rock sugar stewed pears kept warm in a clay pot, sweet but not cloying; ocarinas that could whistle a crisp tune; or clay figurines of all shapes and sizes... None of these things were particularly valuable, yet like fine snow melting into spring, they had quietly seeped into her dull days, bringing her warmth even in her illness.

While she was dazed, Xia Yuning stepped closer. Today, he wore a dark blue brocade robe with subtle patterns, embroidered with fine silver thread in a cloud motif that shimmered as he moved—not flashy, but refined. His ink-black hair was half-tied with a warm white jade hairpin, and a few stray locks brushed against his cheeks, making his already fair face appear even more luminous, like fine mutton-fat jade with a delicate luster. Looking at the perfect touch of baby fat on his cheeks, Cui Mingyu suddenly remembered the New Year’s dolls she had seen as a child—if one were to add a dot of cinnabar to his brow, he could be pasted right on a door to bring good luck for the whole year. As this thought emerged, she couldn't help but curl her lips, a hint of irrepressible amusement flashing in her eyes, which eased her earlier awkwardness.

"Greetings, Young Master Xia." She quickly gathered her thoughts, nodded softly, and spoke with a newfound gentleness—she didn't know why, but under his gentle gaze, she felt as if even her breathing had slowed by half a beat.

Seeing her response, the smile on Xia Yuning’s face deepened instantly. His warm eyes seemed to hold a sky full of starlight, shining brilliantly. "You have finally recovered." His voice held undisguised joy—ever since his last failed attempt to visit, once he received word that she would be joining him to view the lotus flowers, he had worried that visiting would disturb her rest. He could only spend his days pondering what gifts might please her, hoping she would get well soon. Seeing her standing in the warm sun now, with a rosy complexion and clear eyes, the heart that had been hanging in his chest finally settled.

Hearing the genuine concern in his voice, Cui Mingyu felt a warmth in her heart and quickly said, "It is all thanks to your blessings, Young Master Xia. With all the tonics you sent, I was able to recover so quickly."

"Don't say that." Upon hearing this, the blush on Xia Yuning’s cheeks deepened, and he looked quite shy. He subconsciously scratched his temple, looking a bit embarrassed. "I was already happy enough that you accepted those things." As soon as he finished speaking, as if remembering something, he stepped forward and pulled an exquisite gold-traced box from his wide sleeve. When he opened it, a fresh, sweet fragrance wafted out, instantly lingering at the tip of her nose and making the very air feel sweet. "Wufangzhai released some new crystal dragon-phoenix cakes today. I thought you might like them, so I brought some for you to try."

Cui Mingyu stared at the box held out before her, stunned once again. The image of the New Year’s doll hadn't yet faded, and now, watching him pull things from his sleeve like a magician—he wasn't a New Year’s doll at all; he was clearly Doraemon. The man before her stood tall and straight in the warm spring sun, his sleeves fluttering, a picture of elegance, yet this sudden gesture added a touch of endearing, clumsy charm.

"How much longer are you going to dawdle? There are so many eyes watching." Princess Chaogui, beside her, had lost her earlier petulance and was now propping her chin on her hand to watch the show. Seeing Cui Mingyu standing there blankly, she couldn't help but tap her knee, her tone teasing. She had previously thought Xia Yuning was chubby and uninteresting, but seeing the cautious way he offered the cakes, she found this little fatty more agreeable—at least he was better than those young masters who only knew how to put on airs and spout grand principles; he actually knew how to cherish someone.

Reminded by Chaogui’s words, Cui Mingyu suddenly became aware of the surrounding gazes. She subconsciously scanned the area; indeed, many people were peeking their way. Her cheeks grew hot, and she quickly reached out to take the gold-traced box. "That... thank you, Young Master Xia. I shall accept them, then."

The moment she finished speaking, a collective gasp rippled through the crowd. In their eyes, Cui Mingyu had always chased after Wei Songjun, who had never given her the time of day, while Xia Yuning’s feelings for her were no secret—he had been sending gifts for so long, and she had never once looked at him properly. Yet today, in front of everyone, she had personally accepted cakes from Xia Yuning and even offered a shy, sweet smile.

Xie Changchuan, sitting nearby, nearly dropped his teacup. He looked at Wei Songjun beside him in disbelief: "She... how did she accept them?" This Cui Mingyu, why had she suddenly changed her nature? Wasn't she a loyal devotee of the Prince of Jingnan?

Xia Yuning clearly hadn't expected Cui Mingyu to accept so quickly. He held his empty hand, the flush on his face spreading to his ears. His warm eyes were brilliantly bright as he stared fixedly at Cui Mingyu, the emotions in his gaze no longer hidden, surging toward her like a rising tide—a long-held joy, concern, and expectation, so intense that Cui Mingyu dared not meet his eyes.

Wei Songjun was leisurely holding his teacup, his expression so indifferent it was as if everything around him had nothing to do with him. But upon hearing Xie Changchuan’s words, he slowly raised his eyes, his gaze crossing the crowd to land on Cui Mingyu.

At this moment, she was looking down, her cheeks flushed with a faint red, like a half-bloomed peach blossom, filled with shyness and softness. That look was completely different from how she was in front of him; that shameless, brazen demeanor was nowhere to be found!

Watching her acting so well-behaved, a surge of inexplicable irritation rose in Wei Songjun’s heart. He let out a cold snort, a hint of mockery flashing in his eyes. He remembered that day at the Prince of Jingnan’s estate, when she had taken the medicine and actually clamored to find Xia Yuning—they had likely already finished things between them.

He suppressed the disgust rising in his heart and shifted his gaze, squeezing the teacup hard with his fingertips until his knuckles turned white. What this woman did, what did it have to do with him? As long as she stopped hovering around him like before, stopped jumping about in front of him, and stopped using those clumsy tricks to provoke him, he could pretend he had never known this person. They would be even, with no further ties.

But was it truly wiped clean?

Wei Songjun’s fingertips, holding the cup, inadvertently brushed against the corner of his lips. The sensation seemed to retain a lingering, burning warmth.

That day, she had drugged him. She had seen his well-defined chest, and even more, when his consciousness was clouded, she had kissed his lips.

Damn it.

Wei Songjun’s fingertips tightened abruptly, and the teacup emitted a faint cracking sound as several fissures spread along the rim.

That was his first kiss.

He had lived for twenty-five years, never having such intimate contact with a woman, strictly upholding propriety and keeping himself pure, only to be wantonly teased by her, his very dignity torn to shreds.

He looked up at Cui Mingyu again, the mockery in his eyes replaced by darkness, his breathing becoming heavy. That woman... she had clearly taken advantage of him, yet turned around to smile like a flower at Xia Yuning.

Violence churned in his eyes. If he had known, he shouldn't have been soft-hearted that day at the Ningguo Duke’s estate; he should have finished her off on the spot!

And what was wrong with him, anyway, to come to this godforsaken poetry gathering?!

chapters.title: A Youth’s Affection
chapters.content:
Suddenly, a commotion erupted in the crowd, and the noisy chatter was abruptly suppressed. Then, a loud, gravelly voice cut through the courtyard: "The daughter of the Prime Minister’s residence, Miss Mu Wanzhou, has arrived—!"

This announcement was like a boulder thrown into a lake, instantly stirring up a thousand waves. The male guests who had been sitting calmly rose in unison, as if rehearsed, each stretching their necks and gazing toward the gate with burning anticipation and curiosity. After all, Mu Wanzhou’s fame for talent was widespread, and rumors claimed her beauty was peerless; she rarely appeared at ordinary banquets, and no one wanted to miss the chance to see her true face today.

Princess Chaogui, lounging lazily on a cushioned bench, raised an eyebrow at the news. A playful, mocking curve touched her lips, and her tone was full of disdain: "What a grand entrance."

Cui Mingyu followed the crowd’s gaze and saw a slender figure walking slowly from the gate. The woman wore a moon-white soft silk dress, with a belt of translucent mutton-fat jade cinched at her waist, accentuating her slender frame. The hem of her skirt was embroidered with sparse orchid grass in silver thread, swaying gently with her steps like fireflies under the moon. Her posture was graceful, her gait light, and her robes fluttered as she walked, like a fairy stepping down from the clouds.

As she drew closer, Cui Mingyu finally saw her face—eyebrows like distant mountains, eyes like rippling autumn waters, a delicate nose, and lips like cherry petals. Her skin was so fair it was almost transparent, and paired with that white dress, she truly deserved the description "eyebrows and eyes like a painting." Such beauty and talent were indeed worthy of Wei Songjun. Cui Mingyu thought to herself, subconsciously glancing at Wei Songjun. Sure enough, his gaze was locked on Mu Wanzhou, his eyes filled with undisguised amazement and appreciation, even his usually indifferent expression softening.

"Oh ho, the hero and heroine have caught each other’s eyes," Cui Mingyu chuckled to herself, unable to stop her lips from curling. As long as she avoided these melodramatic plots and lived her own quiet little life, Wei Songjun shouldn't have time to bother with her anymore!

"What, are you stunned?" Beside her, Chaogui looked at her with a side-eye. Cui Mingyu came back to her senses to find Chaogui looking at her with a smirk.

She quickly withdrew her gaze, turned her head, and grinned at Chaogui: "If you were to dress up in your finest today, Princess, you would surely be a hundred times more beautiful than her." This was no empty flattery; as a princess, Chaogui naturally possessed an air of noble elegance, her brows and eyes holding a mix of heroic spirit and charming innocence. If she were to dress with care, she would indeed be no less impressive than Mu Wanzhou.

Chaogui picked up the teacup before her and took a slow, deliberate sip. The tea was clear and crisp, yet it could not suppress the pride in her eyes: "Why should I compare myself to her?"

Cui Mingyu thought that was true. Chaogui was of royal blood, having lived in luxury since childhood with an incomparably noble status. No matter how good Mu Wanzhou was, she was merely the daughter of a court official. The two were simply not on the same level, so there was no need to compete. She gave a sheepish smile and changed the subject: "Since Miss Mu has arrived, according to the usual rules of the banquet, will there be a poetry competition later?"

Chaogui glanced at her, a hint of mischief in her eyes: "What? Are you scared?"

A look of embarrassment immediately appeared on Cui Mingyu's face. The original owner's poetry skills were truly mediocre, only slightly better than the average noblewoman, and certainly not fit for refined company. Although she came from the modern era and remembered a few poems, she found that when it came time to use them, she felt woefully inadequate. If she really had to recite one, she feared she would only make a fool of herself.

She gave a dry laugh and gestured to the surroundings: "There are too many people here, it’s a bit stuffy. I want to go out for some fresh air. Would you like to come, Princess?"

Chaogui scoffed and waved her hand: "Look at you, so spineless. Go on then. I’ll stay here and watch this good show; I want to see what kind of astonishing masterpiece our great talented lady Mu can come up with today."

As if granted an amnesty, Cui Mingyu quickly bowed: "Then this subject's daughter will take her leave." With that, her gaze swept quickly over the snack plates on the table. Seeing that the plate of Crystal Dragon and Phoenix Cakes that Xia Yuning had just sent over was still there, she casually picked one up, carefully tucked it into her sleeve pocket, and then tiptoed out of the banquet hall.

The Xu residence was vast. Deep in the back garden was a pavilion by the water, surrounded by lush greenery and very secluded. Cui Mingyu walked along the bluestone path, leaving behind the noise of the front hall, and felt that even the air was much fresher.

She entered the pavilion, sat on a stone stool, and carefully took out the Crystal Dragon and Phoenix Cake from her sleeve. The pastry was made with extreme delicacy; the outer layer was a crystal-clear sugar coating through which one could faintly see the pink and white cake body inside, dotted with finely chopped preserved fruit. It looked very appealing. "I didn't expect ancient snacks to be made so exquisitely," Cui Mingyu marveled, unable to resist leaning in to sniff it. A fresh, sweet fragrance wafted up, instantly making her mouth water.

She took a small bite. The soft, glutinous cake melted on her tongue, sweet but not cloying, with a faint fruity aroma and a delicate, soft texture. It was so delicious that her eyes lit up. She finished the pastry in a few bites and licked her lips, still wanting more.

"Miss Cui—"

A gentle, warm male voice suddenly came from behind her, like a warm breeze in spring, brushing softly against her ears.

Cui Mingyu stiffened in shock, the cake crumbs she hadn't yet swallowed almost choking her. She turned around, still shaken, and upon seeing who it was, a somewhat awkward smile appeared on her face: "Young Master... Young Master Xia?"

At this moment, the corners of her mouth were still stained with a few white cake crumbs, her cheeks were slightly flushed from the recent fright, and her eyes held a trace of panic. She looked exactly like a cat caught stealing food, appearing unexpectedly charming and innocent.

Xia Yuning stood at the entrance of the pavilion. Seeing Cui Mingyu in this state, a flicker of amusement flashed across his eyes. He took a step forward, his gaze falling on the crumbs at the corner of her mouth, and he reached out instinctively.

Cui Mingyu was stunned when she saw him reach toward her face, then suddenly realized she might have something on her mouth, and her cheeks burned instantly. Just as she was about to raise her hand to wipe it off herself, she felt Xia Yuning’s fingertips gently brush the corner of her mouth.

His fingertips had a cool temperature, and the touch was light and soft, like a feather brushing past, bringing an indescribable tingling sensation that instantly spread through Cui Mingyu's entire body.

"!!!" Cui Mingyu’s heart skipped a beat, then began to pound like a drum. Her cheeks were so hot they could have boiled an egg. She stood rigid, forgetting even to breathe, and could only stare at Xia Yuning’s handsome face so close to her, feeling the touch of his fingertips. Her mind went blank, leaving only one thought: *I'm done for, I'm done for, how can this man be so gentle!*

Xia Yuning clearly realized his action had been a bit abrupt. Under the gaze of Cui Mingyu’s watery almond eyes, a faint red glow quickly rose on his fair cheeks, as if stained with rouge, and even his earlobes turned bright red. He quickly withdrew his hand and bowed, somewhat flustered: "Miss Cui, I'm sorry, I was abrupt and offended you."

After saying this, he instinctively looked at his own fingertips, as if the sensation still lingered, and his face turned even redder.

*He's a handsome guy who blushes easily. It's hard to believe he's a businessman; how does he negotiate with others like this?* Watching him, the panic in Cui Mingyu’s heart gradually faded, replaced by an inexplicable flutter. She quickly turned around, facing away from Xia Yuning to hide her burning cheeks, her voice as thin as a mosquito's: "It... it's fine. That... the cake you sent was delicious, thank you."

Hearing this, the embarrassment in Xia Yuning’s eyes gradually dissipated, replaced by a look of warm, gentle joy. He looked at Cui Mingyu’s petite back, his voice so soft it could melt: "I'm glad you liked it. If you don't mind, I can have some sent to the Cui residence every day, would that be alright?"

"Huh?" Cui Mingyu turned back, looking at him in surprise, then couldn't help but laugh, "Young Master Xia, you're joking. No matter how delicious a pastry is, one would get tired of it if they ate it every day."

Xia Yuning, however, looked serious, his eyes burning as he looked at her, his tone extremely solemn: "Then... I shall send them until you no longer wish to eat them."

His gaze was clear and sincere, carrying undisguised tenderness, which made Cui Mingyu’s heart beat even faster. This man was honestly quite adorable.

She lowered her eyes, her fingers twisting the hem of her skirt. After hesitating for a moment, she finally looked up and gathered the courage to ask: "Young Master Xia, my reputation is poor, and my temper is willful and capricious. Why... why do you fancy me?"

This question had been bottled up in her heart for a long time. After all, the original owner's reputation in the capital was indeed not good; her infatuation with Wei Songjun was known to everyone, and her personality was arrogant and domineering. There was really nothing about her worth falling for.

When Xia Yuning heard this question, the smile on his face paused slightly, and his eyes drifted into the distance, as if lost in memory. After a moment, he spoke slowly, his voice carrying a sense of distance: "Miss Cui may not remember, but we met when we were children."

Cui Mingyu was stunned and quickly searched through the original owner's memories. In those memories, things from childhood were mostly blurry; she only remembered playing with other noble children, but there were no fragments related to Xia Yuning at all.

"That day, I accompanied my father to a banquet. I was bullied by a few older noble children who snatched my jade pendant and pushed me behind the rockery." Xia Yuning’s voice deepened, carrying a hint of imperceptible grievance, "It was you, Miss Cui, who happened to pass by. You stood up for me, blocked them, scolded them sternly, and even helped me get my jade pendant back."

He turned his head, his gaze falling gently on Cui Mingyu’s face, his eyes full of gratitude and cherishment: "You were just a tiny thing back then, but you were like a little tiger with its fur standing on end. Even though you were clearly scared yourself, you still protected me. I have kept that kindness in my heart and have never forgotten it."

Cui Mingyu was completely stunned. She searched through the original owner's memories over and over again, but still had no impression of it. So, behind this affection, there was a past she hadn't known about.

She looked at Xia Yuning’s sincere eyes, her heart filled with mixed emotions, and couldn't help but ask softly: "But... but that was just a small act of kindness in childhood. How could it support you until now, and... and make you fall for me?"

Hearing this, a gentle smile appeared on Xia Yuning’s face, like a spring breeze: "To you, it may have been a small kindness, but to me, who was helpless at the time, it was a ray of light in the darkness. Later, I often paid attention to you, watching you be frank and willful, watching you dare to love and hate. Even when the world misunderstood you, you never pretended to be someone else. Such a vivid you, before I knew it, made me lose my heart."

His voice was not loud, but every word was clear, carrying heavy affection. It flowed slowly in the quiet pavilion, crashing into the bottom of Cui Mingyu’s heart and creating ripples.

The feelings of a youth are the purest and most moving.

chapters.title: Passing the Flower to the Beat of a Drum
chapters.content:
Cui Mingyu took a deep breath, her heart still beating somewhat out of rhythm. Looking at the man standing opposite her, she said in a clear voice, "My temper is just like this—I'm stubborn, I love to argue, and I'm narrow-minded. No matter how many times others have tried to persuade me, I can't change—a leopard cannot change its spots. Young Master Xia, can you really accept that?"

Xia Yuning stood under the veranda, his eyes filled with an unmelting tenderness. He looked at the thorny yet vibrant rose before him, his tone one of long-settled seriousness, without a hint of perfunctoriness: "Miss Cui, my feelings for you are not a fleeting impulse of spring, but a conviction accumulated over time. My understanding of you does not stop at a fleeting glance at a banquet; the stubbornness in your bones and the sincerity with which you treat others—I have seen it all and kept it in my heart."

Cui Mingyu’s eyelashes trembled, as if she hadn't expected him to be so frank. She bit her lip and decided to be even clearer: "You may not know me well enough yet. What I seek has never been the bustle of a house full of concubines, but a lifetime with one person. My future husband can only have one wife—me. The thought of taking concubines in the household, let alone having maids or mistresses on the side, is out of the question. This is my bottom line, and I will never compromise."

Hearing the words "husband," Xia Yuning’s eyes suddenly lit up, as if a spark had been ignited in the dark night. His Adam's apple bobbed, and he couldn't hide his excitement: "Miss Cui, if I could marry the girl I love, I, Xia Yuning, would only acknowledge her as my wife for the rest of my life. There will never be a place for a second woman in my household. On this, I swear upon my life."

His gaze was too intense, like light carrying warmth, falling straight onto her face, burning Cui Mingyu’s cheeks until they turned a faint red, and even her earlobes grew hot. She resisted the urge to look away and, meeting his sincere gaze, said softly: "I am willing to believe in your heart, and I am willing to accept your feelings. However... human hearts are fickle, and the world is unpredictable. Why don't we try to get to know each other for a year? If, after a year, your feelings for me remain unchanged, then you and I... perhaps we can take a step further."

"Really?" Xia Yuning was overjoyed, the ecstasy in his heart nearly overflowing. He reached out impulsively and gripped Cui Mingyu’s hands tightly. Her fingertips were cool and delicate to the touch, making his heart tremble; he found himself reluctant to let go.

Cui Mingyu was startled by his sudden action, her cheeks flushing even deeper. She gently pulled back, reminding him with a hint of shyness in her voice: "Xia... Master Xia."

Xia Yuning snapped back to reality, realizing he had been impolite. He quickly released her hands, a flash of panic crossing his eyes, which were slightly reddened. With a mix of apology and irrepressible joy, he said, "I... I’m sorry. I was just so happy that I lost my composure. I didn’t expect that you would truly be willing to give me a chance. Miss... Miss Cui, may I call you Mingyu?"

Cui Mingyu looked at the anticipation in his eyes—he looked so endearingly earnest—and her heart softened. She gave a gentle nod.

A brilliant smile instantly bloomed on Xia Yuning’s face, like parched vegetation meeting a sweet rain; his entire being seemed to come alive. Unable to suppress his excitement, his voice turned much lighter: "Mingyu... then... you may call me Yuning as well."

"Yu... ning." Cui Mingyu parted her lips softly. The two characters felt not at all awkward on her tongue, but rather warm and natural, as if she had spoken them a thousand times before. No sooner had she finished than she saw Xia Yuning’s smile deepen, the tenderness in his eyes nearly spilling over.

Xia Yuning gazed at her flushed cheeks, his thoughts turning, and he suggested softly, "Mingyu, the lotus flowers at Yancui Lake have bloomed, and the scenery is magnificent. Since you were feeling under the weather recently and have now recovered, how about we go to the lake to admire the lotuses together in three days?"

She had already agreed to this invitation in her heart. With a smile crinkling her eyes, she nodded: "That sounds lovely. I was just thinking of going to see the scenery by the lake."

Xia Yuning beamed, his brows relaxing, and he instructed carefully, "Then I shall come to pick you up at the hour of the Snake (9–11 AM) in three days. No need to wake up too early; get plenty of rest and keep your spirits up."

Cui Mingyu nodded obediently: "Okay." She looked up at the sky; the sun was nearly at its zenith. Remembering that the poetry gathering was about to begin when she left, she asked, "By the way, are you not going to attend the poetry gathering? I heard someone say earlier that there is a collaborative poetry segment coming up."

Xia Yuning smiled, his tone quite frank: "I didn't come for the poetry gathering in the first place. I only came because I heard you would be attending."

Cui Mingyu felt a stir in her heart, as if something had gently bumped against it. She suddenly remembered something and asked with wide eyes, "That invitation of yours... it didn't cost you any money, did it? I heard that the invitations for this gathering are exceptionally hard to come by, and many people have been fighting tooth and nail for one."

Xia Yuning shook his head, his tone somewhat nonchalant: "Someone was actually willing to pay two hundred taels to buy it from me, but I didn't agree."

"Tsk tsk, two hundred taels." Cui Mingyu clicked her tongue, calculating in her mind. If she had known he came to this gathering just to see her, she would have rather he sold the invitation to get some money for practical use, and they could have just met at a teahouse to talk—wouldn't that have been more comfortable?

She couldn't help but tease, "Then wouldn't you say you lost out big time on this poetry gathering?"

Xia Yuning shook his head: "Not coming would have been the real loss. If I had missed today, I fear I would have regretted it for the rest of my life. The gathering is full of talent, with both renowned scholars of great learning and elegant young gentlemen. I was always worried that someone would steal your attention and make you unable to see me. Fortunately..." He paused, his gaze resting on her face again, full of relief and appreciation, "Fortunately, you are willing to give me a chance."

Seeing him belittle himself so, Cui Mingyu couldn't help but comfort him: "You don't need to put yourself down like that. You have a talent for business and are humble with others; my father often praises you in front of me."

Xia Yuning was stunned, his face full of surprise: "Lord Cui... actually praises me? Although I have met Lord Cui a few times, we have never spoken at length. I wonder how the old gentleman evaluates me?"

Seeing his curious expression, Cui Mingyu couldn't help but smile radiantly, a trace of mischief flashing in her eyes: "Want to know? Then you'll have to ask him yourself."

Hearing this, a glimmer of anticipation flashed in Xia Yuning’s eyes, and he nodded quickly: "Very well, I shall certainly pay a visit another day to seek Lord Cui’s counsel."

Cui Mingyu estimated that the time was about right, so she said to Xia Yuning, "The poetry gathering should be drawing to a close. Shall we go back and take a look?"

Xia Yuning had always been compliant with her wishes and nodded immediately: "Very well, as you say."

The two walked one after the other along the corridor toward the main venue of the poetry gathering. The courtyard was bustling with activity, the sound of drums echoing—it was a game of "passing the flower to the beat of the drum." The drumbeats grew faster and faster, carrying a tense rhythm that made everyone hold their breath.

Cui Mingyu didn't want to draw too much attention to herself, so she tried to tiptoe back to her seat, hoping to remain unnoticed. But just then, the rapid drumming came to an abrupt "thump" and stopped!

A flower ball embroidered with pink and white lotuses seemed to have eyes; it landed squarely in her arms.

Cui Mingyu looked down at the flower ball in her arms, her mouth twitching. She couldn't help but curse inwardly: *Damn, what kind of heaven-defying luck is this?*

The expression on her face collapsed instantly, looking exactly like a miserable squash. Facing the gazes of the entire courtyard, she managed to squeeze out a dry, awkward smile: "Whose ball is this? Why are you throwing it around?!"

As soon as she finished speaking, the entire venue erupted into boisterous laughter, and even the previously tense atmosphere became cheerful.

chapters.title: Stunning
chapters.content:
The sunlight, infused with the golden glow of dusk, poured into the Xu family courtyard, casting a hazy veil over the fragrant, silken-clad crowd. Wei Songjun leaned against a purple sandalwood chair, idly stroking the rim of his celadon cup, his gaze, however, cold as a frozen pool, locked onto that abruptly appearing figure.

Cui Mingyu stood in the center of the crowd, clutching the flower ball embroidered with entwined lotus vines, as if she had been pushed onto the stage when caught off guard.

A cold, sharp arc tugged at the corners of Wei Songjun’s mouth. When the poetry gathering began, he had noticed the girl slipping out. At the time, he assumed she simply couldn't endure the dullness of the banquet, but now it seemed she had somewhere else to be. His peripheral vision swept over the courtyard entrance without a trace; Xia Yuning was walking in slowly.

The two of them, one after the other, arriving at such a coincidental moment—if this wasn't a secret meeting, what was it?

A chill spread from the depths of Wei Songjun’s eyes, nearly freezing the celadon cup in his hand. He wanted to see how this audacious girl, now struck by the flower ball, would manage to get through this ordeal unscathed.

The noise in the warm pavilion had long since ceased, and everyone’s eyes were focused on Cui Mingyu. The sudden stop of the drumbeat during the game had left the flower ball in her hands just as she entered, and this turn of events silenced the lively scene instantly, with many wearing expressions of anticipation for a good show.

Xia Yuning spotted the flower ball in Cui Mingyu’s arms and her slightly embarrassed expression, and he understood immediately. He subconsciously took two steps forward, wanting to help her out—after all, Cui Mingyu’s literary foundation was well-known to those in the capital who had heard even a little bit about her; how could she possibly handle the test of such an occasion?

But just as he moved, he saw Cui Mingyu shake her head slightly. Xia Yuning froze in his tracks; though still worried, he suppressed the urge to step forward, watching her with eyes full of tension.

At this moment, a servant had already quietly approached Elder Xu, whispering to explain Cui Mingyu’s identity. Elder Xu stroked his graying beard, a gentle smile spreading across his face, and said in a clear voice: "Miss Cui, I held this banquet today to allow all the young masters and ladies to enjoy a refined gathering, and the game we are playing is one of poetry and literature. Now that the drum has stopped, a servant shall draw a slip from this bamboo tube, and you need only compose a line of poetry according to the requirement on the slip."

Cui Mingyu breathed a sigh of relief inwardly. It was just a line of poetry; it shouldn't be too hard. She was a person who had undergone nine years of compulsory education in the modern era. While she couldn't recite the *Three Hundred Tang Poems* backward, reciting one or two off the cuff wasn't a problem. Thinking this, the panic on her face gradually faded, and she nodded calmly: "So that is how it is. Thank you for informing me, Elder. Please, set the topic."

A maid nearby immediately stepped forward with the carved bamboo tube. A servant drew a slip at random in front of everyone and handed it to Elder Xu. Elder Xu unfolded the slip and read: "Compose a line of poetry with 'wine' as the topic, but the word 'wine' must not appear in the line."

As soon as he finished, a few low, stifled laughs echoed in the warm pavilion. The topic seemed simple, but it was actually a test of true skill. One had to capture the essence and mood of wine without stating it directly, requiring one to borrow scenery to express emotion and take a winding path to the destination. For the talented scholars and ladies who had been immersed in literature for years, it might not be difficult, but Cui Mingyu? Everyone recalled her usual spoiled nature and felt the topic was intentionally meant to embarrass her.

Women rarely had contact with wine, let alone compose poetry about it. Many had already turned away, unable to bear watching her make a fool of herself in public, while some busybodies had already begun to whisper, their words filled with mockery.

The color drained from Cui Mingyu’s face. A topic about wine without saying "wine"? This ancient poetry game was too devious! She racked her brains, but all that flashed through her mind were lines like "Raising a cup to invite the bright moon" or "Asking the blue sky with wine in hand," all of which contained the word "wine" and didn't meet the requirements at all. Just as she was sweating with anxiety, a voice as crisp as an oriole leaving the valley suddenly rang out: "You old man are being quite unreasonable! Could it be that there is no good wine at your banquet, so you have to use 'wine' to annoy people?"

Everyone looked toward the sound and saw Princess Chao Gui standing up from her seat. Clad in white, she looked ethereal and stunning, though her brow was furrowed with indignation. She walked a few steps to Cui Mingyu’s side, shielding her as if protecting her young, and questioned Elder Xu: "You have separated the male and female guests at this banquet, so why, when setting the topic, did you not distinguish between men and women? Men often gather together to drink and compose poetry, so it is naturally second nature to them. Women, however, mostly stay in their chambers; how would they be so familiar with 'wine'?"

Elder Xu’s face turned bright red instantly. He had once been the teacher of the late Emperor and had always been respected in the court; when had he ever been confronted like this to his face? Moreover, the person was a princess of royal blood. He could neither refute her nor step down, so he could only smile awkwardly, bow, and say: "It was indeed my lack of consideration. I have let the Princess see a joke."

"The Princess is mistaken." Another crisp, melodious voice came, with a hint of disapproval in its tone. Everyone looked over to see Mu Wanzhou slowly rising. She was dressed in a moon-white ru skirt, her temperament gentle and quiet. "From ancient times to the present, literary schools have been either graceful and delicate or bold and unrestrained, but there has never been a reason to distinguish superiority by gender. Men can write delicate verses, and women can also compose bold poetry. How can the Princess think that just because Miss Cui is a woman, she cannot handle this topic?"

Princess Chaogui didn't even look at her, continuing to address Elder Xu: "Old Man Xu, who here doesn't know the purpose of your poetry banquet? It’s merely a platform for these unmarried young men and women to socialize and foster a few good matches; it’s not as if you’re holding an imperial examination to rank scholars. You didn't set a theme at the start, opting instead for drawing lots, which was meant to accommodate everyone's circumstances and allow them to showcase their individual talents—there was certainly no reason to make things difficult for others. Why did the topic become so devious when it came to Mingyu?"

After saying this, she turned her gaze toward Mu Wanzhou, her eyes sharpening slightly: "Miss Mu is hailed as the greatest talented woman in the Great Qi. I do not know who bestowed this title upon you, but judging by your performance just now, your scholarship is indeed well-deserved. However, as the old saying goes, everyone has their strengths and weaknesses. To use your own strengths as a yardstick for all other women is, to say the least, quite biased."

Mu Wanzhou’s cheeks flushed slightly, and she was left momentarily speechless by Princess Chaogui’s words. She had not intended to target Cui Mingyu; she simply held poetry in high regard and, seeing Princess Chaogui being so "unreasonable," could not help but retort, never expecting to be questioned in such a manner.

Princess Chaogui ignored her further, turning instead to Cui Mingyu. She cast a meaningful glance at Xia Yuning not far away and said softly, "Mingyu, I trust your original intention for attending this banquet has been met. If there is nothing else, let us leave together, so as to avoid being slighted by others here."

A surge of warmth welled up in Cui Mingyu’s heart. Princess Chaogui had only come to the banquet to keep her company, yet now she was willing to offend Elder Xu and Mu Wanzhou on her behalf. This gesture moved her deeply. She could not let the Princess stand up for her in vain, nor could she allow others to look down upon her.

She gently disengaged from Princess Chaogui’s hand, stepped forward, and offered a faint smile to Mu Wanzhou: "Miss Mu, the Princess meant no offense. It is just that I happened to be walking by when the floral ball fell into my hands, and I happened to draw a topic I am not skilled in—it was truly too much of a coincidence. The Princess only spoke up to defend me; she meant no disrespect."

As she spoke, a glimmer of cunning flashed in her eyes, and her tone shifted: "However, what is even more coincidental is that I have been idle these past few days and have practiced quite diligently. I happened to learn a line of poetry that I think fits today’s topic perfectly, and I would be so bold as to share it with everyone."

The warm pavilion fell into absolute silence. Everyone held their breath, waiting to see what she could possibly come up with. Mu Wanzhou frowned slightly, clearly not believing she could compose a poem that fit the theme. Xia Yuning was filled with anticipation, his hands unconsciously gripping his sleeves. Meanwhile, Wei Songjun remained leaning in the corner, his gaze profound as he watched her, as if trying to see through her very thoughts.

Cui Mingyu cleared her throat and spoke slowly, her voice clear and melodious, carrying throughout the pavilion: "Draw a blade to sever the water, the water flows all the more; raise a cup to drown sorrow, the sorrow grows all the more."

As her voice faded, the entire room was stunned.

The pavilion was so quiet one could hear a pin drop. A moment later, a low murmur of amazement erupted. No one had expected that Cui Mingyu, who had always been considered inept at poetry, could produce such a masterpiece!

"Wonderful! Truly wonderful!" Elder Xu was the first to react, clapping his hands in admiration. "Using 'raising a cup' to subtly imply the wine, and borrowing the flowing water and idle sorrow to express one's inner feelings—the imagery is profound, the parallelism is precise, and it even carries a touch of philosophy. Miss Cui, what talent!"

The crowd chimed in, their gazes toward Cui Mingyu shifting from initial mockery and disdain to shock and admiration. Those who had been secretly laughing now wore expressions of shame, not daring to whisper anymore.

The flush on Mu Wanzhou’s face had long since faded, replaced by a deathly pallor. She stared at Cui Mingyu, her eyes filled with disbelief, which then transformed into deep respect. She straightened her collar and bowed solemnly to Cui Mingyu: "Miss Cui’s work is a masterpiece; I am ashamed to compare myself to you. My previous remarks were rash."

Princess Chaogui beamed, stepping forward to pat Cui Mingyu on the shoulder, her tone full of pride: "Cui Mingyu, you really know how to play the fool to catch the prey! I underestimated you before; I never expected you to have such talent!"

Xia Yuning stood where he was, looking at Cui Mingyu with joy. The admiration and relief in his eyes were almost overflowing, and he could not hide the smile on his lips. He had known all along that she was never the empty-headed girl others perceived her to be.

In the corner, Wei Songjun slowly withdrew the coldness from his eyes, replacing it with deep contemplation. He stared in Cui Mingyu’s direction, his deep black eyes churning with complex emotions.

Did she really write this poem?

Cui Mingyu, a sheltered young lady known for her reckless and willful nature—where did she find the courage to "draw a blade," or the sorrow to "drown" it? With her flighty and flamboyant personality, how could she compose such a philosophical and profound verse?

chapters.title: The Emperor
chapters.content:
As Cui Mingyu and Princess Chaogui sat back down under the gaze of the crowd, Cui Mingyu sighed, "Who is it that dislikes me so much that they deliberately dug a pit for me?"

Beside her, Princess Chaogui’s lips curled into a faint smile, though it did not reach her eyes, carrying instead a touch of indifferent coldness. Her voice was soft but every word was clear: "You should ask yourself, how many people here actually like you?"

The smile on Cui Mingyu’s face collapsed instantly, and she couldn't help but mutter to herself. The original owner might have been spoiled and overbearing, offending many people, but surely not to the point of being "universally despised," right? Subconsciously, she raised her eyes and swept her gaze across the crowd.

Just then, a gentle gaze came from the end of the room, landing steadily upon her. Cui Mingyu’s heart skipped a beat as her eyes met his—it was Xia Yuning. His eyes held a faint smile, and his gaze was as gentle as the spring sun, dispelling the embarrassment she had felt under the crowd's scrutiny.

Cui Mingyu’s tense lips softened involuntarily, and a hint of sweetness stirred in her heart. Her voice even became lighter as she whispered to Chaogui, "At least, he likes me."

Chaogui followed her gaze and immediately spotted Xia Yuning in the crowd. Seeing him still looking toward Cui Mingyu with an undiminished smile, she withdrew her gaze and looked at Cui Mingyu with a playful, enigmatic expression: "Oh? Did you two... just pour your hearts out to each other?"

Cui Mingyu’s cheeks burned slightly, but she did not deny it: "I told him that if his feelings for me haven't changed in a year, I will marry him."

The smile on Chaogui’s face gradually faded. She stared intently at Cui Mingyu, her peach-blossom eyes, usually so nonchalant, now unusually serious. "Mingyu, I find myself increasingly unable to read you," she said softly. "You were once so obsessed with Wei Songjun, pining for him to the point of losing your appetite, yet now you let go so decisively."

She paused, casting her gaze into the distance, her tone softening: "But that is for the best. By not clinging to people and things you cannot have, life will surely be much easier."

For some reason, as Cui Mingyu watched Chaogui’s slightly lowered lashes, she felt a trace of indescribable melancholy in her tone, as if she were speaking of Cui Mingyu, and yet also of herself. Just as Cui Mingyu was about to ask something, a flurry of hurried footsteps outside the courtyard broke the brief silence.

A servant dressed in the livery of the Xu household pushed through the crowd with a panicked expression, hurried to Elder Xu’s side at the main table, and whispered something into his ear. Elder Xu’s face, which had been smiling only moments before, turned deathly pale. He stood up abruptly, his teacup clattering to the floor. He didn't even notice the tea splashing onto his robes as he stammered, "The... the Emperor is here!"

"The Emperor is here?"

"How could the Emperor be disturbed?"

"Is this poetry banquet really such a grand affair?"

Elder Xu’s words were like a stone thrown into a calm pond, instantly stirring up a thousand ripples in the crowd. Everyone present was shocked, whispering to one another, their faces filled with disbelief. Although this poetry banquet was hosted by Elder Xu, it had always been a casual gathering of unmarried young men and women from noble families, at most attended by a few princes or aristocrats. But today, not only were Princess Chaogui and the Prince of Jingnan, Wei Songjun, present, along with the "Greatest Talented Woman of Great Qi," Mu Wanzhou, but now even the reigning Emperor, Shen Ji, had arrived!

No one dared to be the least bit negligent. They all stood up from their seats, smoothed their robes, and, led by Elder Xu and Wei Songjun, walked toward the courtyard entrance to greet him.

Cui Mingyu stood in the crowd, but her gaze fell upon Chaogui beside her. She saw the Princess’s face turn slightly pale, yet she only stood up slowly. Unlike the others, she did not hurry forward, but silently followed at the back of the line, her eyes lowered, showing no intention of coming forward to greet him.

Soon, a tall, slender figure appeared at the courtyard entrance. The reigning Emperor, Shen Ji, was dressed in simple blue civilian attire, wearing no dragon robes and accompanied by only two personal eunuchs, yet he could not hide the imperial aura about him. He crossed the threshold, his gaze sweeping over the flowers and the crowd. A bright, gentle smile appeared on his face, and his voice was resonant and warm: "I heard the Xu family’s poetry banquet was lively today, so I came in disguise to have a look. Please, continue, do not be constrained."

Despite his words, who would dare to truly be "unconstrained" with the Emperor present? Everyone present lowered their heads and held their breath. The courtyard, which had been so bustling just moments ago, was now so quiet that even the sound of the wind blowing through the leaves could be heard.

Elder Xu, filled with trepidation, quickly stepped forward and bowed: "This old subject greets Your Majesty! Long live the Emperor! Your Majesty has come at the perfect time; I was just fretting over how to judge the best poem of this banquet. I humbly ask Your Majesty to take a look!"

Hearing this, Shen Ji’s smile deepened, and he nodded with interest: "Oh? Is that so? Bring it to me." As he spoke, he took the poem scroll from Elder Xu, but his gaze inadvertently swept across the crowd, finally landing on Chaogui at the end of the line.

The smile in his eyes vanished instantly, and his tone turned colder: "Chaogui, why are you not staying at the Princess’s residence today? Why are you here causing a scene?"

Chaogui took a deep breath, slowly raised her head to meet Shen Ji’s gaze, her voice trembling slightly: "Imperial Brother, I am also an unmarried woman; why can I not be here?"

Cui Mingyu stood beside Chaogui, hearing her subtle trembling clearly, and couldn't help but chuckle inwardly—truly, every creature has its master. Princess Chaogui had always been fearless, daring to defy the world by keeping a stable of male favorites in her residence and mocking Wei Songjun to his face for being "impotent." Just moments ago, she had even helped her talk back to the venerable Elder Xu. Yet, in front of her own brother, that arrogant spirit instantly withered, and even her voice softened significantly.

Upon hearing this, Shen Ji’s lips curled into a meaningful arc. He rubbed the jade thumb ring on his finger, his gaze locked tightly on Chaogui, his eyes flashing with an inscrutable light. "Oh? Still waiting to be wed?" He paused, his tone carrying a hint of playfulness. "Since that is the case, is there any young nobleman at this poetry gathering today who has caught your eye? If there is, your Imperial Brother shall bestow a marriage upon you. How about that?"

Chaogui pouted at these words, then lifted her head and swept her gaze slowly across the crowd. Seeing this, those young noblemen were so frightened that they hurriedly lowered their heads, wishing they could bury their faces in their collars, not even daring to breathe loudly—who didn't know that this Princess Chaogui was reckless and kept male favorites? If they were to catch her eye, their future days would likely know no peace!

Chaogui scanned the circle and said indifferently, "Replying to Imperial Brother, there is none. Thank you for your concern."

"Whew—"

Hearing this, everyone present let out a sigh of relief in unison; even the air seemed to become much easier to breathe.

Shen Ji took a deep look at Chaogui, then withdrew his gaze and picked up the poem sheet in his hand, reading it carefully. But the more he read, the deeper his brows furrowed, and his expression gradually darkened—the poems today were either piles of flowery, hollow rhetoric or pretentious and affected; not a single one could catch his eye.

Mu Wanzhou, standing in the crowd, quietly raised her head, her gaze falling upon Shen Ji. Since childhood, she had been a famous talented woman in the capital, having attended several palace banquets and seen this Emperor of Great Qi many times. Yet, in the past, when she saw him, he was always clad in dragon robes, sitting upright on the dragon throne, radiating majesty and detachment, leaving her without even the courage to look up for more than a glance.

Since she could remember, her family had constantly drilled into her that she was to be the Empress, the future mistress of the Middle Palace. But toward that high and mighty monarch, she felt only awe, not a shred of romantic affection. For years, the position of Empress had remained vacant, and the Emperor had never shown any intention of appointing one. As she grew older, her family finally relented, no longer insisting on her entering the palace, and she finally breathed a sigh of relief.

Attending this poetry gathering at the Xu residence was also at the behest of her family—it was nothing more than a public announcement that she, Mu Wanzhou, the daughter of the Prime Minister’s residence, was ready to choose a husband.

Mu Wanzhou lowered her eyelashes, a trace of bitterness welling up in her heart. Sometimes, she felt her marriage was merely a chip in her parents' hands, a tool to consolidate the family's status. She raised her head, her gaze falling on Wei Songjun not far away.

Wei Songjun, dressed in black brocade robes, stood tall and straight in the crowd, his side profile cold and rigid, carrying a sense of aloofness that kept others at a distance. The way he looked at her was not filled with the amazement and covetousness of the other noblemen, yet it held a hint of undisguised appreciation. Mu Wanzhou bit her lip gently—raised since childhood by the standards of an Empress, her standards were extremely high; ordinary noblemen naturally could not catch her eye.

And Wei Songjun, the only prince of a different surname in Great Qi, was renowned, with both appearance and talent of the highest order. For her, he was just right.

Just then, Shen Ji picked up a poem sheet and asked, "Who wrote this?"

Elder Xu stepped forward to look; it was indeed Cui Mingyu’s line: "Draw a blade to cut the water, the water flows all the more; raise a cup to drown sorrows, the sorrows grow all the more."

chapters.title: The Best Poem
chapters.content:
Elder Xu bowed and cupped his hands, his voice resonant yet respectful: "Replying to Your Majesty, this poem was written by Cui Mingyu, daughter of the Minister of Revenue, Cui Yong."

Shen Ji’s hand holding the vermilion brush paused slightly. He raised his eyes to scan the crowd below the steps, his brows furrowing imperceptibly. He had some impression of the name Cui Mingyu—it was rumored she was close with Chaogui, and her reputation in the streets was not top-tier, mostly described as flighty and unconventional; he had never heard of her having such talent.

Shen Ji looked down at the poem on the plain paper: "Draw a blade to cut the water, the water flows all the more; raise a cup to drown sorrows, the sorrows grow all the more." The artistic conception between the lines far exceeded the scope of an ordinary lady’s boudoir. He mused to himself that the rumors must have been biased; this poem was indeed well-written.

With that thought, Shen Ji turned his wrist, the vermilion brush descended, and a vigorous "Excellent" was imprinted on the sheet, the red ink contrasting with the black, making it exceptionally striking.

Elder Xu was quick-witted; seeing this, he immediately called out loudly: "The best poem of the day is by Cui Mingyu, personally approved by the Emperor’s vermilion brush! Miss Cui, why don't you come forward to offer your thanks!"

As soon as these words were spoken, the courtyard fell silent for a moment, followed by a chorus of low gasps. No one had expected that, with so many fine works appearing today—especially Mu Wanzhou, known as the "First Talented Woman of Great Qi," whose poem "Spring Journey" had drawn endless praise—everyone had assumed the best would be hers. Who would have guessed the Emperor would favor Cui Mingyu’s poem alone?

Mu Wanzhou, standing in the front of the crowd, saw her usually gentle complexion turn pale. Having read poetry since childhood and possessing a widespread reputation for talent, she had come to the gathering determined to win, never imagining the top honor would fall to another. She stared in Cui Mingyu’s direction, a trace of unwillingness flashing in her eyes—Cui Mingyu’s line did have some merit, but to say it surpassed her own was something she could never admit.

As for Cui Mingyu, who had been named, she was currently hiding behind Princess Chaogui, her eyes wide with shock. She stared blankly at Elder Xu, then at the Emperor on the throne, her mind a complete blank: No way? She had just been forced into a corner and recited a line of Li Bai’s poetry on a whim; how did it become the best of the day? Li Taibai was truly amazing. If she had clung to Li Taibai’s coattails back then, she would be like a poetry immortal in this Great Qi Dynasty.

"Why are you standing there like a fool? Go up!" Princess Chaogui, standing beside her, gave her a gentle nudge with her elbow, her eyes full of laughter and pride.

Cui Mingyu finally snapped out of it, held her breath, and stepped forward quickly. Arriving below the throne, she knelt down properly, her voice still floating with disbelief: "Your subject’s daughter... Cui Mingyu, thanks Your Majesty for the grace!"

Shen Ji looked down at her from above. The girl before him wore her hair in simple double-ring buns, the wisps of hair on her forehead swaying slightly in the spring breeze. Her eyes were bright and round, revealing a hint of innocence and nervousness, not at all like the flamboyant person in the rumors. He curled his lips into a faint smile and said warmly, "I did not know that Minister Cui had raised such a talented daughter."

Cui Mingyu’s heart skipped a beat, and she grumbled inwardly: Your Majesty, please stop praising me! I don't know how to write poetry; I’m purely a "transporter" who memorized a lot of ancient poems in the modern world! She was drumming in her heart, but she dared not show it on her face, so she could only lower her head and say cautiously, "Your subject’s daughter... thanks Your Majesty for the undeserved praise; I am unworthy of such honor."

"No matter." Shen Ji waved his hand and turned his gaze to Chaogui. "I hear you are very close with Chaogui, and Chaogui also has some accomplishments in poetry. You two can study and improve together in the future."

Cui Mingyu, fearing that saying too much would lead to a slip, buried her head even lower and replied respectfully, "Yes, your subject’s daughter obeys the decree."

Seeing this, Shen Ji said no more and called out loudly, "Chaogui, you have seen enough excitement for today; follow me back to the palace!"

The smile on Princess Chaogui’s face froze instantly, as if a basin of cold water had been poured over her, and her shoulders slumped slightly. Knowing she could not defy him, she replied in a low, dejected voice, "Yes, Imperial Brother."

Cui Mingyu knelt to the side, watching Chaogui’s expression, and couldn't help but laugh to herself—she looked exactly like a child who had snuck out to play and was caught by their parents to be taken home. Seeing Chaogui’s low spirits, she leaned over and whispered in a voice only the two of them could hear, "Princess, look, the poetry gathering is almost over. The rest is just polite social niceties, nothing interesting. I’m planning to head back soon too."

Chaogui barely pulled at the corners of her mouth, squeezed out a smile, and nodded gently, "Okay."

Shen Ji stood up and said indifferently, "I shall take my leave first; you may do as you please." With that, he turned and left with the palace attendants. Chaogui followed reluctantly, her retreating figure appearing to Cui Mingyu to be filled with an indescribable sense of desolation and grievance.

Cui Mingyu was staring at Chaogui’s back, wondering when she could ask her out to play again, when a gentle, soft voice came from her side: "Miss Cui, congratulations."

She turned to see Mu Wanzhou standing behind her, dressed in a moon-white long dress, her temperament elegant, though her brows carried a trace of undisguised complexity. Cui Mingyu understood—this was the heroine of the original book, a truly talented woman. Her own "transported" best poem made her feel quite guilty in front of her.

She hurriedly stood up, cupped her hands toward Mu Wanzhou, and smiled, "Miss Mu is too kind; it was purely a coincidence! Your vast knowledge and widespread reputation for talent are plain for all to see; you are a role model for us juniors and the deserved first talented woman. I feel quite ashamed to have received this 'best' honor."

Mu Wanzhou smiled faintly, but the smile did not reach her eyes. "They are but empty names. I usually stay shut away, and only by attending this poetry gathering today did I realize there are heavens beyond heavens and people beyond people. I hope to have many opportunities to consult with you in the future, Miss Cui; I hope you will not begrudge your guidance."

Cui Mingyu felt guilty, cold sweat almost breaking out on her back, and she could only force a laugh and squeeze out two words: "Happy to, happy to." Her eyes darted around, and she suddenly caught sight of Prince Jingnan Wei Songjun standing by the railing in the corridor not far away.

A plan suddenly formed in Cui Mingyu’s mind—since she had transmigrated into the book, why not take the opportunity to play matchmaker for the original hero and heroine, so Wei Songjun wouldn't keep finding trouble for her because of the "vicious supporting character’s" past infatuation!

She immediately pointed toward Wei Songjun with a smile and said to Mu Wanzhou, "Miss Mu may not know, but Prince Jingnan’s accomplishments in poetry are truly the pinnacle! I have also occasionally heard that the Prince greatly appreciates your talent, Miss. Instead of asking me for advice, why not take this opportunity to exchange ideas with Prince Jingnan?
