You will surely benefit greatly!"

As soon as she finished speaking, she saw Mu Wanzhou raise her eyebrows slightly, her gaze toward her carrying a hint of inquiry: "So, Miss Cui’s poem was guided by Prince Jingnan?"

Cui Mingyu: "???"

No, Miss, you’ve got the wrong focus! The point is "Prince Jingnan appreciates you," it’s about matching you two up! She was stunned for a moment, then hurriedly waved her hands to explain: "Miss Mu, you’ve misunderstood! Although I was young and ignorant in the past and had a bit of a naive crush on Prince Jingnan, that is all in the past and has long been turned over! The Prince has never had any other intentions toward me; I am very clear about that."

Fearing that Mu Wanzhou might not believe her, she added, "I think it must be a peerless beauty like you, with both immortal grace and inner virtue, who can truly catch His Highness's eye!"

This was said with such sincerity that Mu Wanzhou’s expression softened slightly. But just then, a sinister voice sounded without warning behind them, carrying a chilling, piercing quality: "Oh? I was unaware that Miss Cui and I were on such intimate terms that you could so confidently speculate on my intentions?"

Cui Mingyu stiffened all over, as if struck by a bolt of lightning, and nearly jumped in fright. This voice... was it Wei Songjun?! She turned her head stiffly and slowly, and sure enough, she saw that Wei Songjun had appeared behind them at some point. His deep eyes were fixed on her with a look that was half-smile, half-stare, and the coldness in their depths made her shudder.

It’s over, it’s really true that you shouldn't speak ill of people behind their backs. What kind of supernatural skill has he mastered? How did he get over here in the blink of an eye?

Seeing this, Mu Wanzhou hurriedly curtsied: "This subject's daughter pays respects to His Highness, the Prince of Jingnan."

Cui Mingyu managed to force out a dry, awkward smile. "Just now... at the poetry gathering, I saw that Your Highness truly appreciated Miss Mu," she paused, "Um, Your Highness! Miss Mu's poetry is truly remarkable, you two should exchange ideas! I suddenly remembered my father asked me to return home early, so I shall take my leave first. Goodbye!"

Without waiting for them to react, she gave a hurried bow and turned to run like a gust of wind, her skirt fluttering behind her, looking for all the world like a little rabbit being chased by a wolf.

Wei Songjun watched her retreating figure, a flash of cold light in his eyes that instantly sank back into their depths.

chapters.title: Imprisoned Phoenix (I)
chapters.content:
Chaogui followed Shen Ji’s footsteps and stopped outside the vermilion gates. The sun overhead was scorching, yet it could not warm the chill in her heart.

"Imperial Brother, I can return to the Princess's Mansion by myself." Her voice was very soft, like a feather landing on a calm lake.

Shen Ji’s footsteps stopped abruptly, and the air pressure around him plummeted. He turned slowly. "Ah Zhi," he called her by her childhood name, his voice as cold as tempered ice, "you are testing my patience."

Chaogui’s heart trembled violently, as if a heavy object had fallen from a great height, sinking straight into a bottomless abyss. She lowered her eyes, masking the complex emotions within. Shen Ji stopped looking at her and walked straight toward the bright yellow carriage waiting nearby.

Chaogui stood where she was, watching him lift the curtain and step inside. The curtain swayed a few times before settling, but her heart beat faster and faster, as if it were about to burst from her chest. The day was exceptionally beautiful, the sunlight so bright it was dazzling, yet she felt as if heavy black clouds were pressing down on her, making even breathing difficult.

She knew that the man behind the curtain must have eyes as heavy as frost and snow at this moment. Even through the thin fabric, the heavy aura of the Emperor firmly enveloped her, leaving her almost unable to breathe. Chaogui sighed inwardly, suppressing the bitterness in her heart, and walked numbly toward the carriage that symbolized her imprisonment.

As soon as the curtain fell, cutting off the sunlight and noise outside, a warm, powerful hand suddenly grabbed her wrist. The grip was so tight it hurt, and in the next instant, she was pulled by a great force into a broad and familiar embrace.

Chaogui did not cry out, as if she had long expected this scene. She only lowered her long eyelashes, which trembled slightly, deliberately avoiding Shen Ji’s gaze. Shen Ji’s fingers, calloused from years of handling weapons, gently hooked her chin, forcing her to look up at him. His phoenix eyes narrowed, complex emotions churning in their depths—possession, anger, and even a trace of grievance.

"Ah Zhi, what is this?" his voice was low and hoarse, carrying a hint of danger. "Are you looking for another consort? Are the many male favorites in your mansion not enough to amuse you?"

Chaogui’s expression remained indifferent, as if she hadn't heard the mockery and jealousy in his words. "Why is Imperial Brother in such a rush?" She struggled slightly, but could not break free from his grip. "Didn't I choose not to?"

Shen Ji’s fingertips slowly traced her lips, his movements carrying a lingering tenderness that contrasted sharply with his cold, hard tone. "There is no one else here, Ah Zhi," his voice softened, yet remained unyieldingly firm, "do not call me Imperial Brother."

A faint, mocking smile curled the corners of Chaogui’s mouth, though her eyes remained cold. "But in the eyes of the world," she raised her eyes to meet his deep phoenix gaze, "you are my Imperial Brother, and I am your Imperial Sister. This status is a shackle that neither of us can break free from."

Just as Shen Ji was about to speak, a eunuch’s cautious voice came from outside the carriage: "Your Majesty, shall we return to the palace now?"

Shen Ji’s brow furrowed almost imperceptibly, and he said in a deep voice: "To the Princess's Mansion." He paused, turned his head, and let his gaze fall on Chaogui’s pale face, his tone carrying a trace of exhaustion and pleading. "Ah Zhi, you are mine," he cupped her face, his fingertips gently stroking her cheek, "you are mine for this life and the next. I will not allow you to harbor any other thoughts!"

"When Liang Siqi used the late Emperor’s blank imperial decree to force me to let him marry you, I had no choice but to agree," his voice lowered, a flash of painful regret crossing his eyes. "But I have spent countless days and nights regretting it—regretting letting you marry him, regretting not being able to keep you by my side. Ah Zhi, in this life, I will never let you marry another man, never!"

Chaogui sneered, a hint of redness appearing in her eyes. "So Imperial Brother rushed to the poetry gathering," her voice trembled slightly, "because you were afraid that your subject's sister had thoughts of choosing a husband, afraid that I would remarry and escape your control?"

"The world knows the purpose of Elder Xu hosting this poetry gathering," Shen Ji’s gaze locked onto her, filled with scrutiny. "You never attended such occasions before, why go today?"

"Imperial Brother worries too much." Chaogui turned her face away, avoiding his burning gaze. "Since my husband passed away, my heart has been like withered wood; I have no other desires. Furthermore, my reputation is ruined. In this capital, who would dare to marry me?"

Shen Ji’s heart ached sharply. He cupped Chaogui’s face, forcing her to look at him. Seeing the bloodshot eyes and her forced display of strength, the anger and possessiveness in his heart were instantly replaced by heartache. He lowered his head and kissed her lips fiercely, his movements carrying a hint of punishment, yet also revealing extreme longing.

"Withered wood?" He pulled away from her lips, looking at her with unsteady breath, his eyes churning with intense emotion. "What right does Liang Siqi have to occupy your heart? Ah Zhi, your heart, your person, can only be mine! Only mine!"

Chaogui slowly closed her eyes, and tears finally spilled from the corners, soaking her temples. The tears were scalding, yet they could not extinguish the chill in her heart.

"Shen Ji," her voice was heavily nasal, every word seemingly squeezed out from the depths of her throat with great difficulty, "I could have been happy with him. I risked my life to escape the cage of the Imperial Palace, to escape you. If it weren't for you, he and I would have lived very happily..."

"Ah Zhi, you blame me!" Shen Ji’s voice rose sharply, carrying a sense of being offended and an irrepressible anger. He cupped her face, forcing her to look at him, his deep phoenix eyes filled with bloodshot redness. "You are mine! From beginning to end, you are mine! Liang Siqi was merely a subject; how dare he harbor designs on you? And to dare use the late Emperor’s decree to threaten me—how could I let him have his way! How could I let him snatch you from my side!"

His voice trembled with agitation, his fingertips rubbing her cheeks forcefully, as if he wanted to knead her skin into his own palms.

"Imperial Brother, that is all in the past," Chaogui opened her eyes, her gaze dead and still, like a late autumn lake without a ripple. "I don't want to talk about it anymore, and I don't want to think about it anymore."

But Shen Ji would not let her go. He lowered his head and kissed her lips again, this time more frantically, more forcefully, with a despair that bordered on self-destruction, as if he wanted to swallow her whole, to carve her into his very bones and blood so that she could never be stripped from his life again.

Chaogui was kissed until she was nearly suffocating, and could only weakly grab his lapels, her nails digging deep into the expensive cloud-brocade fabric. She closed her eyes in resignation, her body trembling slightly in his arms.

Just as her consciousness was about to be completely submerged by this predatory kiss, an image of a gentle and humble figure uncontrollably flashed through her mind—it was Liang Siqi.

chapters.title: Imprisoned Phoenix (II)
chapters.content:
They first met in the Imperial Garden. That year, she was sixteen, in the prime of her youth. At that time, she lived in the palace with extreme caution, walking on thin ice. He was eighteen, the new top scholar, with handsome features and a gentle temperament. He had noticed her at a glance as she admired flowers alone in a corner.

He said: "Your Highness, I am Liang Siqi. I am willing to spend my whole life protecting you."

At that time, she was determined to escape Shen Ji’s omnipresent control, to escape the golden cage of the Imperial Palace. She thought Liang Siqi was her salvation, the only hope for her escape.

But how could Shen Ji agree? He viewed her as the treasure in his palm, an obsession carved into his marrow; how could he allow her to turn and throw herself into another’s arms?

In order to marry Liang Siqi, Chaogui gathered her courage for the first time and had a bitter confrontation with Shen Ji. She argued with him, every word revealing her determination to escape. Shen Ji remained cold-faced, silent, his heavy gaze almost swallowing her whole.

Driven to a dead end, Chaogui finally resorted to her last measure. She held a sharp dagger to her own throat, her vision blurred with tears, her voice trembling with despair: "Imperial Brother, if you do not allow me to marry him, I will die before your eyes!"

Shen Ji’s pupils contracted sharply, the cold air around him almost freezing the atmosphere. Just as Chaogui closed her eyes, preparing to push the blade, Shen Ji lunged forward and gripped the dagger pressed against her throat with his bare hand.

The cold blade sliced through his palm, and blood surged out instantly, staining the dagger and her clothes. He used immense force to wrench the dagger from her hand, then turned it around, gripping the handle, and thrust it straight toward his own chest.

"Ah Zhi," his voice was hoarse, his eyes churning with blood-red madness and despair, "if you want to marry him, you must step over my dead body!"

Chaogui trembled in terror, tears streaming down her face. She tried to grab the dagger back, but Shen Ji held her hand firmly. He looked at her with a resolve that burned his bridges: "Either you stay, or I die. You choose."

Chaogui broke down in tears. She had never seen Shen Ji like this—so paranoid that he would use his own life as a threat. Her resistance seemed so pale and powerless in the face of his desperation.

Just as the two were at a stalemate and Chaogui was about to give up, news of Liang Siqi arrived. He had personally requested an audience with his grandfather—that venerable old official who had once been deeply trusted by the late Emperor. The old man, feeling pity for his grandson and cherishing the memory of the late Emperor’s past favors, finally relented. He retrieved a blank imperial decree from his secret chamber and personally wrote out the edict granting the marriage.

When that decree, bearing the late Emperor’s jade seal, was placed before Shen Ji, his entire aura of arrogance instantly dissipated. He stared at the bright yellow scroll, his eyes churning with monstrous rage and unwillingness, yet he was ultimately helpless. The late Emperor’s final decree was like an unbridgeable chasm; even as the sovereign, he could not openly defy it.

He looked at Chaogui for a long time before squeezing a few words through his teeth: "Fine, I grant it."

On the day of her wedding, she wore a bright red bridal gown and sat in the sedan chair that would take her away from the imperial palace. Turning back to look at the towering palace walls, she revealed a smile of relief—she had finally left; she could finally have a life of her own.

But she did not expect that this was merely the beginning of another nightmare.

On the wedding night, in the bridal chamber, the red candles burned brightly, and the "double happiness" characters cast a red glow across the room. No sooner had Liang Siqi finished the nuptial wine than he felt dizzy and collapsed onto the bed, unconscious. Immediately after, the door was shoved open, and Shen Ji walked in, clad in his black dragon robe, his body radiating a chilling coldness.

He reached out, his fingertips calloused, and gently stroked her cheek. His movements held a strange, eerie tenderness, but his eyes were cold and obsessive. "You are mine," he said, enunciating every word. "In this life, the next life, for all eternity, don't even think about marrying anyone else."

That night, the red candles burned down, the wicks gave a faint "pop," and the room plunged into total darkness. Tears silently soaked the silk quilt beneath her, pressing against her skin like cold, unmeltable ice. Shen Ji’s movements carried a near-destructive possessiveness; every touch made her tremble, yet she was powerless to resist. She bit her lip hard to keep from making a sound, her gaze hollow as she stared at the impenetrable darkness above the canopy, as if her soul had been ripped from her body.

Not far away, on the daybed in the outer room, Liang Siqi remained in a deep sleep, oblivious to the humiliation and despair filling the room. His peaceful sleeping face became the most stinging irony in Chaogui's eyes.

From that day on, her marriage became a complete and utter joke.

After Liang Siqi woke up, he seemed to know everything, yet he also seemed to know nothing. He did not question her, nor did he show anger; it was just that in the way he looked at her, there was an added layer of something heavy and unreadable. He remained gentle and attentive, picking out hairpins for her every morning, silently keeping her company while she read, and attempting to soothe the scars in her heart with his quiet presence beneath her seemingly calm facade.

But Chaogui knew that everything could never go back to how it was.

The shadow of that night was like an invisible chasm lying between them. His gentleness became a burden, and his attentiveness only made her feel more guilty and pained. She began to subconsciously avoid his gaze and reject his closeness. Though they lived under the same roof, it was as if they were separated by vast mountains and rivers, polite yet distant. She knew he was protecting her in his own way, and punishing himself in his own way. Yet, she lacked the courage to even give him an explanation or an apology.

Later, while Liang Siqi was hunting, his mount was startled, and he unfortunately fell from his horse, suffering grave injuries.

When she heard the news, Chaogui was trimming a pot of blooming begonias by the window. The scissors in her hand fell to the floor with a "clang," the flower stems were snapped in two, and the delicate petals scattered across the ground like her shattered hopes.

Liang Siqi held on to his final breath to see her. He lay on the sickbed, his face as pale as paper, his breathing faint: "Ah Zhi, my greatest regret in this life was taking that blank decree to marry you. If I had known it would come to this, I should have..." Before he could finish his sentence, he closed his eyes forever.

Chaogui stood there quietly, neither crying nor making a scene. She looked at the ruined petals on the floor for a very, very long time. Her heart felt hollow, as if a piece had been forcibly carved out, with cold wind blowing into the void. That was the last faint light in her life, and it, too, had been extinguished.

Later still, she became a princess looked at askance by everyone in the capital. She began to seek out one lover after another, vengefully, using Liang Siqi’s features as a template. Some had similar brow bones, some had gentle eyes, and some had shallow dimples when they smiled... She kept them by her side, filling the void in her heart with the most extravagant means, trying to piece together that long-lost figure from them.

However, she knew clearly that no matter how similar those faces were, they were not him. They lacked the clarity in his eyes, the faint scent of ink about him, and, most of all, his deep-seated gentleness and respect.

She could never find that gentle youth who would smile at her in the Imperial Garden and say, "I wish to spend my whole life protecting you, Your Highness."

The carriage slowed to a stop at the Princess's Mansion. Shen Ji walked into the mansion openly, as if nothing were amiss. The servants, long accustomed to this, lowered their heads, not daring to look twice.

As soon as he entered Chaogui's bedchamber, Shen Ji impatiently threw her onto the bed and covered her body with his own. His kisses fell densely upon her forehead, cheeks, and lips, carrying a frantic possessiveness, as if he wanted to tear her apart and swallow her whole, melting her into his own flesh and blood.

Chaogui lay on the bed, her eyes hollow, staring at the exquisite phoenix embroidery on the canopy, tears sliding silently into her hair. She neither resisted nor responded, like a soulless porcelain doll.

She knew that in this life, she would never escape.

Shen Ji’s love was a honey-coated poison, a diamond-encrusted shackle. It caused her unbearable pain, yet in his occasional moments of tenderness, it made her harbor a desperate, forbidden hope. She had once been grateful to him because he had saved her, but she also hated him—hated him for destroying everything she had.

chapters.title: Expressing Affection Through Food
chapters.content:
As Cui Mingyu slipped out of the Xu residence, steady footsteps sounded behind her. She didn't need to turn around; that familiar, crisp scent already lingered at the tip of her nose. Cui Mingyu turned to see Xia Yuning standing not far away. Sunlight filtered through the begonia branches, casting light upon him and outlining his tall, upright figure; the jade hairpin in his hair glowed with a warm luster.

"The Xu residence is hosting a banquet at noon. Are you not staying to dine?" Having run in such a hurry to avoid Wei Songjun, Cui Mingyu’s breath was still a bit uneven as she spoke.

Hearing this, Xia Yuning approached slowly. His deep eyes seemed to be filled with the starry sky, bright and reflecting Cui Mingyu’s figure, so gentle they could melt. "I was never one of them to begin with," he said, a faint, light smile tugging at the corners of his lips, his tone carrying a touch of detachment. "They are all brilliant scholars who can compose poetry at the drop of a hat, while I am full of the 'stench of copper,' knowing only how to calculate business. In the end, we have nothing in common to talk about."

He paused, his gaze resting on Cui Mingyu’s face with a hint of unhidden awe and shyness, his voice softening: "Mingyu, at the poetry gathering today, I had no idea your mastery of poetry was so profound—even His Majesty couldn't stop praising it..."

Cui Mingyu felt a warmth in her heart. She naturally understood Xia Yuning’s concerns. In the hierarchy of scholar, farmer, artisan, and merchant, the merchant was at the very bottom. Even though he was born into the Changning Marquis’s house, the heir had long been decided, and for some reason, the Marquis had not allowed him to pursue an official career, instead having him take over his mother’s businesses. Over the years, Xia Yuning had often been looked down upon by those self-proclaimed lofty literati because of his status as a "merchant."

Cui Mingyu’s small nose crinkled slightly: "Of the four classes, each one is indispensable to the world—scholars govern the country, farmers till the land to feed us, artisans craft goods with clever hands, and merchants facilitate the exchange of goods. None can be spared. Industries can be categorized, and roles can be divided, but human hearts should not be ranked. One cannot say that being a scholar makes one superior, nor that being a merchant makes one inferior. As long as one can shine in their own field and achieve something, they are the best of the world; they are all worthy of respect and are all remarkable!"

Xia Yuning was slightly stunned, his footsteps halting as he stared blankly at Cui Mingyu. The sunlight fell into her clear eyes, which held no trace of disdain, only pure recognition and sincerity. He had lived for nearly twenty years, hearing too many cold words because of his status as a merchant—even people in his own household often gossiped behind his back—but no one had ever told him so directly that a merchant could also hold their head high and become a leader in their field.

His heart felt as if it were blocked by something soft, heavy, and yet it was as if a long-standing knot had suddenly been untied. A sense of relief spread from the bottom of his heart, and even his breathing became much easier. His Adam's apple bobbed as he gazed at Cui Mingyu, his voice a bit hoarse but incredibly solemn: "Mingyu... thank you."

Seeing the gloom in his eyes dissipate, replaced by a bright luster, Cui Mingyu couldn't help but laugh, her brows curving like the bright blossoms of spring: "So, you shouldn't belittle yourself anymore. Your talent for business is something those scholars who only know how to recite poetry can't compare to!"

Watching her brilliant smile, the warmth in Xia Yuning’s heart deepened. He nodded and looked up at the sky; it was past noon, and the sun was high. "It is past noon, and you surely haven't eaten yet," he said, looking at her with a hint of anticipation. "Shall we go to the Tianxiang Restaurant for a meal? They recently introduced a new roast goose—the skin is crispy, the meat is tender, and it’s incredibly fragrant. I wonder if you’ve tried it before, Mingyu?"

Cui Mingyu’s heart stirred at the mention. She had been in this body for over a month, eating home-cooked meals at the Cui residence every day, and the only other food she had were the delicate pastries Xia Yuning sent over. She had never properly gone out to a restaurant. The roast goose sounded mouth-watering.

However... she frowned slightly, feeling a bit hesitant. Although she had tacitly accepted their courtship, this was, after all, ancient times, where the segregation between men and women was strict. For a man and a woman to dine openly at a restaurant—if they were seen, gossip would inevitably spread.

Xia Yuning, being observant, saw through her concerns at once. The corners of his lips lifted into a knowing smile, and he softly reassured her: "Don't worry, Mingyu. I have reserved a private room at the Tianxiang Restaurant. It is quiet and elegant; no one will disturb us, and no outsiders will see us."

Only then did Cui Mingyu breathe a sigh of relief. A smile bloomed on her face again, and she nodded gently: "Alright, then let's go try that roast goose."

When they arrived at the Tianxiang Restaurant, a waiter was already waiting at the door. Upon seeing Xia Yuning, he hurried forward respectfully: "Young Master Xia, your private room is ready. Please follow me."

The private room was elegantly and comfortably furnished, with a window seat offering a view of the street below. Xia Yuning gestured for Cui Mingyu to sit, then took the menu and asked her to order. Cui Mingyu demurred, insisting that Xia Yuning take the lead. Xia Yuning skillfully ordered several dishes: "First, let’s have the signature roast goose, followed by the crystal pork knuckle, the emerald jade rolls, a bowl of white fungus and lotus seed soup, and a plate of osmanthus cakes."

Watching his practiced manner, Cui Mingyu couldn't help but ask curiously, "How do you know about so many delicacies? You seem to know the restaurants in the capital like the back of your hand."

Xia Yuning handed the menu to the waiter, then turned to look at Cui Mingyu, his gaze gentle and his tone soft. "Because I believe that savoring the world's delicacies is one of the greatest pleasures in life. Over the years, I’ve traveled far and wide and tasted food from many places. Over time, I’ve grown fond of hunting for the world’s best flavors; I know where most of the good food is."

Cui Mingyu suddenly understood, her eyes filled with envy. "That’s wonderful. To be able to taste all the delicacies in the world—just thinking about it makes me feel happy."

As they spoke, the dishes were brought to the table one after another. The roast goose was just as Xia Yuning had described: the skin was crispy and golden, and with a light bite, the fat melted in the mouth while the meat remained tender, juicy, and fragrant. Cui Mingyu’s appetite was piqued; she picked up her chopsticks and began to eat with gusto, clearly enjoying herself, her face wreathed in a satisfied smile.

Xia Yuning watched her happy expression, his eyes filled with doting affection. He ate very little himself, spending most of his time watching her and occasionally placing food in her bowl, reminding her, "Eat slowly, don't choke. There’s plenty more."

Cui Mingyu swallowed the food in her mouth and took a sip of the white fungus and lotus seed soup. It was refreshing and sweet, and she couldn't help but let out a sigh of comfort. She suddenly remembered the mutton soup Xia Yuning had sent over last time; the flavor had been rich and savory without a trace of gaminess, leaving a deep impression on her.

"By the way," Cui Mingyu looked up at Xia Yuning, her eyes filled with anticipation, "where was that mutton soup you sent last time made? It was so delicious, and there wasn't a hint of gaminess. It was the first time I’d ever had such good mutton soup."

Hearing this, a faint smile tugged at the corners of Xia Yuning’s lips. "That’s from an inconspicuous little shop in the capital. The owner is quite temperamental; he cooks a pot only when he feels like it, and if he doesn't, he doesn't open for business. Moreover, he only makes one pot a day and closes once it’s sold out, so it’s very hard to reserve. I had to pull some strings with an acquaintance last time to get a portion."

chapters.title: The Sensible Daughter
chapters.content:
Cui Mingyu’s face showed a hint of disappointment. So it was that hard to reserve; it seemed she wouldn't have a chance to drink it again. However, she also knew that such delicacies were a matter of luck, not something one could force. She quickly adjusted her mood and said with a smile, "The owner is quite a character. Being so free-spirited is a kind of freedom in itself."

Xia Yuning took in the changes in her expression and understood her thoughts. After a moment’s reflection, he changed the subject, his tone carrying a hint of temptation: "There are many such delicacies hidden in the alleys of the capital, but they are tucked away and few outsiders know of them. When I have time in a few days, I’ll take you to try them. I guarantee you’ll have a feast."

Cui Mingyu’s eyes lit up instantly. A bright smile bloomed on her face again, and she nodded vigorously. "Okay, okay! It’s a deal then, and you’re not allowed to go back on your word!"

"I won't go back on it." Xia Yuning felt his heart soften as he looked at her radiant smile.

The two spent nearly an hour at the Tianxiang Restaurant before leaving at a leisurely pace. Xia Yuning accompanied Cui Mingyu all the way to the entrance of the Cui residence. He watched her walk through the gate and didn't turn away, filled with reluctance, until her figure was no longer visible.

Back at the Cui residence, Cui Mingyu had just sat down to have a cup of tea when she heard a servant report that her father, Cui Yong, had returned from work. Her heart tightened, and she thought to herself, *This is bad.* Her father must have heard about what happened at the poetry gathering today; she was likely in for a lecture.

Sure enough, as soon as Cui Yong walked into the living room, his gaze fell on Cui Mingyu. His expression was complex—a mix of surprise, suspicion, and a trace of imperceptible worry. He stroked his beard, his brows furrowed as he stared at her, his tone stern. "Mingzhu, I’ve heard about what happened at the Xu family’s poetry gathering today. Tell me honestly, did you really write that line, 'Draw a blade to cut the water, the water flows more; raise a cup to drown sorrow, the sorrow grows more'?"

Cui Mingyu sighed inwardly, complaining to herself. How was she to know that reciting a line from Li Bai would lead to an imperial annotation from the Emperor, earning her the title of "best in the gathering"? Had she known it would cause so much trouble, she wouldn't have been impulsive and tried to show off; she should have just played dumb. Now, she had to rack her brains for an excuse to cover the lie.

"Father," Cui Mingyu looked up, her eyes slightly evasive, her tone tinged with grievance. "I really heard those lines vaguely in a dream. I remembered a few sentences after I woke up, and today at the gathering, I was caught up in the moment and recited them. I never expected to gain the Emperor's appreciation..."

Cui Yong naturally didn't believe her. He knew his daughter; while she was clever, she had never shown any talent for poetry. How could she suddenly write such philosophical lines? He frowned even more deeply, his tone becoming more severe. "Mingzhu, stop talking nonsense! Father knows you are competitive, but if you don't have the skill, don't take on the task. It’s not shameful to admit you don't know something, but you must never claim someone else's poetry as your own!"

Cui Mingyu lowered her head, feeling helpless. She *had* claimed it as her own, but Li Bai was a man from a thousand years ago—he couldn't exactly crawl out of his grave to cause her trouble, could he? She looked up, her eyes slightly red and brimming with tears, and looked at Cui Yong with a mix of coquetry and grievance. "Father, it’s all true. Why don't you believe me? Even if I’m not always sensible, I wouldn't joke about something like this!"

Seeing his daughter’s reddened eyes, Cui Yong’s heart softened. He sighed, his tone easing, his eyes filled with worry. "Mingzhu, it’s not that I don't believe you, but today’s events are too suspicious. You shone brightly at the gathering and received the Emperor’s personal annotation; I fear your name is known throughout the capital now. A tall tree catches the wind. With you being so prominent, there’s no telling how much jealousy and plotting you’ll attract. I don't ask for you to be outstanding; I only hope you grow up safely, marry into a good family, and live a stable life."

He paused, his tone filled with regret. "It’s a pity. Although that boy Xia Yuning is a merchant, he is sincere toward you, his character is upright, and he has a solid foundation, yet you just don't seem to fancy him..."

"Who says I don't fancy him!" Cui Mingyu retorted subconsciously.

Cui Yong was stunned. He looked up abruptly, staring at Cui Mingyu in disbelief. "You... what did you say? You fancy that boy Xia Yuning?"

Cui Mingyu’s cheeks flushed slightly, but she nodded solemnly, her eyes firm. "Father, I told Xia Yuning that if his heart remains unchanged after one year, I will marry him."

Cui Yong was stunned for a moment, then an expression of overjoyed surprise appeared on his face. He was so excited that his beard twitched. "Really? Mingzhu, are you telling the truth? Are you truly willing to marry Xia Yuning?"

"Yes." Cui Mingyu nodded solemnly again. Seeing Cui Yong’s excitement, she felt a warmth in her heart. She knew that Cui Yong had always liked Xia Yuning, and he must be very happy that she was now willing to accept him.

She paused, looking at the gray hairs at Cui Yong’s temples, and felt a pang of sorrow. Her mother had passed away many years ago, and Cui Yong had raised her alone, acting as both father and mother, which was very difficult. He had never remarried. She hesitated, then gathered her courage and asked, "Father, Mother has been gone for so many years. Have you... ever thought about finding a companion?"

The teacup in Cui Yong’s hand clattered onto the table, his eyes wide as copper bells. "Y-you, what did you say?"

In the past, whenever he mentioned remarrying, his daughter would immediately fly into a rage, either crying, making a scene, or going on a hunger strike, driving him to distraction. Today, the girl had actually brought it up herself, and with such a sweet, obedient smile—Cui Yong felt as if the sun had risen in the west.

Cui Mingyu’s heart skipped a beat, and she realized her mistake. She hadn't fully digested the original owner's memories and had spoken too quickly, forgetting the original owner's attitude. Thinking fast, she immediately leaned against Cui Yong, shook his arm, and said in a cloyingly sweet voice, "Father~ I was just young and ignorant before, always afraid that someone would take away your love for me. Now that I’ve grown up, I realize how lonely you must be. Once I’m married, you’ll be all alone in this house with no one to talk to. How pitiful that would be."

As she spoke, she secretly observed Cui Yong’s expression. Seeing his tense face gradually relax and his eyes even welling up with tears, she finally breathed a sigh of relief.

Cui Yong was so touched and moved by his daughter’s words that he spent the night crying bitterly before his wife’s memorial tablet.

chapters.title: Boating on the Lake
chapters.content:
Three days later, the weather was perfect. The sweltering heat of the past few days seemed to have been gently paused by an invisible hand. The sun had reined in its usual scorching power, leaving only a warm, glowing halo that gently spilled over the bluestone path. A breeze, carrying the unique coolness of early morning, brushed past the eaves, swept up a few early-falling phoenix tree leaves, and quietly grazed the ears of the stone lions in front of the Cui residence’s vermilion gate.

It was in this pleasant morning light that Xia Yuning stood quietly outside the Cui residence. He did not ask the doorman to announce him, but stood with his hands behind his back. His moon-white brocade robe made his posture appear even more upright, and his eyes held a hint of imperceptible anticipation. The morning dew had not yet dried and had dampened the hem of his robe, but he seemed unaware, his gaze fixed steadily on the closed gate, as if he could see through the wood to the figure he had been longing for.

One incense stick of time, two incense sticks of time... Time flowed quietly in the breeze. About an hour later, the side gate of the Cui residence finally creaked open. Cui Mingyu walked out, lifting her skirt. She was dressed in a pale pink ru-skirt, with only a simple, elegant white jade hairpin in her hair. The morning light fell on her face, making her look as soft as a pool of spring water. As soon as she stepped out, she saw Xia Yuning standing not far away, as straight as a pine, looking at her with a smile.

"How long have you been here?" Cui Mingyu was slightly startled, then walked up quickly, her tone filled with surprise and a hint of reproach. "Why didn't you have someone announce you? How long have you been standing here?"

Xia Yuning took a step forward and naturally took the small bundle from her hand, saying warmly, "I only just arrived. I was afraid of disturbing your rest, so I waited here for a while." His voice was low and pleasant, like jade soaked in morning dew, showing no sign of impatience.

Cui Mingyu looked at him skeptically. Seeing the dew on his hem, she knew he must have been waiting for a long time. Her heart warmed slightly, but she said, "You mustn't do this next time. You’ll catch a cold if you stand here for too long."

"Alright, I'll listen to you." Xia Yuning smiled and agreed, reaching out to support her arm. "Let's go, the carriage is already prepared."

The two walked side by side toward the carriage parked at the street corner. Xia Yuning lifted the curtain first, helped Cui Mingyu into the carriage, and then followed her inside. The interior was covered with soft brocade cushions, and in the corner sat a small table holding a pot of hot tea, from which wisps of steam curled, emitting a faint fragrance.

Xia Yuning took an exquisite brocade box from his sleeve, handed it to Cui Mingyu, and smiled. "For you."

Cui Mingyu took the box and opened it to find a box of crystal-clear crystal dragon-phoenix cakes—the signature snack of Wufangzhai. She couldn't help but laugh. "Wufangzhai cakes again? Xia Yuning, are you planning to feed me until I'm a little fatty so that I can never get married?"

Watching her charming expression, the smile in Xia Yuning's eyes deepened. He said gently, "How can I break a promise made to you? If I don't give them to you to eat, how will you ever get tired of them?"

Cui Mingyu’s heart softened. Holding the brocade box, her fingertips felt slightly warm. She pulled something from her own sleeve, handed it over, and said with some embarrassment, "You’ve given me so many things, and I’ve never had a proper return gift. This sachet is filled with mosquito-repellent herbs. Summer is coming, and you might find it useful when you're out and about."

Xia Yuning took the sachet. The brocade felt soft in his hand, embroidered with a few simple blades of orchid grass with delicate stitches. He felt a slight jolt in his heart and looked up at Cui Mingyu. "This... did you make this yourself?"

Cui Mingyu’s cheeks flushed a light red instantly. She lowered her head quickly and whispered, "I... I’m not good at needlework, so I had to have someone else do the sewing." She paused, then hurriedly added, "But I filled it with the herbs myself. They are all good herbs for repelling mosquitoes." After saying this, she felt a bit foolish; it was just filling a sachet, why did she feel the need to explain? It was truly gilding the lily.

Xia Yuning, however, gripped the small sachet tightly, feeling as if it weighed a thousand pounds, as if it carried a profound weight of affection. A surge of indescribable warmth rose in his heart, and he asked in a low voice, "Was it made specifically for me?"

Cui Mingyu took a bite of a crystal dragon-phoenix cake. "It... it wasn't specifically for you. The Dragon Boat Festival is coming, and the maids in the manor were all making sachets. I thought it looked fun, so I made one too. I thought since your skin is fair and delicate, you must be a magnet for mosquitoes in the summer, so... so I made one for you."

Xia Yuning’s hand tightened on the sachet. He shook his head with a helpless smile and said softly, "Mingyu... you really won't say a single word to coax me."

Cui Mingyu was startled. She looked up and met Xia Yuning’s smiling eyes, only then realizing that her words had indeed been too blunt. She laughed awkwardly and quickly tried to remedy it. "That... it counts as being made specifically for you! Really!"

Seeing her earnest expression, Xia Yuning’s heart melted. He carefully tied the sachet to his waist, placing it in a conspicuous spot where he could see it by just looking down. After doing this, he suddenly reached out a hand toward Cui Mingyu.

Cui Mingyu looked at his outstretched hand, her eyes full of confusion, wondering what he was doing.

Xia Yuning’s gaze was burning as he looked steadily at her. "Mingyu, the Dragon Boat Festival is almost here. May I ask you for a five-colored string?"

Cui Mingyu was stunned at first, then a look of difficulty appeared on her face. She said with some embarrassment, "But... I don't know how to make five-colored strings. My hands are very clumsy; I can't even embroider a simple pattern, let alone braid a five-colored string."

Xia Yuning did not withdraw his hand. He continued to look at her steadily, his eyes full of expectation and persistence. "It doesn't matter, I don't mind. As long as it is made by Mingyu’s own hands, no matter what it looks like, I will be very happy."

Cui Mingyu tilted her head and thought about it. It was just a five-colored string; it shouldn't be that hard, right? The maids in the manor must know how to braid them. She could ask them for advice, and she should be able to learn quickly. Seeing the expectation in Xia Yuning’s eyes, her heart softened, and she nodded. "Well... alright. But I'll say it upfront: I’m sure it won't look good, so you aren't allowed to complain later."

A triumphant smile immediately appeared on Xia Yuning’s face. His eyes curved like a child who had received a beloved toy, and he quickly said, "How could I complain? As long as it is made by Mingyu for me, even if it were just an ordinary piece of string, I would treasure it like a precious jewel."

Watching his happy expression, Cui Mingyu couldn't help but laugh, and the small concerns in her heart vanished.

The carriage moved steadily along the road, and before long, they arrived at Yancui Lake. Xia Yuning stepped out first, then lifted the curtain and reached out a hand, gently helping Cui Mingyu down from the carriage.

As soon as Cui Mingyu stepped onto the bluestone path by the lake, she gasped in amazement at the sight before her. The lake surface was covered with lush green lotus leaves, layered and crowded together like a green ocean extending to the horizon. Countless blooming lotus flowers were dotted among the leaves—pink, white, and pale red, in a thousand different poses. Some were still in bud, like shy young girls; others were in full bloom, revealing tender yellow stamens and emitting a faint, fresh fragrance. Sunlight spilled onto the leaves and flowers, and water droplets rolled on the surfaces, refracting crystal-clear light. It truly lived up to the line, "The lotus leaves reach the sky in endless green, the lotus flowers reflect the sun in unique red."

"So beautiful!" Cui Mingyu stared in awe, unable to help but exclaim. This was the most beautiful scenery she had seen since arriving in this era.

Xia Yuning stood beside her, watching her surprised expression with gentle, smiling eyes. "I knew you would like it here, so I specially booked a painted boat. We can sit on it and slowly enjoy the beauty of the lake and mountains."

Cui Mingyu turned to look at Xia Yuning. He was always like this—no matter what he did, he arranged everything perfectly so she didn't have to worry about a thing. Being with him, she always felt an unprecedented sense of peace and security. She nodded and smiled. "Alright, let's get on the boat quickly."

The two boarded the painted boat. With a light push from the boatman, the boat drifted slowly toward the center of the lake. The boat was not large but was elegantly furnished. The cabin was covered with soft carpets and set with a few tables and chairs, with fresh fruit and snacks placed on the table. Cui Mingyu walked to the side of the boat, held the railing, and watched the lotus flowers passing slowly by. Feeling the gentle breeze blowing across the lake, with the sun not too harsh and the temperature just right, she felt all her exhaustion wash away. It was extremely pleasant.

She couldn't help but think that if Xia Yuning weren't by her side, she would really want to lie down by the side of the boat and take a nap, enjoying this rare tranquility and comfort. If she were back in the modern era, such weather and scenery would be perfect for camping—inviting three or five friends, setting up a tent by the lake, eating barbecue, and chatting; how wonderful that would be.

"Xia Yuning," Cui Mingyu turned her head to look at Xia Yuning, who was sitting to the side watching her with a smile. She couldn't help but say, "I think you are truly someone who knows how to enjoy life. Eating good food and admiring beautiful scenery—the greatest enjoyment in life probably doesn't go beyond this."

Xia Yuning smiled, his gaze burning as he looked at her, his voice so gentle it could melt. "Yes, good food and beautiful scenery are indeed refreshing. But for me, you are the most pleasing sight in this world."

Cui Mingyu’s cheeks instantly flushed, and her heartbeat quickened. Ever since she agreed to consider being with him, Xia Yuning’s sweet talk seemed to come naturally. The youth who used to blush at the slightest provocation could now easily make her ears and face burn. She lowered her head in embarrassment, avoiding his scorching gaze.

Cui Mingyu turned her head to look at the lake. By now, there were quite a few painted boats drifting on the water, in twos and threes, with constant laughter. Just as she was about to change the subject, her gaze inadvertently caught a figure on a nearby boat.

That figure... why did it look so familiar?

Cui Mingyu’s heart sank, and she thought her eyes were playing tricks on her. She steadied herself and looked carefully. On that painted boat, a man in a dark blue brocade robe was standing by the railing, his posture upright, the profile of his face sharp and distinct. It was none other than Prince Jingnan, Wei Songjun!

Why was he here? Why would he come to Yancui Lake for a boat ride?

chapters.title: Falling into the Water
chapters.content:
Cui Mingyu stumbled into the cabin of the painted boat, her heart pounding like a trapped rabbit. She barely managed to steady herself and turned to look at Xia Yuning, who was leaning against the window. "That... shouldn't we stop going forward?"

Xia Yuning looked up, his eyes clear and gentle, carrying a hint of inquiry. Cui Mingyu hurriedly looked away, pretending to be focused on the view outside. "I think the lotus flowers here are blooming beautifully—pink and white mixed together, reflecting in the clear water. It’s actually more scenic than the busy area ahead. Why don't we just stop here and rest for a while?"

Her words were half-true. The lotus pond before her was indeed clear and beautiful, with green covers and red makeup, and waves of lotus fragrance wafting through the breeze, refreshing the heart. But what truly made her want to stop immediately was the painted boat behind them that had been following at a constant distance—the dark blue figure standing at the bow, even through the layers of lotus leaves, felt like an invisible shadow that made it difficult for her to even breathe.

Xia Yuning did not notice her distress. He followed her gaze for a moment, a faint smile curling his lips. "You are right. It is quiet here, perfect for a rest and to enjoy the view." He turned to the boatman and instructed, "Boatman, please stop here for a moment."

"Understood!" the boatman replied. He gently rowed the oars, and the painted boat slowed to a stop, mooring steadily beside a patch of open lotus flowers.

Cui Mingyu nodded, her mind in turmoil, not even noticing the peeled loquat Xia Yuning was handing her. Seeing her distracted and absent-minded, Xia Yuning frowned slightly and softened his voice even more. "What's wrong? Mingyu, is something on your mind?"

Cui Mingyu snapped back to reality and met his concerned gaze. Her heart panicked, and she hurriedly squeezed out a smile, though it looked worse than a cry. "No... nothing. Perhaps I got up a bit too early today and am just a little sleepy." As she spoke, she couldn't help but secretly lift a corner of the boat curtain and take a quick glance behind them.

That one glance made her heart sink to the bottom of the abyss.

The painted boat carrying Wei Songjun had turned its direction at some point and was slowly heading toward them. The dark blue figure at the bow was still standing tall, as if staring intensely at the small boat she was on. The distance was closing, so close that she could even see the dark patterns embroidered on his hem. Cui Mingyu felt a chill rise from the soles of her feet, and her hands and feet instantly turned cold.

"Xia Yuning, I..." She turned around abruptly, her voice trembling uncontrollably. "I suddenly feel a bit unwell. I... I need to go back."

Xia Yuning was startled by her words, then stood up with concern, reaching out to touch her forehead, but Cui Mingyu subconsciously dodged away. A flicker of suspicion crossed his eyes as he followed her gaze into the distance, seeing only a vast expanse of lotus leaves reaching toward the sky, with nothing unusual to be found. Looking back at Cui Mingyu, her cheeks were pale and her eyes evasive, clearly looking guilty. Though he had his doubts, he also felt a tinge of disappointment—after all, he had arrived at the Cui residence early that morning, full of joy at the prospect of spending this lotus-viewing time with her, yet they had been here for less than half an hour before she insisted on leaving in such a rush.

However, he was always gentle and considerate. Seeing that Cui Mingyu truly did not look well, he suppressed his thoughts and said softly, "Very well, let's head back. Where do you feel unwell? Is it dizziness or nausea? Should we see a physician at the clinic first?"

Cui Mingyu knew her request was somewhat unreasonable. Xia Yuning had always been attentive to her, and today he had even specially arranged this exquisite pleasure boat just to accompany her in viewing the lotus flowers. Anyone else would have lost their temper at such a sudden interruption. Thinking of this, a wave of guilt washed over her. She lowered her head and whispered, "I'm fine, I think I'm just a bit seasick. I'll be better after resting at home. Xia Yuning, I am truly sorry... Next time, next time I will definitely treat you properly to make amends."

Watching her lowered eyelashes, the disappointment in Xia Yuning's heart was instantly replaced by tenderness. He shook his head and reached out to gently brush a stray lock of hair from her cheek, his movements so soft as if he were afraid of startling her. "It was my lack of consideration. I should have thought that you might feel unwell after being on a boat for so long. We are heading back early, so why speak of making amends? There will be plenty of time for us in the future; there are many opportunities to view the lotus, no need to rush it at this very moment."

A warmth spread through Cui Mingyu's heart. She looked up, meeting Xia Yuning's gentle eyes. His gaze was as clear as water, filled with concern and tolerance, without a hint of reproach. She thought to herself that the Dragon Boat Festival was approaching, and she must finish weaving the five-colored silk thread he wanted before the holiday. "Thank you..." she said softly, her voice tinged with a slight choke.

Xia Yuning sighed slightly, leaned in, and looked into her eyes with burning intensity. "Mingyu, you don't need to be so formal with me. I hope you can be more at ease in my presence and not feel so constrained."

His breath brushed against her cheek, carrying the faint scent of lotus, which made Cui Mingyu's heart beat even faster. She hurriedly looked away, not daring to meet his gaze again, and simply nodded slightly.

The pleasure boat slowly turned its bow and headed toward the shore. Cui Mingyu leaned against the window, watching the lotus flowers receding rapidly outside, feeling a secret regret. Such beautiful scenery—if she could calm her heart and truly appreciate it, she wouldn't feel bored even after watching it for a whole day. But it had been ruined by that bane, Wei Songjun! He didn't come early or late, but chose today to appear and ruin her good mood for the entire day.

Thinking this, she saw that the boat had traveled some distance and was getting further away from Wei Songjun's boat, so her suspended heart finally settled a little. She stood up and walked to the side of the boat, wanting to take one last look at the lotus flowers filling the lake. Just then, a unique lotus flower caught her eye.

It was a twin lotus. Two delicate lotus flowers were tightly intertwined, sharing a single stem, looking exceptionally beautiful and moving against the backdrop of green leaves. The twin lotus symbolized unity and a lifelong bond, and had always been an extremely rare and auspicious omen. Cui Mingyu was instantly captivated by this wonder, throwing all her troubles and anxieties to the winds. She turned around in surprise and called out to Xia Yuning, "Xia Yuning, look! I've found a twin lotus! Right there!"

Hearing this, Xia Yuning hurried over and looked in the direction she was pointing. The twin lotus stood elegantly amidst the emerald leaves and red blossoms, its pink and white petals layered upon one another, the edges tinged with a faint rouge color, glowing with a soft, warm light in the sunset. The two flower heads leaned against each other like whispering lovers. "It really is a twin lotus!" A smile curled his lips, his voice filled with surprise as he hinted, "This is a once-in-a-thousand-year auspicious omen, signifying a match made in heaven."

Cui Mingyu did not catch the implication in his words and said excitedly, "Shall we go closer and take a look? I've never seen a real twin lotus before!" As she spoke, she couldn't wait to move toward the side of the boat, but her foot slipped, and she stepped right over the edge, falling toward the cold lake water.

"Mingyu!" Xia Yuning exclaimed, reaching out with quick reflexes to grab her, but he only caught a piece of her sleeve, which tore away. Cui Mingyu's figure instantly vanished into the lake, leaving only ripples behind.

Xia Yuning did not hesitate; without even taking off his outer robe, he dived into the lake. The water was cool, instantly engulfing him. He struggled to search for Cui Mingyu's figure underwater, his heart filled with anxiety. Seconds ticked by, and his heart beat faster and faster, terrified that something might happen to her.

Finally, not far underwater, he saw that familiar pink figure. Cui Mingyu was struggling, bubbles constantly rising from her mouth and nose. Xia Yuning's heart tightened; he swam over, grabbed her tightly, and then fought to swim toward the surface.

The commotion they caused was so great that it drew the attention of everyone on the surrounding pleasure boats. Some gasped, some whispered, and others wanted to come over to help.

Holding Cui Mingyu, Xia Yuning finally managed to drag her onto the boat. The boatman hurriedly handed over a dry towel. Xia Yuning took it, signaled the boatman to step back, and began to gently pat Cui Mingyu's back. Cui Mingyu choked on several mouthfuls of water and coughed for a long time before she slowly recovered. Her face remained pale, but her eyes were much clearer.

However, her dress was already soaked through, clinging tightly to her skin. Summer clothing was thin to begin with, and now the wet fabric outlined her exquisite curves, her waist slender enough to be encircled by a hand, and the skin on her shoulders glowing with a lustrous sheen in the sunset. Xia Yuning had been entirely focused on saving her while in the water and hadn't noticed these things, but now that they were so close, he could clearly feel the cool touch of her body, and his nose was filled with the fresh, sweet scent of her hair mixed with the dampness of the water—a fragrance that tickled his heart like a feather.

Xia Yuning looked down at her. Her hair was plastered to her cheeks, water droplets still clinging to her long eyelashes, and her eyes held a trace of lingering shock and bewilderment. His heart rate suddenly accelerated, his hot breath fanning her face. The surrounding air seemed to freeze, leaving only the sound of their rapid, intertwined breathing.

chapters.title: Gifting a Robe
chapters.content:
"Bang!" A crisp shattering sound suddenly exploded inside the pleasure boat, like a stone thrown into a calm lake, instantly disrupting the stagnant ambiguity in the cabin. Cui Mingyu stiffened, looking at the cherries and pears rolling across the floor, then looked down at her own soaked undergarment—the thin fabric clung tightly to her body, leaving her delicate curves with nowhere to hide, and even the undried water droplets on her skin were clearly visible.

Across from her, Xia Yuning also snapped back to reality. The tension from saving her suddenly relaxed, but his earlobes uncontrollably flushed with heat, as if stained with a light red. He hurriedly looked away, his gaze fixed firmly on the water stains on the deck, his Adam's apple bobbing twice before he finally managed to choke out, "I... I'm sorry."

Cui Mingyu's cheeks were hot enough to fry an egg. She hurriedly took two steps back, wrapping her arms tightly around her chest, curling herself into a ball. Her voice was as thin as a mosquito's, filled with unconcealable shyness and apology: "Um... Xia Yuning, thank you. I... I've caused you trouble again..."

Only then did Xia Yuning lift his eyes, his gaze falling on her soaked clothes and embarrassed appearance, and the panic in his heart was instantly replaced by pity. He did not hesitate, quickly taking off his outer robe—the fabric still carried the cool warmth of his body, and though it was also soaked by the lake water, it could at least partially cover her figure. He lowered his eyes, deliberately avoiding her gaze, and gently draped the robe over Cui Mingyu, his voice as gentle as a spring breeze: "Mingyu, it is my fault. I did not protect you well, which is why you accidentally fell into the water."

Cui Mingyu clutched the fabric, her nose filled with the faint scent of pine from Xia Yuning, and that fragrance, mixed with the freshness of the lake water, actually made her panicked heart settle slightly. She buried her head and muttered softly, "It's not your fault. I was the one who was greedy for the lotus flowers and accidentally missed my footing..."

Xia Yuning frowned, his gaze sinking as he looked at her soaked skirt, his expression becoming increasingly grave. If Cui Mingyu returned to the city in this state, the gossip of those long-tongued women would likely drown her—although the Great Qi dynasty had relatively open social customs, an unmarried girl being seen in such a state with a man would be branded with the charge of "loss of virtue," enough to ruin a girl's reputation for life.

Cui Mingyu also thought of this, and her heart sank. She made a bitter face, muttering to herself, *It's over, it's over. I didn't bring a change of clothes when I left. If I go back like this, I'll really become famous in this capital, and I'm afraid my original father would be too ashamed to face anyone...*

"Don't panic," Xia Yuning said softly. "I will have the boatman head to the shore. You wait in the cabin for a moment, and I will immediately have someone ride at full speed to the city to buy you a new set of clothes. It won't take long."

This was the safest method for the moment. Sure enough, a man who could solve problems was charming. Just as Cui Mingyu was about to nod in agreement, she suddenly heard a crisp, melodious voice from outside the boat, ringing like a mountain spring: "Is Miss Cui here?"

Who was it? The voice sounded familiar. Cui Mingyu frowned slightly, searching her memory—at the last poetry gathering, the First Talented Woman, Mu Wanzhou, who wore a moon-white dress and had a gentle temperament, had just such a clear voice.

She hurriedly lifted the cabin curtain and poked her head out. She saw another pleasure boat, even more exquisite than theirs, moored alongside. Standing at the bow was a young girl in a plain white dress—it was indeed Mu Wanzhou. The girl stood amidst the lotus breeze, her white clothes fluttering lightly, a simple silver hairpin in her hair, her eyebrows curved, and her smile as gentle as the lotus flowers in the pond.

Seeing Cui Mingyu poke her head out, a flash of understanding crossed Mu Wanzhou's eyes. She then signaled the maid behind her to hand over a neatly folded bundle of clothing. "Miss Cui, I think you might just happen to need this."

Cui Mingyu reached out to take it. The fabric felt like soft, smooth cloud brocade. When she unfolded it, she saw it was a wide, long robe, seemingly in a masculine style. The robe was a plain, clean moon-white, which would not look out of place on a woman. The material was of high quality, and it was faintly permeated with a cool, deep agarwood scent—a fragrance that was cold yet mellow, carrying an undeniable air of nobility.

Her heart was full of doubts—why would Mu Wanzhou be so kind? They had only met once at the poetry gathering, and she had even stolen Mu Wanzhou's spotlight. By rights, the other girl should hold a grudge against her; why would she go out of her way to send clothes to help her?

Cui Mingyu subconsciously turned to look at Xia Yuning beside her. Their eyes met, and both saw the same confusion and bewilderment in each other's gaze.

But right now, she was in dire need of this robe to cover herself; she couldn't keep wrapped in Xia Yuning’s wet outer garment forever. After a moment’s hesitation, Cui Mingyu offered Mu Wanzhou a grateful smile, bowed with cupped hands, and said, "Many thanks to Miss Mu for this timely help. Mingyu will remember this kindness."

Mu Wanzhou pursed her lips and smiled, her eyes dancing with a touch of clever playfulness. "Miss Cui, you are thanking the wrong person. I am merely borrowing flowers to offer to Buddha; this robe is not mine."

Borrowing flowers to offer to Buddha? A thought stirred in Cui Mingyu’s mind as she clutched the robe and hurried into the cabin. The robe was indeed oversized; on her, the hem nearly dragged on the floor, and the sleeves were far too long, making her look like a child playing dress-up in an adult’s clothes. She struggled to roll up the sleeves before lifting the cabin curtain to step out.

Xia Yuning followed closely behind her, and the two walked to the bow of the boat. A breeze blew by, carrying the faint fragrance of the lotus pond. Cui Mingyu looked toward the pleasure boat behind Mu Wanzhou. Upon closer inspection, her pupils suddenly constricted—she had seen the style of this boat before! It was precisely Wei Songjun’s pleasure boat!

Then, this robe, which smelled of sinking incense... could it be Wei Songjun’s?

As soon as this thought occurred, Cui Mingyu was startled. Wei Songjun had always loathed her; it was a miracle he hadn't taken her life, so why would he lend her his robe to save her dignity? Could this be a trap?

Hesitation clouded her mind, but she mustered the courage to bow to Mu Wanzhou once more, her tone sincere: "Miss Mu, may I ask whose robe this is? Once I have washed and dried it, I will certainly return it in person and offer my thanks!"

No sooner had she finished speaking than a cold, piercing voice came from the cabin behind Mu Wanzhou, striking like an ice pick, devoid of any warmth: "Since the robe is soiled, just throw it away. There is no need to return it."

It was Wei Songjun’s voice! Cui Mingyu shuddered, recoiling two steps in fright, and nearly slipped. Xia Yuning was quick to react, reaching out to steady her arm. Once she was standing firm, he looked toward the other cabin, bowed, and spoke with a respectful yet measured tone: "So it was the Prince who acted with such chivalry. Xia will remember this favor and will surely repay it in the future!"

"Don't get involved!" Cui Mingyu quickly grabbed Xia Yuning’s sleeve, lowering her voice urgently. "This is my business, it has nothing to do with you! That Wei Songjun is no good; stay away from him so you don't get schemed against!"

She thought she was speaking quietly, unaware that Wei Songjun in the cabin heard every word clearly. The next second, that cold voice came again, laced with heavy mockery and disdain: "There is no need for thanks. I simply cannot stand the sight of certain people—an unmarried man and woman alone in a room, pulling and tugging at each other, showing no sense of shame! It is a disgrace to the reputation of noble families. If the common people were to see this, they would think the imperial court raised a group of people who offend public decency!"

Cui Mingyu’s face flushed red. Just as she was about to argue with him, Xia Yuning pulled her behind him.

Xia Yuning looked toward the cabin, his tone remaining polite: "The Prince is mistaken. As the old saying goes, 'A fair lady is a good match for a gentleman.' My affection for Mingyu is an honorable matter. Today’s events were merely due to an accidental fall into the water, which led to these misunderstandings. My relationship with Mingyu is pure and transparent; there is absolutely no 'illicit' intent. I ask the Prince to be careful with his words, lest he tarnish Mingyu’s reputation."

"Pure and transparent?" Wei Songjun inside the cabin chewed on these words, his tone dripping with sarcasm, before letting out a cold snort and falling silent.

A moment later, the boatman slowly docked the pleasure boat at the shore. Just as Cui Mingyu was about to disembark, she suddenly remembered that Xia Yuning’s clothes were also mostly wet. If he were to take her back while still wet, he might catch a cold. As she worried about this, Mu Wanzhou spoke up at the right moment, her smile remaining gentle: "If Miss Cui doesn't mind, why not return to the city with me? It is on the way, and it will save Young Master Xia the trouble of another trip."

Cui Mingyu felt a warmth in her heart and nodded quickly: "Thank you, Miss Mu, you truly are my savior!"

Xia Yuning also breathed a sigh of relief and bowed to Mu Wanzhou: "In that case, many thanks to Miss Mu. I will certainly call on you another day to express my gratitude."

"Young Master Xia is too polite, it was but a small effort," Mu Wanzhou said with a faint smile.

As they stepped onto the shore, Wei Songjun emerged from the cabin. He wore a dark blue brocade robe, his posture as straight as a pine, his expression cold and stern, his brows furrowed, radiating an icy aura that kept others at a distance. From start to finish, he never once looked directly at Cui Mingyu, as if she were mere air.

Cui Mingyu watched his retreating figure, her confusion deepening—Wei Songjun’s actions today were truly too abnormal. What was his purpose in helping her? Did he want her to owe him a favor so he could manipulate her later? Or... was there some other reason?

Regardless, he had lent her his clothes and helped her out of a predicament, and she had to accept this kindness. After a moment of hesitation, Cui Mingyu gathered her courage, stepped forward, and bowed slightly toward Wei Songjun: "Your Highness, thank you for the robe today. I will certainly make a new one and send it to you to repay this kindness."

Wei Songjun paused and looked down at her. The young girl was wearing the oversized moon-white robe, which made her figure appear even more slender. Her face was somewhat pale from falling into the water, yet it could not hide her delicate beauty. Her almond-shaped eyes were bright, filled with a touch of stubbornness and sincerity.

"Forget it. I only did it for the sake of Minister Cui. I should be asking Minister Cui for this favor, not you."

As expected, Cui Mingyu ground her teeth in frustration; he was targeting her father.

chapters.title: You Are Not Worthy
chapters.content:
Cui Mingyu lay slumped in Mu Wanzhou’s elegantly decorated carriage, her mind replaying the words Wei Songjun had said before leaving like a carousel.

"Despicable!" she couldn't help but grit out, the word low but filled with resentment.

"What was that?"

A soft, surprised question came from beside her. Cui Mingyu snapped back to reality and realized Mu Wanzhou was looking at her with eyes as clear as water, filled with innocent confusion. She realized she had spoken out of turn, her cheeks heating up slightly. She waved her hand awkwardly, forcing a smile that looked worse than a cry: "Oh... Miss Mu, I wasn't talking about you! I was just... just suddenly lamenting my tragic fate. It has nothing to do with you, really!"

Hearing this, Mu Wanzhou couldn't help but cover her mouth and laugh softly. The smile was gentle and moving, like a breeze brushing across a lake in spring. "Miss Cui is quite humorous. Such self-deprecation makes you seem remarkably candid."

Cui Mingyu breathed a sigh of relief; fortunately, this heroine wasn't the type to overthink things. She steadied herself, and her curiosity flared up again. She cautiously probed: "By the way, Miss Mu, how did you end up coming to admire the lotus with the Prince of Jingnan today?"

At the mention of Wei Songjun, a faint blush spread across Mu Wanzhou’s cheeks like the evening glow on the horizon. She lowered her eyes, her voice as thin as a mosquito’s: "We just happened to meet here today, so we sat together for a while. It was... just a coincidence."

A coincidence? Cui Mingyu rolled her eyes internally. How could there be so many coincidences? They must have arranged it beforehand. It seemed that even without the original vicious female supporting character stirring up trouble, the two of them would naturally gravitate toward each other—this must be the protagonist's halo! She glanced at Mu Wanzhou’s shy, spring-struck expression, and the genes of the original vicious character began to stir—she really wanted to trip Wei Songjun up so he wouldn't win the beauty so easily!

But then, thinking of the original owner’s fate—being tortured by Wei Songjun until not even a corpse remained—Cui Mingyu couldn't help but shudder. Forget it, forget it! Her life was more important! In this life, she only wanted to stay away from the hero and heroine and live her own quiet, peaceful life. He had his "white moonlight," and she would have her own ideal husband. To each their own, living in peace without disturbing one another was the best way.

She cleared her throat, plastered a "sincere" smile on her face, and said with exaggerated tone: "Oh, Miss Mu, don't be so modest! Seeing you two today, you are truly a match made in heaven! A talented man and a beautiful woman, standing together like a picture—you are perfectly suited!"

At these words, Mu Wanzhou’s face turned even redder, like a ripe apple. She waved her hands in a panic: "Miss Cui, you... please don't tease me! It’s really not what you think between the Prince and me!" She paused, as if remembering something, her eyes flickering slightly, and she said softly: "Actually... today, I felt that the Prince was unusually different toward you, Miss Cui."

Cui Mingyu was stunned: "Me?"

"Yes," Mu Wanzhou nodded, saying earnestly, "The Prince is usually cold by nature and doesn't like to meddle in others' affairs, but today, after you fell into the water, he took the initiative to give you his own robe." A man giving his robe to a woman—the implications were always thought-provoking.

Hearing this, Cui Mingyu couldn't help but sigh, her face showing an expression of utter hopelessness: "Miss Mu, please don't misunderstand! The Prince only helped me reluctantly for the sake of my father. You saw it yourself; he looked at me with disdain and didn't even spare me a glance! I did many foolish things before that annoyed him, and now I just hope he is magnanimous enough not to hold a grudge against a small woman like me. That would be a blessing."

Mu Wanzhou looked at her "remorseful" expression, a hint of hesitation flashing in her eyes as she probed: "Miss Cui, I heard... that you used to be deeply in love with the Prince..."

"Oh, that’s all ancient history!" Cui Mingyu waved her hand, her tone firm and decisive. "Times have changed, and I’ve long since come to my senses! That was just youthful ignorance and foolishness. Thinking back on it now, I truly regret it! Miss Mu, you are close to the Prince; if you have the chance in the future, I hope you can put in a good word for me, so he might overlook my youth and ignorance and stop holding a grudge."

Her words neatly distanced herself from Wei Songjun while subtly pushing Mu Wanzhou toward him—it was killing two birds with one stone.

Mu Wanzhou listened with a thoughtful expression. After a moment of silence, she asked softly: "By the way, Miss Cui, I saw you and Young Master Xia playing by the lotus pond today. You and Young Master Xia..."

At the mention of Xia Yuning, Cui Mingyu’s eyes lit up instantly. The gloom on her face vanished, replaced by a gentle smile: "He is a very good person—gentle, considerate, well-read, and he takes great care of me." She paused, adding firmly, "In my opinion, he... is someone worth entrusting my life to."

The four words "worthy of trust" clearly stated her position. She had transmigrated into this book, not to repeat the original owner's mistakes. Since she already had a reliable, handsome man like Xia Yuning, she wouldn't be foolish enough to revolve around that big ice block, Wei Songjun, ever again!

Meanwhile, beside Yancui Lake, Xia Yuning stood where he was, watching Wei Songjun prepare to board his carriage. His brows were tightly knitted, and his eyes held a hint of confusion.

"Your Highness," he began, his voice cold and clear, "you could have stood by and watched today's events. Why did you give your robe to Mingyu?"

Wei Songjun’s footsteps halted. He turned slowly, his gaze falling upon Xia Yuning. His eyes were indifferent, his tone calm: "I have already stated the reason. Does Young Master Xia wish for me to repeat it?"

Xia Yuning gave a light smile. In his view, the reason Wei Songjun gave was far too high-sounding and held no water. Xia Yuning straightened his back and met Wei Songjun's gaze without fear: "Your Highness, Mingyu and I have already made a one-year agreement. In one year, she will marry me as my wife. The person she admires now is no longer Your Highness. Could it be that Your Highness is regretting it because Mingyu has changed her mind?"

Upon hearing this, Wei Songjun suddenly let out a low laugh, a sound tinged with playfulness and a touch of contempt. He walked step by step toward Xia Yuning, looking down at him from his height, his eyes as sharp as blades: "Indeed, a newborn calf is not afraid of the tiger; you certainly have a lot of nerve. Even your father, the Marquis of Changning, would not dare speak to me in such a manner."

Xia Yuning’s face turned slightly pale, but he persisted, "I am merely speaking of the matter as it stands. Why does Your Highness not dare to respond to my question directly?"

Wei Songjun raised an eyebrow, the mockery in his eyes deepening: "Xia Yuning, compared to that straw-bag brother of yours, Xia Yu'an, you do have more backbone and a bit more capability. It is a pity, however, that you are, after all, the son of a secondary wife. Your father, Xia Chang, would rather have you go into business than allow you to enter the officialdom, all to secure the position of his legitimate heir. I can understand that you wish to use Cui Mingyu to climb the great tree of Cui Yong to carve out a path for yourself."

He paused, his gaze locking onto Xia Yuning’s eyes, and said word for word: "But there are some things that, if you pretend too much, you start to believe yourself."

Xia Yuning’s face turned deathly pale in an instant. His body trembled slightly, his eyes filled with shock and panic: "You... you are spouting nonsense! My feelings for Mingyu are sincere! I have never thought of using her!"

"Whether your feelings are sincere or fake, I do not care." Wei Songjun withdrew his gaze and said in an indifferent tone, "I will warn you only once: do not attempt to guess my thoughts. You... are not qualified!"

Having said this, he did not spare Xia Yuning another glance, turned, and boarded his carriage, leaving Xia Yuning standing alone, his face pale, his expression complex, motionless for a long time.

chapters.title: The Pawnshop
chapters.content:
When Cui Mingyu returned to the Cui residence, her mind felt as heavy as a ball of water-soaked cotton. She had Qinghe and Bitao fetch hot water. The steam from the hot water soon filled the entire bathing room, and only when Cui Mingyu submerged herself in the warm water did her tightly strung nerves finally relax. The warmth slowly dispelled the chill from her limbs. She leaned against the edge of the tub, her gaze drifting involuntarily toward the moon-white robe draped over the screen.

It was Wei Songjun’s.

She didn't want to owe him any favors. Didn't he despise the robe for being "soiled" after covering her body? Then she would make him a new one, exactly the same! That would save him from using this matter to claim credit before her father.

After her bath, Cui Mingyu felt much more refreshed. She told Qinghe to wash the wet robe. As luck would have it, the sun was bright that day, and it dried completely after an afternoon in the sun. Early the next morning, Cui Mingyu tucked the robe under her arm and headed straight for the capital's most famous tailor shop, "Jinxiu Pavilion," with Bitao.

As soon as she entered, a clerk greeted her enthusiastically: "Miss, please come in. What would you like to see? Are you looking to make new clothes or alter old ones?"

Cui Mingyu placed the robe on the counter and said with great confidence: "Clerk, help me make one exactly like this, identical in every way."

The clerk looked down, his eyes widening into circles, his hands beginning to tremble: "M-Miss, are you joking? This... this is Zhuanghua cloud brocade! It’s even woven with gold thread inside—truly worth its weight in gold! Are you certain you want to make this?"

Cui Mingyu was startled by his reaction, her heart skipping a beat: "Then... how much would it cost to make one like this?"

The clerk held up five fingers: "At least five hundred taels of silver."

"Pfft—" Cui Mingyu felt as if she were about to spit out a mouthful of blood, and her vision went dark. Five hundred taels? Her monthly allowance was only five taels, and her father, Minister Cui’s annual salary combined might not even reach five hundred taels! That bastard Wei Songjun, how could a single piece of clothing be worth five hundred taels? How was she supposed to pay him back?
