Cui Mingyu wore a bitter expression, her fingers unconsciously scratching the edge of the counter as her mind raced. She definitely couldn't come up with five hundred taels. Should she just let it go? No, she couldn't swallow this insult!

"Um..." Cui Mingyu looked up, a glimmer of hope in her eyes, "This cloud brocade... are there any similar substitutes? Something that looks about the same but is cheaper?"

The clerk’s eyes darted around, and he immediately put on a mysterious expression, leaning close to Cui Mingyu’s ear to whisper: "Miss, you’ve asked the right person! We do have a type of brocade satin in the shop. The color is similar to yours, and it’s also embroidered with gold thread. If you don't look closely, you can't tell the difference at all. An ordinary person would absolutely never know!"

"An ordinary person..." Cui Mingyu felt doubtful. Wei Songjun was no ordinary person; he was the Prince of Jingnan, a man of vast experience. What if he noticed?

The clerk saw her hesitation and quickly added fuel to the fire: "Don't worry, Miss! Unless you are a professional embroiderer, you absolutely won't see any flaws! The luster and texture of this brocade satin are not much different from cloud brocade!"

Cui Mingyu pondered this and felt the clerk had a point. Wei Songjun was a grown man, a prince, busy with a thousand things every day—where would he find the time to study whether the fabric of a robe was cloud brocade or brocade satin? He couldn't possibly compare the clothes with an embroiderer, could he?

"Fine! Then use this brocade satin!" Cui Mingyu made her decision. "How much for this one?"

The clerk held up one finger.

"Ten taels?" Cui Mingyu’s eyes lit up.

The clerk shook his head, his smile a bit awkward: "Miss, it’s one hundred taels."

"One hundred taels?!" Cui Mingyu’s face fell instantly. "Why is it so expensive? Can you make it cheaper? How about fifty taels?"

"Miss, this is already the lowest price!" The clerk looked troubled. "This brocade satin is also a top-tier material, and it has to be intricately embroidered according to the pattern you provided. One hundred taels really isn't expensive—you get what you pay for!"

Cui Mingyu haggled with the clerk for a long time, but he remained unmoved and refused to lower the price. Cui Mingyu gritted her teeth, thinking that to save face, one hundred taels it was! She pulled out the only ten taels of silver she had from her pocket and slapped it on the counter: "Fine! Ten taels as a deposit, and I will pay the remaining ninety taels in a few days! You must remember the pattern exactly; not a single detail can be wrong!"

"Don't worry, Miss!" The clerk immediately found the shop's best embroiderer and had her carefully note the style, pattern, and measurements of the robe, fearing any mistake.

After paying the deposit, Cui Mingyu looked at her empty purse and began to worry again. Where would the remaining ninety taels come from? Xia Yuning certainly wasn't short on money, but she didn't want to ask him. As for her father, if he knew what she was doing, he certainly wouldn't approve.

"Miss, what should we do?" Bitao was also pacing anxiously. "We can't ask the Master, can we? If the Master finds out you spent one hundred taels to make a robe for the Prince of Jingnan, he’ll be furious!"

Cui Mingyu frowned, her gaze unintentionally falling on the cloud brocade robe of Wei Songjun’s in her hand. Suddenly, her eyes lit up as if she had thought of a brilliant idea.

"Bitao," Cui Mingyu lowered her voice, her eyes sparkling with cunning, "tell me... if we pawned this robe, how much could we get for it?"

Bitao was shocked, her mouth opening wide enough to fit an egg: "Miss! Are you crazy? This is the Prince of Jingnan’s clothing! If you pawn it and he finds out, we’ll be in big trouble!"

"What’s there to be afraid of!" Cui Mingyu waved her hand dismissively. "Didn't he say this robe was dirty and he wanted to throw it away? Since he doesn't want it, it’s my property now! It’s worth five hundred taels; what a waste it would be to throw it away! If I pawn it, I’ll have just enough to pay for the new robe. It kills two birds with one stone!"

Bitao was still hesitant: "But... this is the Prince’s item after all, what if..."

"There are no 'what ifs'!" Cui Mingyu interrupted her, pulling her outside. The two chose the Ruifeng Pawnshop. When the clerk saw Cui Mingyu and Bitao enter, he hurried over: "Young ladies, are you here to pawn something?"

Cui Mingyu handed over the cloud brocade robe: "Take a look at this. How much can you pawn it for?"

The clerk took the robe. At first, he was indifferent, but when he saw the material and the craftsmanship, his expression changed instantly. He scrambled to fold the robe and lowered his voice to Cui Mingyu: "Miss, this... I cannot make the decision. I must ask our head manager to take a look."

Cui Mingyu felt suspicious: It’s just a piece of clothing, isn't it? Is it worth such a fuss? Could there be something special about this robe?

Soon, a head manager wearing a long gown and sporting a goatee came out. He took the robe from the clerk, examined it carefully for a long time, and flipped it over to check the embroidery on the collar and cuffs. His expression grew increasingly solemn.

"Miss," the head manager looked up, his gaze sharp as he looked at Cui Mingyu, "how much silver are you looking to pawn this item for?"

Cui Mingyu had no idea. The original price of the robe was five hundred taels, but it had been worn, so it must have depreciated. She thought for a moment, feeling that three hundred taels would be quite good, but to leave room for the manager to haggle, she tremblingly held up five fingers, her voice lacking confidence: "F-five hundred taels?"

After saying this, she looked at the head manager nervously, fearing he would refuse outright.

But to her surprise, the head manager nodded without changing his expression, put the robe away, and asked: "Miss, is this a temporary pawn or a permanent sale?"

"Permanent sale! Permanent sale!" Cui Mingyu said quickly, fearing he might change his mind. A temporary pawn would require redeeming it, and she wasn't about to make such a losing deal!

The head manager asked again: "Miss, would you like silver notes or cash?"

Cui Mingyu was completely stunned. This manager... he didn't even haggle? Based on her knowledge of pawnshops, three hundred taels would have been a sky-high price. He had agreed to five hundred taels just like that? This was practically a windfall from the heavens!

Cui Mingyu swallowed hard, suppressing the excitement in her heart, and tried to make her voice sound as calm as possible: "That... give me one hundred taels in cash, and exchange the remaining four hundred taels for silver notes."

"Very well, Miss, please wait a moment." The head manager turned to the back of the counter and soon returned with a four-hundred-tael silver note and one hundred taels of cash. He also handed over a pawn ticket. "Miss, please sign and affix your thumbprint."

Cui Mingyu picked up the brush, casually wrote the name "Su San," then took the money and the pawn ticket, grabbed Bitao, and ran out of the pawnshop impatiently.

As soon as they were out of the pawnshop, Bitao couldn't help but shriek: "Miss! We made a fortune! Five hundred taels! A whole five hundred taels! This is enough for us to live on for many years!"

Cui Mingyu was also beaming, her smile stretching from ear to ear. She finally understood why some people in modern society were obsessed with digging through trash cans in wealthy neighborhoods—look, a piece of cloth casually discarded by a rich person was worth so much! Five hundred taels was enough to cover her monthly allowance for 500 months, which was over forty years of expenses!

"Let's go, Bitao! Let's go buy something delicious!" In high spirits, Cui Mingyu grabbed Bitao and ran off.

Watching the backs of Cui Mingyu and Bitao as they walked away, the head manager immediately folded the cloud-brocade robe carefully, wrapped it in a piece of fine silk, and instructed a shop assistant beside him: "Follow that young lady immediately, find out her identity and address, and come back quickly!"

The assistant took the order and left, returning shortly after. He said respectfully to the head manager: "Manager, I've found out. That young lady is the eldest daughter of Minister Cui's mansion, Cui Mingyu."

The head manager nodded, picked up the package, and said to the assistant: "Prepare the carriage! We're going to the Prince Jingnan's mansion!"

chapters.title: Headache
chapters.content:
The study of Prince Jingnan's mansion always exuded a quiet scent of ink. Wei Songjun was reclining on a rosewood daybed, holding a volume of *Zhuangzi* (Nanhuajing). His gaze rested on the pages, and not even the drifting clouds outside the window could distract him in the slightest.

It wasn't until a steady sound of footsteps approached from afar and stopped outside the study door that he spoke without looking up, his voice carrying a touch of indifferent laziness: "What is it?"

The steward outside the door bowed and replied: "Your Highness, Manager Zhou from the Ruifeng Pawnshop is here, saying he has an urgent matter to see you."

Wei Songjun's fingers, which were turning the pages, paused, and his eyebrows arched slightly. "Let him in."

The door was pushed open gently. Manager Zhou walked in carrying a dark blue silk package. As soon as he crossed the threshold, he bowed, his posture respectful to the point of caution: "Greetings, Your Highness. Today, our shop received a pawned item. I truly couldn't make a decision, so after much thought, I felt I had to ask for your judgment."

Manager Zhou of the Ruifeng Pawnshop was someone he had personally selected—shrewd, capable, and well-informed. Ordinary pawned items had never caused him to make such a formal trip to the mansion.

Wei Songjun finally put down the book and raised his eyes to look at him, his ink-colored eyes filled with a hint of inquiry: "Oh? What is it that has troubled you so much?"

Manager Zhou quickly opened the package in his hands and gently handed over the clothing inside. It was a moon-white cloud-brocade robe. The fabric was as smooth as a mirror, and the collar and cuffs were embroidered with exquisite dark-patterned gold thread, shimmering with a soft luster in the light of the study.

The moment Wei Songjun saw the robe, his expression sank abruptly. He remembered this robe clearly; it was the one he had thrown at Cui Mingyu yesterday! He had told her to throw it away, but he never expected she would actually dare to discard it, let alone pawn it the moment she turned around!

Observing his reaction and seeing his darkening expression, Manager Zhou quickly explained: "Your Highness, I recognized at a glance that this was your garment. I wanted to refuse it directly, but the person who came to pawn it was a young lady. I was afraid that if I refused her outright, it might damage your reputation if word got out, so I accepted it first and came here without delay to seek your instructions."

Wei Songjun reached out and picked up the cloud-brocade robe, the corners of his mouth curling into a cold arc. A fine Cui Mingyu indeed; she had quite the nerve to actually take his things to a pawnshop for money!

"Your Highness, please calm your anger." Sensing the low pressure surrounding him, Manager Zhou added quickly, "That young lady pawned it for five hundred taels of silver. I have already sent someone to investigate, and she is the eldest daughter of Minister Cui of the Ministry of Revenue, Cui Mingyu."

"Cui Mingyu..." Wei Songjun chewed on the three words in a low voice, his tone full of gnashing teeth, as if he wanted to crush the name and swallow it. He pondered for a moment, looked up at Manager Zhou, and his tone returned to calm: "I understand. You did well in this matter. You may go now; leave the robe here."

"Yes, Your Highness." Manager Zhou breathed a sigh of relief, bowed, and retreated, gently closing the study door behind him.

Wei Songjun was left alone in the study. He stared at the moon-white cloud-brocade robe, feeling more and more irritated the longer he looked at it. He tossed the book in his hand onto the table; the pages scattered, and he could no longer read a single word. As expected of the daughter of Minister of Revenue Cui Yong, she was truly obsessed with money—she even dared to pawn his belongings!

Meanwhile, in her boudoir at the Cui mansion, Cui Mingyu was holding the five-hundred-tael silver note, her eyes crinkled into slits with joy. She gently stroked the texture of the note, her heart blooming with happiness. It felt so good to be rich; from now on, she could buy whatever she wanted and would never have to look at anyone else's face again!

When she had dinner with her father, Cui Yong, that evening, Cui Mingyu noticed that her father looked unwell, his brows tightly locked, appearing deeply troubled. Her heart skipped a beat, fearing that Wei Songjun had told her father about the incident yesterday where she fell into the lake and he gifted her the robe. She carefully put down her chopsticks and asked softly: "Father, did you encounter any troublesome matters at court today?"

Cui Yong rubbed his throbbing temples, his tone somewhat weary: "Nothing much, just some trifles at court, I'm just tired."

Cui Mingyu was still worried. After hesitating for a moment, she asked in a low voice: "Then... did Prince Jingnan say anything to you today?"

Hearing this, Cui Yong frowned and looked up at her: "Mingzhu, why are you still thinking about Prince Jingnan? Didn't you tell me a few days ago that you had your eye on that boy from the Xia family?"

Hearing her father say this, the heart that had been hanging in Cui Mingyu's chest instantly dropped. It seemed Wei Songjun hadn't told her father anything; perhaps he didn't know about the incident, or if he did, he couldn't be bothered to care. She quickly laughed: "No, no, I was just asking casually. Seeing that you were in a bad mood, I thought you had encountered something unpleasant!"

Cui Yong sighed and took a sip from his teacup: "It's nothing, just my old headache acting up. I'll be fine after some rest."

Cui Mingyu quickly stood up, walked to her father's side, and said with a smile: "Father, let me massage it for you; it might help alleviate it." In her modern life, her grandmother had also suffered from chronic headaches, and she had specifically learned some basic massage techniques from an old traditional Chinese medicine practitioner. She hadn't expected it to come in handy today.

Cui Yong was stunned for a moment, then nodded: "Alright, then I'll trouble my Mingzhu."

Cui Mingyu stretched out her fingers and pressed them gently onto her father's temples, kneading slowly according to the techniques the old practitioner had taught her. Her pressure was just right—neither too light to be ineffective, nor too heavy to be uncomfortable.

Cui Yong closed his eyes, enjoying his daughter's massage. His originally tense brows gradually smoothed out, and he kept muttering: "Mingzhu has grown up and knows how to care for her father. I really can't bear to see you get married; if only you could stay by my side forever."

Hearing this, Cui Mingyu smiled mischievously: "Does that mean if your daughter were disobedient, you'd be eager to marry me off early, out of sight and out of mind?"

Cui Yong opened his eyes and glared at her: "You girl, what nonsense are you spouting! No matter what, you are always Father's precious daughter!"

As the father and daughter chatted and laughed, Cui Mingyu continued to massage for a while. Cui Yong felt his originally throbbing head become much lighter, and his spirits lifted significantly. He looked at his daughter in surprise: "Mingzhu, where did you learn this massage technique? The effect is so good; my headache has truly eased a lot."

Cui Mingyu had already prepared her story and replied with a smile: "A while ago, I met a traveling old doctor on the street. Seeing that his medical skills were good, I learned a few massage techniques from him. I thought that since you often have headaches, it might help you, and I didn't expect it to actually work."

These words warmed Cui Yong's heart, and his eyes even grew a little moist. His daughter was not only sensible but also so filial; it was truly his blessing. That night, when Cui Yong returned to his room, he hugged his wife's spirit tablet and wept again, murmuring that their daughter had grown up and his wife could rest easy.

The next morning, Cui Yong went to court in high spirits, his face glowing, without a trace of the haggard look he usually had when suffering from a headache. His colleagues saw him and gathered around in surprise: "Minister Cui, what has happened to you? You looked so haggard yesterday; we thought you would ask the Emperor for leave to rest today!"

Cui Yong smiled triumphantly, his tone full of pride: "It's all thanks to my Mingzhu. She specifically learned some massage techniques from an old doctor and massaged me for a while yesterday. I slept through the night, and my headache is completely gone!"

That colleague quickly flattered him: "Minister Cui, you are truly blessed! Your daughter is not only beautiful as a flower, but she also won the best poem at the poetry gathering a few days ago, and now she is so filial and sensible—truly gifted in both talent and appearance. I think the threshold of your mansion will be worn down by suitors in the future!"

Cui Yong was overjoyed by the praise, though he waved his hands repeatedly: "You flatter me, you flatter me. She's just a child, still ignorant." But in his heart, he was already blooming with joy, wishing he could tell everyone about how wonderful his daughter was.

Not far away, Wei Songjun saw and heard everything. He lowered his eyes, masking the expression in them, while the corners of his mouth slowly curled into a meaningful smile.

As it happened, he also suffered from chronic headaches and had been troubled by them for years. Cui Mingyu had pawned his cloud-brocade robe and obtained five hundred taels of silver; this debt could not be settled just like that.

Since she was so good at massage, that was perfect—it would serve as the interest on her debt.

chapters.title: The Secret Exposed
chapters.content:
Two days later, the assistant from the Jinxiu Pavilion finally delivered the imitation of that "sky-high price" robe to the Cui mansion. As soon as Cui Mingyu received the heavy brocade box, her eyes lit up instantly. She didn't even bother to put down her teacup, but instead pulled Qinghe to the window to examine it carefully in the daylight.

"My god, this craftsmanship is absolutely stunning!" The more Cui Mingyu looked, the more satisfied she became. She couldn't help but reach out and gently stroke the fabric and the patterns embroidered with gold thread; even the stitches were so fine they were almost invisible. This Jinxiu Pavilion was indeed the number one tailor shop in the capital—it lived up to its reputation!

She compared the newly made robe with the memory of the old one repeatedly, from the curve of the collar to the piping on the cuffs, and then to the pattern of the hidden embroidery on the hem. Compared to the original she had pawned, it was not exactly the same, but it was at least ninety percent similar. If the two robes were not placed side by side, anyone would assume they were the same one.

Cui Mingyu happily paid the remaining balance and watched the young shop assistant leave with profuse thanks, her mental abacus clicking away. Last time, she had gotten five hundred taels for the old robe; this time, she spent one hundred taels to return the favor, netting a profit of four hundred taels. This deal was an absolute steal!

Thinking that Qinghe was reliable and tight-lipped, Cui Mingyu handed her the brocade box, patted her on the shoulder, and instructed, "Qinghe, help me take this robe to the Prince Jingnan’s mansion. Just say... say that I had it specially remade for the Prince and ask him to accept it. Remember, be respectful and don't give him any reason to find fault."

Qinghe took the brocade box and nodded solemnly, "Don't worry, Miss, I will certainly handle it."

But who would have thought that less than an hour after Qinghe left, she would return, carrying the brocade box just as it was, looking furious. Her cheeks were flushed red, and she looked as if she had suffered a great injustice: "Miss, the people at Prince Jingnan’s mansion are too much! I didn't even get to see the Prince; I was stopped at the door by a servant who said arrogantly—'Our Prince said, showing gratitude requires a proper attitude. If you don't come to thank him in person, where is the sincerity?'"

"Pfft—" Cui Mingyu spat out half the plum juice she had just taken, nearly choking herself into a coughing fit, tears welling up in her eyes.

Wei Songjun, that bastard, actually wanted her to come and thank him in person?!

She rolled her eyes hard. In her mind, Wei Songjun’s cold face appeared instantly. Every time she saw him, he either looked at her through his nostrils or down his chin, his gaze suggesting she was some sort of lowly filth not worth a second glance.

What was wrong with him? She didn't go in person precisely because she didn't want to annoy him.

She recalled the last time she went to Prince Jingnan’s mansion, he had forced her to drink an aphrodisiac and left her soaking in an ice bucket for the whole night, causing her to be bedridden—well, "bedridden for half a month," as she claimed.

"Didn't we turn the page on that? What kind of twisted scheme is he playing now?" The more Cui Mingyu thought about it, the angrier she became. Grinding her back teeth, she slammed the brocade box onto the table. "Returning a favor to this villain is harder than paying off a loan shark!"

Seeing her anger, Qinghe stepped forward and advised worriedly, "Miss, please don't be angry. How about... when the Master returns, you go to Prince Jingnan’s mansion with him? The Prince has to give the Master some face and wouldn't dare bully you."

Bitao also nodded repeatedly from the side, echoing with lingering fear, "Yes, yes! With the Master there, no matter how arrogant Prince Jingnan is, he wouldn't dare do anything to you! We really can't rest easy if you go alone, what if he does what he did last time..."

"Alright, that's enough." Cui Mingyu interrupted Bitao and shook her head slowly. She didn't want to trouble her father with these personal matters or let it affect his political affairs.

She took a deep breath, feigned composure, patted her chest, and tried to make her tone sound confident: "It's fine, I'll go and be right back. It's just a thank you, isn't it? I'll say a few nice words, coax him into a good mood, and the matter will be settled. Prince Jingnan isn't that big of a deal; what is there to be afraid of?"

But as soon as she finished speaking, she lowered her head, feeling guilty—she wasn't unafraid; she was scared to death.

Even so, Cui Mingyu still had Qinghe accompany her to Prince Jingnan’s mansion. But when they arrived at the gate, the gatekeeper stopped Qinghe from entering, saying with a straight face, "Our Prince has ordered that only Miss Cui may enter; no one else is allowed to trespass."

Qinghe’s eyes turned red with anxiety, and she grabbed Cui Mingyu’s hand tightly, refusing to let go: "Miss! You can't go in alone! Who knows what he's planning! I must go with you; if something happens, at least there will be someone to help!"

Cui Mingyu sighed helplessly, knowing that arguing with the gatekeeper was useless, so she whispered, "Don't worry, I'll be out soon. You go back first."

Qinghe was still uneasy, but seeing Cui Mingyu’s determined gaze, she could only nod reluctantly: "Then Miss, you must be careful. If anything happens, shout loudly. I'll be waiting for you at the gate!"

With that, Cui Mingyu took a deep breath and stepped alone through the vermilion gate of Prince Jingnan’s mansion.

The mansion was filled with carved beams and painted pillars, with winding corridors, exuding the grandeur of a noble family, yet it was terrifyingly quiet. Even the sound of the wind blowing through the leaves was clearly audible. Cui Mingyu walked along the corridor step by step, her heart pounding, feeling as if something bad was about to happen.

After turning several corners, the outline of the main hall gradually came into view. It was here that she had been forced to drink that lethal medicine. The humiliation and chill of the past surged into her heart instantly. Cui Mingyu couldn't help but shiver, her pace slowing down.

Just then, the sound of "thump, thump" footsteps came from the direction of the main hall, steady and powerful, each step seemingly landing on her heartstrings. Cui Mingyu felt her heart beating faster and faster; that taut string seemed ready to snap at any moment.

She bit the bullet and looked up, seeing Wei Songjun standing at the entrance of the main hall at a glance.

He was wearing a pale white brocade robe today, with faint, flowing cloud patterns embroidered on the hem. A jade belt of the same color was tied around his waist, making his posture as straight as a pine and his face as handsome as jade. Cui Mingyu had never seen him wear such light colors; he was usually dressed in black or dark-colored robes, exuding a cold, unapproachable air. But today, this white attire gave him a more gentle and refined quality, reminiscent of the saying, "The young master is like jade, peerless in the world."

She suddenly realized why the original owner was so obsessed with Wei Songjun—with such looks and such bearing, it was indeed easy for a woman to fall for him.

What a pity; the original owner's honey was her arsenic.

Cui Mingyu swallowed nervously, her voice trembling slightly: "G-Greetings, Your Highness."

Wei Songjun didn't speak, just looked at her with a slight frown, his deep eyes seemingly able to see through a person's heart. He walked step by step to the seat of honor and sat down, his posture lazy yet carrying an invisible sense of oppression. The air in the entire hall froze instantly, making it difficult to even breathe.

Cui Mingyu felt her chest tighten under the oppressive atmosphere, feeling as if her heart, liver, spleen, lungs, and kidneys were all shifting. She hurriedly raised the brocade box with both hands, trying to make her voice sound calmer: "Your Highness, this robe was newly made based on your old one. Do you... find it satisfactory?"

Wei Songjun didn't take the box, but his slender fingers tapped lightly on the armrest. The "tap, tap, tap" sound was exceptionally clear in the empty hall, each beat hitting Cui Mingyu’s heart, making her increasingly restless.

After a long while, he spoke slowly, his voice low and cold, revealing no emotion: "Made by Jinxiu Pavilion?"

Cui Mingyu’s heart skipped a beat. A sense of foreboding, accompanied by a bone-chilling cold, crawled up her spine. She feigned composure and nodded: "Yes... it was made by the masters at Jinxiu Pavilion. Their craftsmanship is among the best in the capital."

"Cost... one hundred taels?" Wei Songjun asked again.

She looked up abruptly, crashing into Wei Songjun’s bottomless eyes, with only one thought in her mind—it's over! This ancestor knows everything!

Cui Mingyu’s survival instinct kicked in instantly. Almost instinctively, she jumped up and turned to run toward the door—just kidding, with Wei Songjun’s temper, if she were a second too slow, she might lose her head! She didn't want to experience the ice-and-fire torture again, and she certainly didn't want to lose her life here!

"Cui Mingyu—"

Behind her came Wei Songjun’s cold voice, carrying an unquestionable threat, like a cold blade held to her throat: "Do you believe that whichever foot you step out of this door with first, I will chop off that foot!"

Cui Mingyu’s sprinting footsteps came to an abrupt halt. The foot that had already stepped over the threshold retracted quietly, and she didn't even dare to breathe loudly.

She believed him! The original owner had died a gruesome death at his hands!

Cui Mingyu turned around stiffly, forcing a smile that looked worse than crying: "Y-Your Highness is wise! Indeed... nothing can escape your sharp eyes! You are truly omniscient; I am in awe, truly in awe!"

chapters.title: Unequal Treaty
chapters.content:
Wei Songjun beckoned slightly, and a black shadow darted out from behind a pillar outside the door, moving as fast as a gust of wind. It was Qin Yi. Qin Yi placed a neatly folded moon-white robe on the table. The hidden patterns embroidered on the hem shimmered in the light; it was the very robe Cui Mingyu had pawned.
Wei Songjun stood up and walked to the table, his slender fingers brushing over the fabric of the robe. The touch was delicate and smooth, completely different from the shoddy imitation. He looked up at Cui Mingyu, who was standing opposite him, his gaze as cold as frost: "Cui Mingyu, who gave you the nerve to pawn my robe and then dare to send me a fake to fool me?"
This sentence was like a heavy hammer, smashing into Cui Mingyu’s heart and shattering her last shred of hope. Her legs went weak, and she fell to her knees with a loud "thud," tears streaming down her face as she sobbed: "Your Highness, I was wrong! I was possessed by a ghost, and it was only in a moment of confusion that I did something so stupid. Please, be the bigger person and spare my life; I will never dare to do it again!"
Wei Songjun frowned even deeper, finding the sobbing in his ears extremely noisy. He looked down at the disheveled girl crying on the floor, his tone full of impatience: "Cui Mingyu, you are a lady of a noble family; can't you have some backbone?"
Backbone? In the face of her life, what was that worth? Cui Mingyu cried even harder, wiping her tears while hurriedly saying: "Your Highness, I really know I was wrong! I will go back right now and bring you all the money left from pawning the robe. Please don't hold this against me!" If the money was gone, she could earn more, but if her life was gone, everything would be lost!
Wei Songjun raised an eyebrow, looking at her with a half-smile: "The rest? This fake robe cost one hundred taels, so you mean there are four hundred taels left?"
Cui Mingyu nodded like a garlic masher, tears still hanging on her face, but she replied hurriedly: "Yes, yes! Your Highness is wise!! There are indeed four hundred taels left."
"Oh?" Wei Songjun drew out his tone, a hint of playfulness flashing in his eyes, "You pawned my robe and got five hundred taels. Why do you think I should pay for this fake of yours?"
Cui Mingyu’s movements came to an abrupt halt, and the expression on her face froze instantly. What was going on? Was Wei Songjun actually asking her to pay back five hundred taels? That was too much of a loss! He had already taken back the robe, and now he wanted five hundred taels for nothing. The key was that he was a dignified Prince; he didn’t need this five hundred taels of silver at all! She cursed Wei Songjun a thousand times in her heart, but she could only calculate quickly. Money could be earned again if it was gone, but if her life was gone, it was truly over. Five hundred taels it is, she thought. At worst, she would pawn her gold and silver jewelry; that should be enough to scrape it together.
Thinking of this, Cui Mingyu hurriedly squeezed out a smile that looked worse than crying: "The Prince is right! It was my lack of consideration! Then... then please give me a few days of grace, and I will definitely send over the five hundred taels of silver, not a penny less!"
Wei Songjun looked at her forced smile, and a meaningful smirk curled the corner of his mouth: "The amount is settled, but the method of repayment must be decided by me."
The smile on Cui Mingyu's face instantly solidified. Her heart skipped a beat, and an ominous premonition welled up. She looked at Wei Songjun with a face full of confusion, not knowing what kind of medicine he was selling in his gourd.
Then she heard Wei Songjun ask slowly: "What is your monthly allowance in the manor?"
Cui Mingyu subconsciously held up five fingers, her voice a bit faint: "Replying to the Prince, five... five taels."
Wei Songjun chuckled twice, the laughter carrying a hint of mockery: "How about this? I heard that you are skilled at massage, especially in relieving headaches. It just so happens that my headaches have recurred recently. Every time they flare up, I will ask you to come over. Each time will cost five taels, which will be deducted from the five hundred taels."
"What?!" Cui Mingyu jumped up from the ground, her eyes wide as saucers, looking at Wei Songjun in disbelief. "Prince, this... this is too unfair! Five hundred taels divided by five taels is one hundred times! You want me to come here one hundred times?!"
This was simply an unequal treaty! Who pays off a debt like this? Why not just pay the money directly? Why did he have to torment her!
Wei Songjun, however, acted as if he hadn't heard her protest and continued: "Cui Mingyu, my headaches had already healed. As for why they recurred, I believe you know in your heart."
Cui Mingyu was almost laughed to anger. What did it have to do with her! The one who drugged him that day was the original owner, not her! If she hadn't transmigrated into the book and stopped the original owner's foolish act in time, Wei Songjun would have lost half his life long ago! She had clearly saved him, but now, it had become her fault? Truly, no good deed goes unpunished!
Seeing her head bowed and silent, Wei Songjun assumed she was acquiescing, so he spoke again: "My head hurts a bit right now; come over and massage it for me."
Cui Mingyu pouted, greeting all of Wei Songjun's ancestors in her heart. This left her absolutely no room for maneuver! It seemed Wei Songjun had known her little thoughts all along and had deliberately dug a pit waiting for her to jump in! She raised her head, gathered her courage, and tentatively asked: "If... if I say no?"
Wei Songjun raised his eyebrows in some surprise, not expecting this woman to dare to bargain with him at a time like this. He looked at her feigned toughness, and the smile at the corner of his mouth deepened: "You won't."
He was right; she wouldn't. She was a coward, and in front of someone like Wei Songjun who held her life in his hands, she couldn't be tough at all.
Cui Mingyu sighed in resignation, shuffled over behind Wei Songjun, reached out to place her hands on his scalp, and began to knead gently. As she massaged, she gritted her teeth in her heart: If I had known, I should have learned some acupuncture and just poked him with a couple of needles, letting him taste the feeling of a splitting headache too!
After massaging for a while, Cui Mingyu suddenly sniffed. Heavens, why did Wei Songjun's hair smell so good? A faint woody scent mixed with a hint of ethereal floral fragrance made one's mood inexplicably better. A grown man, and he was so particular, using such good incense?
Hearing the sniffing sound from behind, Wei Songjun thought she was crying from grievance. His movements paused slightly, and his tone softened involuntarily: "Are you... what's wrong?"
Cui Mingyu's brain short-circuited, and without thinking, she blurted out: "You... you smell so good!"
As soon as the words left her mouth, she immediately shut her lips, wishing she could find a crack in the ground to crawl into. It’s over, it’s over; how could she say such a thing! The classic scene of Hong Shixian talking to Aili instantly flashed uncontrollably in her mind, and that line "You are so seductive" looped infinitely in her brain.
Help! Was she possessed by something?!
Wei Songjun's body stiffened abruptly, and his chest felt stifled. He had actually thought she was crying from grievance just a moment ago, but she hadn't taken it to heart at all and was instead focusing on his scent? How could someone as shameless as her know what grievance was?
He took a deep breath, suppressed the strangeness in his heart, and his tone returned to its previous coldness: "Don't get distracted, keep massaging."
Cui Mingyu didn't dare to speak again and could only obediently focus on her hands. But honestly, Wei Songjun's hair quality was truly excellent—black, shiny, and smooth as silk to the touch. Moreover, her hands were naturally light and soft, and the pressure was just right. Wei Songjun closed his eyes comfortably, his tense nerves gradually relaxing, and even the feeling of the headache eased quite a bit.
After massaging for a while, Cui Mingyu's arms began to ache. She secretly raised her eyes to look at Wei Songjun, who was enjoying it with his eyes closed, and her heart became unbalanced again. Why was he sitting there comfortably while she had to work herself to the bone massaging him?
As she massaged, she calculated in her heart: one hundred times, how long would this take? Even if Wei Songjun had a headache once every three days, she would have to wait until after three hundred days to completely get rid of this creditor. Heavens, how long would this last?!
Also, she and Xia Yuning had already agreed to marry in a year if nothing unexpected happened. Surely she couldn't still be coming to massage Wei Songjun's head after she was married, right?

chapters.title: The Aggrieved Ancestor
chapters.content:
Cui Mingyu felt as if her hands were no longer her own; they were so sore they felt like they were filled with lead, numb and swollen, almost ready to snap in two. She gritted her teeth, mechanically kneading the top of Wei Songjun's head, cursing this Prince of Jingnan a thousand times in her heart.
"Stop."
Finally, after nearly half an hour of massaging, Wei Songjun's cold and slightly lazy voice finally sounded. Cui Mingyu felt as if she had been granted amnesty; she immediately withdrew her hands and quietly shook them, trying to alleviate the piercing soreness. She peeked at Wei Songjun and saw him leaning back in the large armchair with his eyes closed, his face calm, seemingly not dissatisfied.
The opportunity had arrived! Cui Mingyu’s heart stirred, and she tentatively asked: "Prince, that... can I discuss something with you?"
Wei Songjun slowly opened his eyes. Those deep eyes were like cold pools, looking straight at her. His thin lips parted, and he said only one word: "Speak."
Cui Mingyu's heart skipped a beat, but she bit the bullet and weighed her words: "Prince, look, one hundred times—isn't that a bit too many? How about we discuss it: could a portion be settled with money? Do you think that’s possible?" As she spoke, she watched his expression, terrified that some word might annoy this living King of Hell.
Wei Songjun raised an eyebrow, a faint trace of mockery curling his lips: "What? Are you afraid you won't live that long?"
Cui Mingyu was almost choked to death by him. What kind of talk was that! She was here swallowing her pride, enduring his cold violence and this inhuman massage task, wasn't it all to save her own life? She suppressed the anger in her heart, quickly lowered her eyelids to hide the indignation in her eyes, and made her voice even softer: "The Prince is joking. I was thinking, I'm not young anymore, and my father is urging me to get married. If in some time I really get married, it wouldn't be proper for me to come and massage your head every day, and it wouldn't sound good for your reputation if it got out. Besides, this massage technique isn't something only I can do; I could teach my craft to Miss Mu and let her help you. What do you think?"
She was calculating in her heart: Mu Wanzhou was the heroine of the book, Wei Songjun's official match. If she threw this hot potato to her, wouldn't she be free?
Wei Songjun leaned his head back against the chair, his posture relaxed, but his gaze became sharper: "Get married? Who are you marrying? Xia Yuning?"
Seeing him point out Xia Yuning, Cui Mingyu thought this was perfect. She could use this to express her heart and let him be completely reassured that she no longer had any improper thoughts about him. She raised her head, met his gaze frankly, and nodded gently: "If nothing unexpected happens, it will be him."
Wei Songjun was silent for a moment, as if thinking about something. After a while, he suddenly tilted his head and looked at Cui Mingyu with a hint of inquiry: "How did this get back to Mu Wanzhou?"
Cui Mingyu was stunned, then widened her eyes, wearing an expression that said, "Why are you pretending?" "Prince, aren't you fond of Miss Mu? Last time we went boating, weren't you two together? A talented man and a beautiful woman, what a perfect match! In the future, when you marry Miss Mu, naturally it should be her coming to massage your head."
"Which eye did you see me being fond of her with?" Wei Songjun's face sank instantly. He turned his head abruptly to glare at Cui Mingyu, his tone carrying a hint of imperceptible anger.
Cui Mingyu was startled by his sudden anger and quickly lowered her head, her voice becoming weaker: "It... it was just what I saw at the lake last time. Maybe... maybe I misunderstood; please don't take it to heart."
She ranted crazily in her heart: Why are you pretending! How could you two leads not end up together in the end? This man is not only cold-hearted but also stubborn! Simply unreasonable!
Wei Songjun snorted coldly, his gaze like a torch, staring straight at Cui Mingyu, saying word by word: "You had better watch your mouth and not say things you shouldn't. As for these one hundred times, not a single one can be missing. As for you... if you get married halfway through, that's your business; you solve it yourself!"
"You!" Cui Mingyu was so angry she almost jumped up, her chest heaving violently. She was about to burst into a torrent of abuse, pouring out all the grievances and anger in her heart. But as Wei Songjun’s sharp, knife-like gaze swept over, all her words were instantly stuck in her throat, as if gripped by an invisible hand. She could only swallow her anger, turn her face away, and mutter under her breath: "Solve it myself then, who's afraid of who!"
Wei Songjun seemed not to have heard her muttering, or perhaps he simply didn't care. He stood up, straightened his robes, and said faintly: "That's all for today. I will summon you again later. Qin Yi, see Miss Cui out."
As soon as the words fell, Qin Yi popped out from nowhere, bowed, and saluted: "Yes, Prince. Miss Cui, please this way."
This was the first woman to spend the night in the Prince's manor, and she was personally kept by the Prince himself; he dared not show the slightest negligence.
Cui Mingyu followed Qin Yi out of the Prince Jingnan’s mansion, feeling listless. The sun was already slanting westward, casting a golden glow over the entire street, yet it carried an indescribable sense of desolation. Her mood, much like the setting sun, had sunk to rock bottom.
"Miss!"
A crisp voice rang out. Qinghe was standing anxiously not far from the mansion gate. Seeing Cui Mingyu emerge, she immediately hurried over, looking her up and down with deep concern. "Miss, are you alright? Did Prince Jingnan do anything to you? Did he bully you?"
Hearing this from the side, Qin Yi couldn't help but cough twice, saying somewhat awkwardly, "Young lady, please watch your words. How could our Prince be the type to bully people? He treated Miss Cui with the utmost courtesy today."
Qinghe shot a glance at Qin Yi, and seeing his roguish demeanor, she felt a surge of irritation. She couldn't help but mutter under her breath, "Birds of a feather."
"Hey—" Qin Yi’s ears were sharp, and he caught it immediately. He widened his eyes. "What did you say?"
"Was she wrong?" Cui Mingyu suddenly straightened her back, hands on her hips like a cat provoked, and shouted at Qin Yi, "There isn't a single good person in your Prince Jingnan’s mansion! From top to bottom, you’re all rotten! When the upper beam is crooked, the lower ones are askew! You eat the imperial grain but do no proper work; all you know is how to bully the weak and hold positions without performing duties! A bunch of degenerates!"
These words were like a thunderclap, leaving Qin Yi dumbfounded. He pointed at Cui Mingyu, unable to utter a complete word for a long time: "You... you..."
Qinghe was also startled by her mistress's sudden outburst. She looked at Cui Mingyu in disbelief, her eyes wide. Her mistress’s courage had truly grown quite a bit today!
After finishing her rant, Cui Mingyu felt the stifled frustration she had been holding in for so long finally vanish, and her whole body felt relieved. She took a deep breath and looked at the still-stunned Qin Yi, her eyes carrying a hint of a threat. "Do not breathe a single word of what I just said to Prince Jingnan! Your Prince still relies on me to treat his head ailment. If you dare to leak even half a word, you will bear the consequences!"
With that, she stopped looking at Qin Yi’s shocked expression, grabbed the equally bewildered Qinghe, and walked away with her head held high, leaving Qin Yi standing there alone. It took him a long time to recover, and he rubbed his nose with a wry smile. This Miss Cui was truly a handful!
